ar.name: قطعة من حرير منسوج.
description:
قطعة من الحرير المنسوج المزين بتصميم رباعي الفصوص، ومحدد بكتابات وأشكال متعددة الفصوص تشغل الفراغات بينها، وتذكر لقب "الأشرف". ما يزال ضرورياً دراسة تطور المنسوجات المملوكية وتأريخها، فالمنسوجات الحريرية المملوكية وغيرها من المنسوجات نادرة، والكثير من المتبقي منها تم العثور عليه في القبور والتنقيبات في مصر العليا. تم استعمال الحرير الثمين في خياطة أثواب التشريفات، والهدايا الدبلوماسية، والقطع الفخمة المعدة للتصدير، وكان الحرير المقلم دارجاً ومرغوباً، وعادة ما كان يتم إدخال اسم السلطان وألقابه ضمن التصميم. اشتهرت مناطق صناعة الحرير في مصر كأسيوط، وهي مدينة في مصر العليا، المعروفة بكتانها وحريرها عاليي الجودة. وتعتبر قطع الحرير التي تحمل اسم لقب "الأشرف" من بين آخر القطع التي تم تأريخها من الفترة المملوكية، ويضم متحف فيكتوريا وألبرت العديد من القطع التي تحمل هذه المواصفات.  
يفترض الباحثون أن المنسوجات من هذا النوع قد تم إنتاجها خلال حكم السلطان قايتباي الذي حكم في الفترة 872-901/ 1468-96، والذي كانت ألقابه الرسمية تتضمن لقب "الأشرف". ومن المثير للاهتمام أن المنسوجات الزرقاء كان يرتديها أهل الذمة خلال الفترة المملوكية، ولذلك، وعلى سبيل المثال، فقد تم العثور على أسقف قبطي، مدفون في قصر إبراهيم في مصر العليا، ملفوفاً في عباءة من الصوف الأزرق الأسود.

قطع الحرير المملوكية نادرة، إلا أننا نعلم أنها كانت تُنتج لصنع أثواب الشرف، وهدايا الدبلوماسيين، وسلع فاخرة مُعدَّة للتصدير. أعداد كبيرة من هذه القطع، تحمل أسماء وألقاب السلاطين، وهذه القطعة يُفترض أنها منتَجة في عهد السلطان قايتباي (حكم فيما بين عامي 872 – 901هـ/1468 – 1496م).
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
keywords: الحرير، السلطان قايتباي.

en.name: Fragment of woven silk.
description:
A blue silk woven with a quatrefoil design, bordered by inscriptions, and a polyfoil occupying the spaces in between. The inscription, written in Arabic reads: ‘Honour to al-Ashraf’. The development and chronology of Mamluk textile design has yet to be clearly defined. Mamluk silks and other textiles are exceedingly rare, and many of those that have survived have been retrieved from excavations of burials in Upper Egypt. Precious silks were used in the production of honorary robes, diplomatic gifts and high-class articles produced especially for export. Striped silks were particularly popular, and frequently the names and titles of sultans were incorporated into the design. Areas of Production for textiles such as this one included Asyut, a town in Upper Egypt, well-known for its high-quality linens and silks. Silks inscribed with the benediction ‘Honour to al-Ashraf’ are amongst the latest datable fabrics of the Mamluk era, the V&A in London holding several fragments with this feature.  
It has been suggested that fabrics such as this one may have been produced during the reign of Sultan Qaytbay (AH 872–901 / AD 1468-96), whose official titles included ‘al-Ashraf’. Interestingly, blue textiles were often worn by *dhimmis* (the religious minorities)in the Mamluk period. Thus, a Coptic bishop buried at Qasr Ibrim in Upper Egypt, for example, was found wrapped in a blue-black woolen cloak.

Mamluk silks are rare, but we know that they were used in the production of honorary robes, diplomatic gifts and high-class articles produced for export. Many bear the names and titles of sultans and this piece is assumed to have been produced during the reign of Sultan Qaytbay (AH 872–901 / AD 1468–96).
place: From a tomb at al-Drounka, Egypt.
keywords: Silk; Sultan Qaytbay; textile

es.name: Fragmento de tejido de seda
description:
Fragmento de tejido de seda azul con cuatrifolios enmarcados por inscripciones y con flores polilobuladas en los espacios intermedios. La inscripción en árabe dice: “Honor a al-Ashraf”. Todavía no se conoce bien la cronología y el desarrollo de la producción textil del periodo mameluco, las pocas sedas y tejidos que se han conservado proceden en su mayoría de excavaciones en tumbas del Alto Egipto. Se utilizaban preciadas sedas para tejer vestiduras honoríficas, regalos diplomáticos y artículos de lujo que luego se exportaban. Eran muy populares las sedas con franjas, a las que era frecuente incoporrar los títulos y nombres de los sultanes. Asyut, en el Alto Egipto, era uno de los centros de producción más reconocidos por la calidad de sus linos y sedas. Las sedas con el bordado “Honor a al-Ashraf” corresponden a la última etapa textil datable de la era mameluca. En el museo Victoria & Albert se conservan varios fragmentos.  
Se cree que este tipo de tejidos se produjo en época del sultán Qaytbay (r. 872-901 / 1468-1496), ya que uno de sus títulos oficiales era “al-Ashraf”. Curiosamente, en el periodo mameluco eran principalmente los miembros de *dimmis* (minorías religiosas) quienes vestían telas azules; sin embargo, un obispo copto enterrado en Qasr Ibrim (Alto Egipto) fue hallado envuelto en un manto azul y negro.

Son raras las sedas del periodo mameluco, aunque se sabe que eran utilizadas en la confección de vestiduras honoríficas, regalos diplomáticos y artículos de lujo para la exportación. Se cree que este tejido se confeccionó en la época del sultán Qaytbay (r. 872-901 / 1468-1496) y, como muchos de estos tejidos, lleva bordados los nombres y títulos del sultán.
keywords: seda; Sultán Qaytbay

fr.name: Fragment de soie tissée.
description:
Tissage de soie bleue à motif de quatre-feuilles, bordé d'inscriptions séparées par des motifs multilobés. Le texte arabe dit : “Honneur à al-Achraf”. Le développement et la chronologie des motifs du textile mamelouk restent à définir avec précision. Les soies et autres tissus mamelouks sont extrêmement rares, et beaucoup de ceux qui sont parvenus jusqu'à nous ont été trouvés dans des fouilles de tombes en Haute-Égypte. Les soies précieuses étaient utilisées pour les robes officielles, les cadeaux diplomatiques et les articles de luxe spécialement produits pour l'exportation. Les soies à rayures étaient particulièrement appréciées, et souvent les noms et titulatures des sultans étaient tissés dans le motif. Celles portant l'inscription “Honneur à al-Achraf” sont parmi les dernières datables de la période mamelouke. Le Victoria and Albert Museum de Londres en possède plusieurs exemplaires. Assyout, ville de Haute-Égypte fameuse pour la haute qualité de son lin et de sa soie, est l'un des centres de production de textiles du type de celui-ci.  
On a pu suggérer que des tissus comme celui-ci avaient été produits sous le règne du sultan Qaytbay (872-901 H /1468-1496 J.-C.), dont les titres officiels comprenaient la mention “al-Achraf”. Il est intéressant de noter que les tissus bleus étaient souvent portés par les *dhimmi* (membres de minorités religieuses) pendant la période mamelouke. Ainsi, un évêque copte enterré à Qasr Ibrim en Haute-Égypte a été trouvé enseveli dans un manteau de laine bleu-noir.

Les soieries mameloukes sont rares, mais nous savons qu’elles étaient utilisées dans la fabrication de vêtements honorifiques, de cadeaux diplomatiques et d’articles sophistiqués produits pour l’exportation.  Beaucoup portent les noms et les titres des sultans et cette pièce est  supposée avoir été produite durant le règne du sultan Qaytbay (872-901 H / 1468-1496 J.-C.).
keywords: soie ; Qaytbay

en.name: Ferdinand I, Czar of Bulgaria (1861–1948)
short_description: Portrait of Ferdinand I (1861–1948) as Duke of Bulgaria. Ferdinand I was born as the son of the Austrian General August von Sachsen-Coburg and Gotha. In 1887 he became ruler of Bulgaria after the abdication of Alexander I von Battenberg. In 1908 he made himself Tsar of Bulgaria. Because he joined the German and Austrian monarchy in WWI and lost the war, he had to abdicate on 3 October 1918 and to emigrate to Germany and Slovakia. In 1948 Ferdinand I of Bulgaria died in Coburg, Germany.
keywords: Ferdinand I, Czar of Bulgaria; Sachsen-Coburg and Gotha

de.name: Kirche (Architektur, Innenraum)
description:
Wenn eine zerstörte Klosteranlage nach einem Krieg oder einem Feuer wieder aufgebaut wurde, begann man meist mit der Kirche. Oder mit den Kirchtürmen, wie es in Lambach geschah, wo man neue Türme auf einen dreigeschossigen romanischen Sockel setzte. Nach Modernisierung der Gebäude und der Mönchszellen errichtete man die Kirche, die als stilistisch reines barockes Gotteshaus überlebte.  
Wie die Fassade verfügt auch das Kirchenschiff an den Wänden über Doppelpilaster. Sie werden von einem mächtigen, durchgehenden Gebälk sowie von Fresken und Stuckdekoration im Gewölbe bekrönt. Der leuchtende Gelb/Ocker-Farbton des Gewölbes und der Wände ist original. Er war viele Jahrzehnte von einer weißen Schicht verdeckt und erhielt erst vor ein paar Jahren wieder den ursprünglichen Farbton. Das Kircheninnere ist kunstvoll ausgestattet: der der Himmelfahrt Mariens geweihte Hochaltar stammt vermutlich von Antonio Beduzzi, der sich damit auf das Hochaltarmodell Fischers von Erlach in der Basilika von Mariazell bezog. Hier und dort dominieren mächtige Säulen, über die sich in Lambach die Figurengruppe der Heiligen Dreieinigkeit spannt. Die großformatigen Gemälde für den Hochaltar und für die Seitenaltäre wurden von Joachim von Sandrart und Mitarbeitern ausgeführt.
dates: 1639 Kirchtürme, 1652-1656 Kirche, 1652-1661 Gemälde Hochaltar und Seitenaltäre, 1655 Gewölbestuck, 1662 schmiedeeisernes Abschlussgitter, 1698 Fresken beendet, 1716-1717 Hochaltar
artist: Vermutlich Filiberto Lucchese: Architektur; Joachim von Sandrart und Werkstätte: Altarbilder; wahrscheinlich Thomas Zaisel: Gewölbestuck; NN: schmiedeeisernes Gitter; Melchior Steidl: Großteil der Fresken; vermutlich Antonio Beduzzi: Hochaltar

en.name: Church (architecture and interior)
description:
When a destroyed monastery complex was rebuilt after a war or a fire, they usually started with the church. Or with the church towers, as was done in Lambach, where they put new towers on the three-storey Romanesque base. After a modernization of the cloister and the monks´ cells they built up the church, which has survived as a stylistically pure Baroque building.  
Corresponding with the façade’s double pilasters, there are double pilasters along the nave´s walls. They are crowned by a mighty continuous entablature as well as by fresco paintings and decorative stucco works in the vault. The bright yellow/ochre colour on walls and vault is original. It had been covered with a white layer for many decades and was only some years ago re-painted. The interior is magnificent: the high altar dedicated to the Ascension of the Holy Virgin was probably executed by Antonio Beduzzi, following Fischer´s von Erlach high altar model in the Mariazell basilica. Here and there dominate mighty columns; in Lambach everything is climaxing in the sculptural Holy Trinity scenery above. The huge paintings at the high altar and side altars were executed by Joachim von Sandrart and employees.
dates: 1639 church towers; 1652–56 church; 1652–61 paintings high altar and side altars; about 1655 stucco work vault; 1662 wrought iron grill; 1698 fresco paintings finished; 1716–17 high altar
place: In the middle of the South wing
artist: Possibly Filiberto Lucchese: architecture; Joachim von Sandrart and employees: altar paintings; probably Thomas Zaisel: stucco work vault, unknown: wrought iron grill; Melchior Steidl: most of the fresco paintings; presumably Antonio Beduzzi: high altar

en.name: Ostrich egg pendants
description: Since the early modern period, ostrich eggs have been suspended in rooms in the Christian and Islamic regions of the Mediterranean. Their purpose is to warn the faithful and to safeguard their souls against harm. In bazaars, they are hung on the fronts of street side shops, and in and above gateways. Ostrich eggs decorate the tombs of saints, churches and mosques. With the fashion for all things Oriental, they have found their way into upper class living rooms furnished "in Moorish style."
materials: Ostrich eggs, silk, wool, cotton, silver thread, pigment
tags: Ostrich eggs, silk, wool, cotton, silver thread, pigment

en.name: Disk
short_description: The disk in green glass with a golden square foil is considered of remarkable interest because of its label, attributed to Ippolito Rosellini, which proves that the relic was found inside a tomb in Thebes. Rosellini, one of the main figures of the Franco-Tuscan expedition in Egypt, wrote on it "Disco di vetro con entro una lamina d'oro. Trovato in una tomba a Tebe, Egitto, da I. Rosellini 1824 -dono di Elenina Ox Sicard, dicembre 1902". The relic was later acquired by Enrico Hillyer Giglioli. As a result of the excavations by W. Petrie and J. De Morgan, who documented the existence of an era preceding the 1st dynasty, Luigi Pigorini decided to expand the Egyptian archaeological collection in the "Museo Preistorico Etnografico e Kircheriano" which he directed at that time. In 1878 he began to acquire important groups, with the main body of the collection donated by David Randall-MacIver in 1901, after the excavations he carried out on the behalf of the Egypt Exploration Fund in the town of el-Amrah, Upper Egypt. Another major purchase — from the Italian Archaeological Mission in Egypt (excavations of Hammamiye) led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, director of the Egyptian Museum in Turin — followed in 1905. The last main acquisition took place in 1913 when the Egyptian objects from the Enrico Hillyer Giglioli’s collection entered the museum collection.
holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
dates: New Kingdom (16th–11th century BC); discovered in 1824
keywords: Egyptomania; Gaetano Rosellini; university; collector; photograph; anthropology; palaeoethnology; material culture; Florence; Pisa; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; hieroglyph; William Matthew Flinders Petrie; Jacques de Morgan; David Randall-MacIver
partner: MIBACT | National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

ar.name: الخيرالدا.
description:
إن الأثر الأكثر دلالة ضمن بقايا المباني الدينية كلها، التي تعود إلى الفترة الموحدية والمحافظ عليها في شبه الجزيرة، هو بدون شك المئذنة التي تعود إلى مسجد اشبيلية الكبير، المعروفة تحت اسم "الخيرالدا".  
انطلقت الأشغال الأولى لمسجد اشبيلية الكبير في ظل مُلك أبي يعقوب يوسف، الذي عاش في اشبيلية كعامل عليها، قبل أن يعتليَ العرش، ويُحوِّل المدينة إلى إقامة للخلفاء الموحدين في شبه الجزيرة. تطلبت مقاييس المسجد الجديد ورفعته تكملة مئذنة كبيرة كُلِّف بأشغال بنائها رئيس البنائين، أحمد بن باسو، الذي بدأ أساسات البرج في عام 580 / 1184. وقد أدت وفاة الملك في السنة نفسها إلى توقف الأشغال حتى وصول ابنه وخلفه، أبي يوسف يعقوب، في عام 584 / 1188 – 1189 ، إلى اشبيلية، والذي قام بإنهاء الأعمال تحت إدارة علي من غمارة. أُتممَت المنارةُ في 30 من ربيع الثاني عام 594 / 10 مارس (آذار) 1198 ، وهو التاريخ الذي حضر فيه الخليفة محاطاً بحاشيته والشعب الاشبيلي لوضع الجامور، المكون من ثلاث كرات مذهبة لتتويج البرج، والتي كان قد أوصي بها للاحتفاء بمعركة الأرك. وتتكون المنارة، التي تستند إلى الحائط الشرقي للمسجد والبارزة عن محيطه، من موشورين اثنين مربعي الشكل، مُدمجين أحدهما في الآخر، ويحملان نواة مركزية حيث تتراكب سبع غرف مغطاة بأقبية. وبين الموشورين، ينبسطُ درابزين يؤدي إلى الجزء العلوي؛ ويبلغ الارتفاع من الأرضية حتى السطح 50.85 متراً.  
تحتفظ المئذنة بكل الزخرفة الخارجية لواجهاتها الأربع تقريباً؛ والجزء السفلي أملس، وبالكاد متقطع بشقوق فتحات الضوء ذات العقود المفصصة والعقود المتجاوزة المؤطرة بالألفيزات. وفي وسط البرج، قُسِّمت زخرفة كل واجهة إلى ثلاث لوحات. مُلئت اللوحة المتواجدة في الوسط، كما هو الحال في الجزء العلوي، بفتحات من أجل الضوء – هنا نوافذ توأمية محفورة داخل قوس كبير مُصمت ومؤطر بألفيز؛ وغُطيت أطراف الجدران الجانبية بتشبيك من الآجر المنقوش والمقطَّع، فوق أرضية ملساء، مُوَّلدٍ بتمدد وتقاطع العقدين المصمتين المرتكزين على أعمدة. وقد زُوِّق الجزءُ العلوي للبرج بست عقود مصمتة في كل واجهة، تستند، هي الأخرى، على أعمدة من الرخام ذات أبدان وتيجان أموية. وعلى غرار معالم أخرى من الطراز نفسه، كُللت المئذنة بشرافات متدرجة لم يتبق منها إلا آثار فوق حاجز الجرس الحالي.  
وفي عام 1355 ميلادي، أدى زلزال إلى انهيار الجامور. وخلال الفترة المسيحية، وبالضبط في عام 1560، انطلقت أشغال الهيكل الجديد الذي يحمل فوقه دوارة ريح سميت شعبيا بال"خيرالدا"، وهي التي أعطت اسمها إلى البرج.

تبقى هذه المنارة التي تشرف على إشبيلية المعلمة الأكبر أهمية بالمدينة؛ وهي تأخذ اسمها "الخيرالدا" من التمثال الذي يدور على شكل دوارةِ ريح في جزئها الأعلى. احتُفظَ بالمنارة كلِّها باستثناء الجسم العلوي للقمة، والذي عُوِّض في القرن 10 الهجري / القرن 16 الميلادي بجرس مسيحي.  
بنيت الخيرالدا من الآجر، وبدرابزين للدخول يحتوي على مالايقل عن سبع غرف متراكبة. كما شيد الزخرفُ على شكل تشبيكات معينية من الآجر، وهو يسندُ أعمدة وتيجانا قرطبيةً، محصلٌ عليها من أطلال مدينة الزهراء، وأعيد استعمالها من قبل الموحدين.
artist: أبو يعقوب يوسف (حكم مابين  558 – 580 / 1163 – 1184)؛ أبو يوسف يعقوب (حكم مابين 580 – 596 / 1184 – 1199).
أحمد بن باسو وعلي من غمارة.
keywords: اشبيلية؛ جامور؛ خيرالدا؛ مئذنة / منارة؛ مسجد؛ منشأة دينية؛ موحدون.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: Giralda.
description:
The most important of the peninsula's surviving religious buildings from the Almohad era is undoubtedly the minaret of the old Great Mosque of Seville, known as 'La Giralda'.  
Work on the Seville mosque was started during the reign of Abu Ya'qub Yusuf, who had lived in Seville as a governor before acceding to the throne, and once he had become the caliph, he made the city the residence of the Almohad caliphs in the peninsula. The size and grandiosity of the new mosque demanded the addition of a great minaret, and the work was entrusted to the master builder Ahmad ibn Baso, who dug the foundations of the tower in AH 580 / AD 1184. The death of the sovereign that same year caused work to be suspended until his son and successor Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur arrived in Seville in AH 584 / AD 1188–9, ordering the work to be recommenced under the direction of Ali de Gomara. The minaret was finished on 30 Rabi al-Thaany AH 594 / 10 March AD 1198, on which date the Caliph, surrounded by his court and the people of Seville, attended the placement of the *yamur*, three golden balls on top of the tower that were commissioned to commemorate the battle of Alarcos.  
The minaret, attached to the eastern wall of the mosque and protruding from its outer perimeter, consists of two square-plan volumes, one inside the other, supported on a central base from which seven vaulted chambers rise. The ramp providing access to the upper part runs in between the two volumes. The height from floor to terrace is 50.85 m.  
Practically all of the exterior decoration on the four sides of the minaret has survived. The lower part is smooth, interrupted only by the lighting apertures, with horseshoe and lobed arches framed with *alfiz* panels. Around the middle of the tower, the decoration on each of the sides splits into three. The middle section, like the lower part, contains lighting apertures, in this case made up of twin windows beneath a large blind arch framed with an *alfiz* panel. The side sections are covered with a network of carved and cut bricks on a smooth base formed by the extension and crossing of two blind arches on columns. The upper part of the tower is decorated with another ten arches with blind fronts that, like the previous ones, rest on marble columns with Umayyad capitals and shafts. As with other monuments of this type, the minaret is topped with stepped battlements, some of which have survived on the parapet of the existing bell tower.  
In 1355, an earthquake destroyed the *yamur*, and in 1560, in Christian times, work was started on the new structure, which was finished with an enormous weather vane known popularly as 'giralda', hence the name of the tower.

The minaret of the great Almohad mosque that dominates Seville is the city’s most important monument. The name Giralda is derived from the weathervane-like statue that crowns the building. It has survived in full, with the exception of the very top which was replaced in the AH 10th / AD 16th century with a Christian bell tower.  
It is made of brick and has ramps connecting the seven superposed rooms. The decorative networks of rhombuses that spring from the Cordoban capitals and columns salvaged by the Almohads from the ruins of Madinat al-Zahra are also made of brick.
artist: Abu Ya’qub Yusuf (r. AH 558–80 / AD 1163–84); Abu Yusuf Ya’qub al-Mansur (r. AH 580–96 / AD 1184–99).
Master builders Ahmad ibn Baso and Ali de Gomara.
keywords: Giralda; Seville, Almohads; minaret; mosque; yamur; religious architecture
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

es.name: Giralda.
description:
Entre los restos de edificios religiosos de época almohade que quedan en la Península, el más significativo es, sin duda, el alminar perteneciente a la antigua mezquita Mayor de Sevilla, conocido como “La Giralda”.  
  
Las primeras obras de la mezquita de Sevilla se iniciaron durante el reinado de Abu Ya'qub Yusuf, quien antes de acceder al trono había vivido en Sevilla como gobernador y, ya califa, convirtió la ciudad en residencia peninsular de los califas almohades. Las dimensiones y grandiosidad de la nueva mezquita exigían el complemento de un gran alminar, cuyas obras se encargaron al jefe de alarifes Ahmad Ibn Baso, que abrió los cimientos de la torre en 580 H. /1184 d. C. La muerte del soberano, ese mismo año, hizo que las obras se interrumpiesen hasta la llegada a Sevilla, en 584 H. / 1188-89, de su hijo y sucesor, Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur, que ordenó reanudarlas bajo la dirección de Alí de Gómara. El alminar estaría concluido el 30 de Rabi al-Thaany de 594 H./ 10 de marzo de 1198, fecha en que el califa, rodeado de su corte y el pueblo sevillano, asistió a la colocación del *yamur*, tres manzanas doradas que coronaban la torre y habían sido encargadas para conmemorar la batalla de Alarcos. El alminar, adosado al muro oriental de la mezquita y sobresaliendo de su perímetro, está compuesto por dos prismas de planta cuadrada, uno dentro de otro, que cargan sobre un núcleo central en que se superponen siete cámaras cubiertas por bóvedas. Entre ambos prismas se desarrolla la rampa de acceso a la parte alta. La altura desde el pavimento hasta la terraza es de 50,85 m.  
  
El alminar conserva casi toda la decoración exterior de sus cuatro frentes. La parte inferior es lisa, sólo interrumpida por los huecos de luces, con arcos de herradura y lobulados, enmarcados por alfices. Hacia la mitad de la torre, la decoración de cada frente se divide en tres paños o calles. La central, igual que en la parte inferior, está ocupada por los huecos de luz, en este caso formados por ventanas gemelas, bajo un gran arco ciego encuadrado en un alfiz. Los paños laterales están cubiertos por una red de ladrillo tallado y recortado, sobre fondo liso, que se forma por la prolongación y el cruzamiento de dos arcos ciegos sobre columnas. La parte superior de la torre está decorada con otros diez arcos ciegos por frente, que se apoyan, como los anteriores, en columnas de mármol, con fustes y capiteles omeyas. Como otros monumentos de este tipo, el alminar se remata con almenas escalonadas, de las que sólo quedan restos en el antepecho del actual campanario.  
  
En 1355, un terremoto derribó el *yamur*; en 1560, ya en época cristiana, comenzaron las obras del nuevo cuerpo, rematado por una enorme veleta llamada popularmente “giralda” que dio nombre a la torre.

Este alminar de la gran mezquita almohade que domina la ciudad de Sevilla es su monumento más importante. Conocido como la Giralda, el nombre deriva de la estatua que, a modo de veleta, gira en su parte más elevada. Se ha conservado íntegramente, excepto el cuerpo superior de remate, sustituido en el siglo X H. / XVI d.C. por un campanario cristiano.  
Se construyó en ladrillo, con rampas de subida a las siete estancias superpuestas. Del mismo material es la decoración de redes de rombos que arrancan de columnas y capiteles cordobeses procedentes de las ruinas de Madinat al-Zahra y reutilizados por los almohades.
artist: Abu Yaqub Yusuf (r. 558-580 H. / 1163-1184 d. C.); Abu Yusuf Ya’qub al-Mansur (r. 580-596 H. / 1184-1199 d. C.).
Maestros de obras Ahmad Ibn Baso y Alí de Gómara.
keywords: Giralda; Sevilla, almohades; alminar; mezquita; yamur; arquitectura religiosa
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

fr.name: Giralda.
description:
De tous les vestiges d'édifices religieux de l'époque almohade conservés dans la Péninsule, le plus significatif est sans aucun doute le minaret appartenant à la Grande Mosquée de Séville, connu sous le nom de “Giralda”.  
Les premiers travaux de la Grande Mosquée de Séville furent commencés sous le règne d'Abou Yacoub Youssouf qui, avant d'accéder au trône et de transformer la ville en résidence péninsulaire des califes almohades, avait vécu à Séville en qualité de gouverneur. Les dimensions et l'éminence de la nouvelle mosquée exigeaient le complément d'un grand minaret, dont les travaux furent commandés au chef des maçons Ahmad ibn Basso, qui commença les fondations de la touren 580 H / 1184 J.-C. La mort du souverain, la même année, causa l'interruption des travaux jusqu'à l'arrivée à Séville, en 584 H / 1188-89 J.-C., de son fils et successeur, Abou Youssouf Yacoub al-Mansour, qui les fit reprendre sous la direction d'Ali de Gomara. Le minaret devait être achevé le 30 *rabi al-Thaani* 594 H / 10 mars 1198 J.-C, date à laquelle le calife, entouré de sa cour et du peuple sévillan, assista à la mise en place du *jamour*, trois boules dorées qui couronnaient la tour et qui avaient été commandées pour commémorer la bataille d'Alarcos. Le minaret, adossé au mur oriental de la mosquée et en saillie sur son périmètre, est composé par deux prismes de plan carré, emboîtés l'un dans l'autre, qui portent sur un noyau central où se superposent sept pièces couvertes de voûtes. La rampe d'accès à la partie supérieure se déploie entre les deux prismes. Du sol jusqu'à la terrasse, la hauteur est de 50,85 m.  
Le minaret conserve presque toute la décoration extérieure de ses quatre faces. La partie inférieure est lisse, à peine interrompue par les fentes des ouvertures de lumière à arcs lobés et arcs outrepassés, encadrés par des *alfiz*. Vers le milieu de la tour, la décoration de chaque face est divisée en trois panneaux. Celui du centre, comme dans la partie inférieure, est occupé par les baies pour la lumière – ici, des fenêtres géminées inscrites dans un grand arc aveugle encadré par un *alfiz*. Les pans de murs latéraux sont recouverts par un réseau de briques sculptées et recoupées, sur un fond lisse généré par le prolongement et le croisement de deux arcs aveugles sur colonnes. La partie supérieure de la tour est décorée de dix autres arcs aveugles par face, qui s'appuient eux aussi sur des colonnes en marbre à fûts et chapiteaux omeyyades. Comme d'autres monuments de ce type, le minaret est couronné par des créneaux échelonnés dont il ne reste des vestiges que sur le parapet de l'actuel clocher.  
En 1355, un tremblement de terre fit s'écrouler le *jamour* et c'est en 1560, déjà à l'époque chrétienne, que furent commencés les travaux du nouveau corps, surmonté d'une énorme girouette appelée populairement '“Giralda”, qui donna son nom à la tour.

Ce minaret de la Grande Mosquée almohade qui domine Séville est le monument le plus important de la ville, et tire son nom de “Giralda” de la statue qui, à la manière d'une girouette, tourne sur sa partie la plus élevée. Le minaret est entièrement conservé, excepté le corps supérieur de la couronne, remplacé au Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.) par un clocher chrétien.  
La Giralda a été construite en brique, avec une rampe d'accès comptant pas moins de sept pièces superposées.  
Également en brique, le décor en réseau de losanges qui s'élève des colonnes et des chapiteaux cordouans provenant des ruines de Madinat al-Zahira et réutilisés par les Almohades.
artist: Abou Yacoub Youssouf (r. 558-580 H / 1163-1184 J-.C.) ; Abou Youssouf Yacoub al-Mansour (r. 580-596 H / 1184-1199 J.-C.).
Ahmad ibn Basso et Ali de Gomara.
keywords: Giralda ; Séville ; Almohades ; minaret ; mosquée ; jamour ; architecture religieuse
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: Constantinople. Inauguration de la ligne d´Eregli en 1905 et Turkhan Pacha (Inauguration of the Eregli Line in 1905 with Turhan Pasha)
description: The postcard depicts the inauguration of the Konya–Ereğli railway section, with Turhan Pasha among the Ottoman officials assembled for the ceremony. Although the postcard is dated 1905, archival records establish that the official opening took place at Ereğli Station on 25 October 1904. The Konya–Ereğli section constituted the first completed part of the Baghdad Railway project, and its inauguration was deliberately scheduled for the birthday of Sultan Abdülhamid II. Turhan Pasha, who was then Minister of Imperial Foundations (Evkaf-ı Hümayun Nazırı), headed the official delegation sent from Istanbul.
keywords: Baghdad Railway; Ereğli; Konya–Ereğli railway; railway inauguration; Turhan Pasha; railway ceremony

en.name: Knotted carpet (fragment)
description:
The oldest preserved knotted carpet fragments date back to the Islamic era and were produced in Egypt between the 8th and 10th centuries. However, only a few carpets produced before the 16th century have stood the test of time. Most of the preserved historical pieces found today stem from subsequent periods. These carpets are divided into two categories: those produced in urban or court weaving mills, and those hand-crafted in countryside homes. The former is closely linked to stylistic developments of contemporaneous art. To create their elaborate symmetrical patterns a template – provided by contemporary painters – was often used. The manner in which rugs were produced in the countryside differed: the pattern designs were long-lived and traditionally passed down from one generation to the next.  
The pattern template for this carpet has also been preserved. Arabesque and palmette tendrils, as well as cloud bands, cover the red middle field in horizontal and vertical mirroring patterns. They are framed with a broad dark-green border of spiral tendrils, palmettes, and birds. This type of design emerged in Herat and Kashan, beginning around the late 16th century, and later also Isfahan.
holder: GRASSI Museum of Applied Art, Leipzig
keywords: blue; Chinese influence; cloud pattern; collection; crafts; craftmanship; dark-blue; decorative arts; floral decoration; floral motifs; fragment; Iranian influence; lotus; palmette; Persia; vegetal decoration; vegetal motifs; wool; Herat

en.name: Dish
description: In the 19th century, new forms and decorative styles began to appear on dishes from Fez, which are remarkable both for the colours used and their design. This dish, decorated with two sailing boats, resembles designs seen on ceramics from Izmir in Turkey.
keywords: Applied arts; craftsmanship; Moroccan craftsmanship; ceramic; Iznik; Ottoman influence; Ottoman art
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate for Cultural Heritage

en.name: Cattedrale di San Pietro
description:
The façade has red bricks which emphasize the decorations in white Istrian stone. It is divided into two levels employing two gigantic Corinthian columns. The front of the building is crowned by a triangular pediment with three entrances. There is a large central window, flanked by the statues of Saints Peter and Paul on both sides.  
The bell tower, positioned on the southern side, was completed in the fifteenth century and incorporates the cylindrical tower of a former basilica, dating back to the end of the tenth century.  
The plan for the church follows the Jesuit outline: a hallway lined with chapels that open out onto the nave. Also lining the nave is a series of arches that alternate with wide pillars culminating in an eighteenth century choir in the middle. A barrel vault, flanked by buttresses, is supported by a rich entablature. The wide upper windows create a luminous atmosphere within the church.  
The richly decorated 16th century presbiterium is constructed on a Greek cross plan with three apses and a rectangular space proceeds the choir. It is covered by a groin vault supported by four large Corinthian columns. On the ceiling of the groin vault, above the main altar, is a fresco depicting *La Dimora Celeste* (“Paradise”) painted by Prospero Fontana in 1579. In the lunette above the altar is the *Annunciation* (1618) by Ludovico Carracci. The semi-dome above the apse has a painting of *Christ Handing the keys to Peter* by Cesare Aretusi and Giovanni Battista Fiorini (1579). The Bolognese artists Donato Creti, Marcantonio Franceschini, Vittorio Bigari, Antonio Rossi, Giuseppe Marchesi known as Sansone and Ercole Graziani painted the eighteenth century altarpieces.

St. Peter's cathedral, whose original nucleus dates back to the 11th century, was remodeled and rebuilt between the second half of the 16th century and the 18th century. The imposing interior, nearly as high as that of St. Peter's in Rome is richly decorated with stuccoes, marbles, gold, frescoes and other works of art. The church holds pictures by Prospero Fontana, Ludovico Carracci, Marcantonio Franceschini and Donato Creti, and a terracotta group of depicting the Mourning over the dead Christ by Alfonso Lombardi.
artist: Archbishop Gabriele Paleotti; Archbishop Alfonso Paleotti; Cardinal Prospero Lambertini later Pope Benedict XIV
Domenico Tibaldi; Pietro Fiorini; Floriano Ambrosini; Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta; Alfonso Torreggiani; Francesco Tadolini
history:
The original Romanesque cathedral was most likely dated from the beginning of the eleventh century. It was destroyed by a fire in 1014 and rebuilt in the second half of the twelveth century. Work continued until the fifteenth century. In the second half of the sixteenth century the Archbishop Gabriele Paleotti began a new ambitious program of works beginning with the apse. In 1575, the architect Domenico Tibaldi built a new presbiterium. This was decorated a few years later by several painters: Cesare Aretusi, Giovan Battista Fiorini, Bartolomeo Cesi, Camillo Procaccini and Prospero Fontana.  
Later, Archbishop Alfonso Paleotti commissioned architect Pietro Fiorini to create a simplification of the original plan by Tibaldi by eliminating the number of columns and pilasters in the naves. Unfortunately, the structuring may have been faulty as the vaults of the church collapsed in 1599. In 1605, work started again following the plan of Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta, under the supervision of Floriano Ambrosini. In 1612, the work continued by master builder Nicolò Donati, who partly modified Magenta's ideas.  
Work stopped for ten years, from 1613 until 1731. In 1734, Cardinal Prospero Lambertini, later Pope Benedict XIV, asked the architect Alfonso Torreggiani to complete the church and to build its façade: the façade was finally finished in 1776 by the architect Francesco Tadolini.
keywords: religious architecture; cathedral
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Cattedrale Metropolitana di San Pietro
description:
La facciata della Cattedrale di San Pietro, con cortine di mattoni rossi su cui risaltano le modanature e i partiti architettonici in pietra bianca d'Istria, è organizzato con due ordini architettonici giganti sovrapposti. Il prospetto, concluso da un frontone triangolare, ha tre portali di ingresso e una grande finestra centrale, affiancata dalle statue dei Santi Pietro e Paolo.  
Il campanile, posto sul lato sud, fu completato nel XV secolo incorporando la torre cilindrica della primitiva basilica risalente alla fine del secolo X.  
L'impianto planimetrico della chiesa segue lo schema gesuitico ad aula unica con cappelle laterali comunicanti, che si aprono sulla navata tramite arcate, alternate ad ampi pilastri con al centro coretti settecenteschi. Su una ricca trabeazione si imposta la volta a botte di copertura, rafforzata da archi di sostegno, e in alto si aprono grandi finestre che rendono l'interno particolarmente luminoso.  
Il presbiterio cinquecentesco, a croce greca con tre absidi e anti-coro rettangolare, è coperto da un'alta volta a crociera costolonata, sostenuta da quattro colonne giganti di ordine corinzio, ed è riccamente decorato. Sulla volta a crociera, sopra l'altare maggiore, è dipinta *La Dimora Celeste* (1579), opera di Prospero Fontana; nella lunetta sopra l'altare, *l'Annunciazione* (1618) di Ludovico Carracci; nel catino absidale *La consegna delle chiavi a San Pietro* (1579) di Cesare Aretusi e Giovan Battista Fiorini.  
L'apparato decorativo della fase settecentesca, tutto di scuola bolognese, è invece affidato a Donato Creti, Marcantonio Franceschini, Vittorio Bigari, Antonio Rossi ed Ercole Graziani.

La Cattedrale di San Pietro, il cui nucleo originale risale all'XI secolo, ha assunto l'aspetto attuale tra la seconda metà del XVI e il XVIII secolo. Il maestoso interno, che sfiora in altezza le dimensioni della Basilica di San Pietro a Roma, è ricco di stucchi ornamentali, materiali pregiati, affreschi e opere d'arte. La chiesa è arricchita dai dipinti di Prospero Fontana, Ludovico Carracci, Marcantonio Franceschini e Donato Creti, e dal gruppo scultoreo in terracotta del Compianto sul Cristo morto, di Alfonso Lombardi.
artist: Arcivescovo Gabriele Paleotti; Arcivescovo Alfonso Paleotti; Cardinale Prospero Lambertini.
Domenico Tibaldi; Pietro Fiorini; Floriano Ambrosini; Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta; Alfonso Torreggiani; Francesco Tadolini
history:
La primitiva cattedrale romanica, risalente presumibilmente agli inizi dell'XI secolo, fu distrutta da un incendio nel 1141 e ricostruita nella seconda metà del XII secolo, continuando ad essere oggetto di nuovi interventi fino al secolo XV. Nella seconda metà del Cinquecento, l'arcivescovo Gabriele Paleotti iniziò un ambizioso programma di restauri che prese avvio dalla zona absidale. Dal 1575 l'architetto Domenico Tibaldi realizzò il nuovo presbiterio che venne decorato, pochi anni dopo, dai pittori Cesare Aretusi, Giovan Battista Fiorini, Bartolomeo Cesi, Camillo Procaccini e Prospero Fontana.  
In seguito, l'arcivescovo Alfonso Paleotti incaricò l'architetto Pietro Fiorini di ridimensionare il progetto di Tibaldi diminuendo il numero di sostegni delle navate, fatto che provocò, nel 1599, il crollo delle volte. Nel 1605 i lavori ripresero secondo il progetto di Giovanni Ambrogio Magenta, sotto la direzione di Floriano Ambrosini, al quale nel 1612 subentrò il capomastro Nicolò Donati, che modificò in parte il progetto del Magenta.  
La costruzione fu sospesa l'anno successivo e nuovamente ripresa nel 1731. Nel 1734 il cardinale Prospero Lambertini, futuro papa Benedetto XIV, incaricò l'architetto Alfonso Torreggiani di completare la chiesa ed eseguirne la facciata, che fu infine conclusa nel 1776 dall'architetto Francesco Tadolini.
keywords: Architettura religiosa; cattedrale

en.name: A Druse Bride from Lebanon
short_description: The bride wears a tantur, a head ornament worn along with a white veil by the women from Antilibano. The photo belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist on his world travels in 1865 to 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum and are important for the histories of anthropological science and photography. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the 1875 foundation of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.
holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”
keywords: Woman; photograph; anthropology; ethnology; geography; travel; exploration; scientific expedition; ethnography; museums; model; genre picture; portrait; representation of the other; costume; material culture; collection; Lebanon; Druze
partner: MIBACT | National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

ar.name: مشربية.
description:
لوحة خشبية مؤلفة من إطار يحيط بخشب مشغول، تسمى مشربية، بنيتها مؤلفة من ثلاث مناطق تتشكل من إطارات محفورة بمقاسات مختلفة، ويتم ملء كل منطقة بتصميم هندسي مشغول. تم ربط القضبان الأفقية والشاقولية في الجزء الخارجي مع قضبان قطرية مرتبة جميعها بالاتجاه نفسه في كل صف مما يعطي الإيحاء بأشكال أغصان وأوراق. وعلى العكس منها، تنطلق القضبان القطرية في المنطقة الثانية بشكل شعاعي من مركز بيضوي مشكلة نماذج زهرية مجردة. تم ملء الفتحة المتفصلة في أعلى المنطقة الثانية بمشغولات خشبية مؤلفة من روابط مستديرة لكل منها أربع قضبان مائلة تنبثق بشكل شعاعي.  
تم تجميع الإطار الخارجي للمشربية بطريقة مختلفة عن إطار الفتحة، ومن المحتمل أنه ليس أصلياً، فالأفاريز ليست من العرض نفسه، كما أنها ليست مشغولة بالطريقة نفسها التي شغل بها الإطاران الداخليان.  
استخدمت المشربيات كنوافذ تطل على الفسحة السماوية الداخلية للبيت،كما استعملت لتطل على الشارع.
لوح خشبي مؤلف من قضبان متشابكة يعرف باسم المشربية. وهذه المشربية المشبكة تتشكل من قضبان عامودية وأفقية متعامدة مرتبة وفق أشكال هندسية معينة، وهي تقوم مقام النوافذ المطلة على فناء البيت أو الشارع.
holder: المتحف الوطني للفنون الجميلة، استوكهولم الذي أعار القسم الرئيس من المجموعة الإسلامية إلى متحف آثار المتوسط والشرق الأدنى بشكل دائم منذ عام 1982 بهدف إعادة تنظيم مجموعاته المتزايدة.
dates: القرن العاشر- الثالث العشر/ السادس عشر- التاسع عشر.
keywords: خشبيات؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ ستارة خشبية؛ عمارة؛ مشربية؛ مشغولات خشبية.
partner: متحف آثار البحر الأبيض المتوسط والشرق الأدنى

en.name: Window screen.
description:
A wooden panel consisting of a framed latticework is called a *mashrabiyya*. The area of this *mashrabiyya* is structured in three zones formed by carved frames of different sizes. Each zone is filled with a geometric design of woodwork. The vertical and horizontal bars of the outer area are combined with diagonals arranged in the same direction in each row giving the impression of a stem and leaf pattern. In contrast, the diagonal bars of the second zone lead away radially from an oval centre forming a pattern of abstract flowers. The hinged aperture situated in the upper part of the second zone is filled with a latticework consisting of round junctions, each with four diagonal bars leading away radially.  
The outer frame of the panel, assembled in a different way from the frame of the aperture, might be not original. The ledges are of various widths and are not carved like the two inner ones.  
Wooden latticework panels are intended to serve as windows onto the inner courtyard of a house or onto the street.

Wooden panel consisting of a framed latticework, called *mashrabiyya*. The latticework is formed by vertical, horizontal and diagonal bars arranged in geometrical patterns. *Mashrabiyyas* serve as windows onto the courtyard of the house or onto the street.
holder: Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities (Medelhavsmuseet).

National Museum of Fine Arts, Stockholm. In order to reorganise the expanding collections, the main part of the Islamic collection has been on permanent loan to the Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities since 1982.
keywords: Mashrabiyya; architecture; woodwork; latticework; geometric design
partner: Museum for Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities

es.name: Mampara para una ventana.
description: Este tipo de paneles de madera, trabajada en forma de celosía con un marco, se denominan mashrabiyya. Marcos tallados dividen la superficie de esta mashrabiyya  en tres partes desiguales, decoradas con un diseño geométrico de madera tallada. Las barras verticales y horizontales del primer espacio desde el exterior, se combinan con motivos diagonales tallados en la misma dirección en todas las filas, creando la ilusión de un diseño de tallos y hojas. Las barras diagonales de la superficie central salen de un centro oval, representando un diseño de flores abstractas. En esta parte de la mampara se abre un vano con bisagras cuya superficie está decorada con una celosía de piezas circulares unidas por barras diagonales. La forma en la que el marco del vano central está armado es diferente a la del marco exterior, por lo que este podría haberse añadido posteriormente. Los antepechos son de varios tamaños y no están tallados como los interiores. Las celosías de madera servían para las ventanas que daban a los patios interiores y a la calle.

Panel de madera compuesto por una celosía enmarcada, denominada  
*mashrabiyya*. La celosía es un diseño geométrico de barras verticales, horizontales y diagonales. Las *mashrabiyyas* cubrían las ventanas que daban a la calle y al patio.
holder: Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Próximo Oriente (Medelhavsmuseet).

Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Estocolmo. En 1982, el grueso de la colección islámica se prestó de forma permanente al Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Próximo Oriente (Medelhavsmuseet) en un intento de reorganizar una colección en constante crecimiento.
dates: Siglos X-XIII de la Hégira/ XVI-XIX d.C.
keywords: mamparas de ventanas; mashrabiyya; arquitectura; carpintería; celosía; diseño geométrico
partner: Museo de Antigüedades del Mediterráneo y Oriente Próximo

fr.name: Écran de fenêtre.
description:
Ce panneau composé d'un treillis de pièces de bois est un moucharabieh. Il est structuré en trois zones réparties dans des encadrements de différentes dimensions. Chaque zone est occupée par un treillis de composition géométrique. Les barreaux verticaux et horizontaux de la zone externe se combinent avec des diagonales orientées dans la même direction sur chaque rangée pour créer une image de tige et de feuilles. Par contraste, les barreaux diagonaux de la seconde zone partent en rayon d'un centre ovale pour former un motif de fleur stylisée. L'ouverture articulée sur charnières en partie supérieure de la seconde zone est également ornée d'un treillis de pièces circulaires d'où partent des barreaux en rayons diagonaux.  
Le cadre extérieur de l'écran est assemblé de façon différente de celle du cadre de l'ouverture et n'est peut-être pas d'origine. Les montants sont de largeurs variées et ne sont pas sculptés comme les deux de la partie intérieure.  
Ces panneaux de bois protégeaient des ouvertures donnant sur la cour intérieure d'une maison ou sur la rue.

Panneau de bois consistant en un treillis encadré ou moucharabieh. Le treillis est composé de barreaux verticaux, horizontaux et diagonaux disposés en motifs géométriques. Les moucharabiehs protégeaient les fenêtres donnant sur la cour de la maison ou sur la rue.
holder: Musée des antiquités méditerranéennes et proche-orientales (Medelhavsmuseet)

Musée national des Beaux-Arts, Stockholm. Dans le cadre de la réorganisation de ses collections en expansion, la plus grande partie des pièces d’art islamique ont fait l’objet d’un prêt permanent au Musée des antiquités méditerranéennes et proche-orientales en 1982.
dates: Xe-XIIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XVIe-XIXe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Écran de fenêtre; moucharabieh; architecture; travail du bois; treillis; composition géométrique
partner: Musée des antiquités méditerranéennes et proche-orientales (Medelhavsmuseet)

en.name: Rimanóczy Mansion
description:
The mansion has two levels, the central bay of which is complete with a mansard. The central bay is only slightly abutting in the middle on the main (courtyard) façade, but the side pavilions on the garden facade explicitly jut out, thus making the base of the building slightly U-shaped. The mansard roof is covered with wooden shingle. The levels are separated with dividing cornices. The windows are rectangular except for the first-floor windows of the central risalit; the middle windows of the side pavilions on the main and garden façades are crowned by linear hood mouldings (curved). The space between the upper-level windows and their hood moulds is decorated with plaster-panel adornments.  
The building is entranced on the ground floor – in the central bay of the courtyard façade – through a basket-arched, stone-framed gate decorated with the coat of arms of the Esterházy family (which had owned the mansion since the 19th century). Next to the gate there is a large terrace upheld on columns with a balustrade, decorated with *putti* and vases. From the terrace, through French windows, the banqueting hall is accessible.  
Three high, half-circle arched windows break up the façade of the central bay divided up by pilasters with composite-headed capitals that reach up to the mansard over the gate. Above them are panels (two blind windows on the sides and a high relief *Madonna and Child* in the middle.  
The central bay, like the main façade, is divided up by composite-headed pilasters. Three openings divide the upper floor with wall panels above them (within the middle panel is the Rimanóczy coat of arms held by lions, and three rectangular fanlights to the mansard). The year of construction is inscribed in Roman numerals on the wall panel above the windows, and above this there is a segmented pediment that has another window mid-field, decorated with a vase adorned with a Sun motif and held by *putti* either side.  
A *sala terrena* is located on the ground floor of the central bay. A staircase decorated with stuccoes with a wrought-iron banister leads to the upper floor, where some rooms have stucco decorations, and a ceiling fresco can be found in the corner room of the northwest wing (*Pallas Athene/Minerva as Patron of the Arts and Sciences*).  
Most spectacular, however, is the banqueting hall with its ceiling fresco of the *Triumph of Apollo* and a representation of the *Four Continents* by an unknown artist. A series of oil-on-canvas portraits over the wooden panelling at door height on the side walls, praise the Habsburg dynasty and the Esterházy family: *Queen Maria Theresia*, *Roman Emperor Francis I*, *Emperor Joseph II*, *Marie Antoinette* and P*rince Nikolaus Esterházy*. According to some scholars, these are by Franz Anton Palko. The Pejacsevich family later had the portraits repainted to represent their own family members, but these were restored in the 1980s with their original iconography.  
The manor buildings further away from the main building have been extensively reconstructed.

The Baroque Rimanóczy Mansion was commissioned for Antal Rimanóczy between 1739 and 1758. The ceiling of the banqueting hall is decorated with an exquisite fresco, *Apollo Riding His Chariot Across the Sky*.
artist: Architect: unknown master (a pupil of Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt or Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach?); Painter: Franz Anton Palko? (1717–1766)
history:
(Zsira-) Gyüleviz became the property of the Rimanóczy family – who built the mansion – in the middle of the 17th century when a local landowner's daughter, Katalin Rátky, married István Rimanóczy. They had no children, therefore the estate and the small mansion standing on it was inherited by the Rimanóczy's children from his second marriage with Krisztina Chernel: by Boldizsár, and after his death in 1730, by Antal.  
The Rimanóczy family achieved nobility in 1646, and received the *prenom* “Rimanóczy” from Charles VI Emperor in 1734. The mansion was commissioned by Antal Rimanóczy, a councillor of the Hungarian Court Chancellery. Building probably began in 1739 as indicated below the pediment on the garden façade.  
The identity of the architect is still a matter for debate. Endre Csatkai (1939) searched for the architect among the pupils of Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt or Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach.  
The grandiose construction was beyond Rimanóczy's financial capability and the mansion was maintained only by mortgaging his estates. After his death in 1758, his heirs inherited so much debt they had to rent out a part of the estate in 1760 and mortgage the rest; in 1771 they even had to sell a part of it to Count János Draskovich. Count Antal Jankovich bought the mansion from the Draskovich family in 1776. It was then inherited by the Pejacsevich family, on the distaff side, through the marriage of Katalin Jankovich and Count János Pejacsevich in 1800. In 1806, Katalin Jankovich commissioned József Hild to prepare designs for reconstruction of the mansion, but work never began. The mansion was then sold by the Pejacsevich family to József János Ruston in 1890, and exchanged owners and lessees frequently until, finally, Princess Margit Esterházy bought it in 1922. She had it renovated along the lines of plans submitted by István Möller between 1923 and 1925, and also had the garden redesigned. In 1929, the princess married János Almásy. László Almásy, János's brother, was a good friend and hunting companion of the princess's brother Antal Esterházy. László Almásy was the real “English patient”: a famous Africanist, cartographer, hunter and pilot, and a frequent guest of the Esterházy family.  
In 1934, the Esterházy family sold the mansion to the Congregation of the Daughters of the Holiest Saviour (*Legszentebb Üdvözítő Leányai Kongregáció*) who instigated social institutions in the building beside their provincial centre. They transformed the ground floor *sala terrena* into a chapel. After the Dissolution of the Monasteries in 1950, the estate was nationalised. The Council of the capital took over management of it in 1951, first hosting a social centre and then a home for the mentally ill from 1975. The building was renovated between 1984 and 1987, and has been managed by The National Trust of Monuments for Hungary since 2008. The garden is a nature reserve.

partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

cs.name: Sněmovní sál, Sláva Moravy
description: Na obelisku, symbolu věčnosti je zobrazen erb země Moravské. Vrchol hlavní části nástropní malby představuje zvěrokruh, znamení stále se opakujícího se času. Personifikace slunce a měsíce po stranách mají poukazovat na stálé působení ústředního argumentu, jenž hlásá Fama (Sláva).

en.name: Glory of Moravia
description: An obelisk, symbol of eternity, carries the emblem of Moravia. The upper section of the main element of the ceiling painting features a zodiac, the eternal cycle of time. The personifications of the sun and moon at the sides accentuate the eternal validity of the central slogan being unfurled by Fame.

ar.name: جامع عبد الله بن جعفر.
description:
يحمل جامع تفسرة اسم سيدي عبد الرحمن بن جعفر. وبالاستناد إلى الموروث الشفهي، فإن جوامع بني سنوس أًنشئت بأمر من عبد الله بن جعفر، ابن أخت الخليفة علي وصاحب عقبة بن نافع. يتم الدخول إلى الجامع من باحة يستعمل جزؤها الأيسر كمصلى (مكان يصلى فيه من حين لآخر) حُفر محرابه في حائط السور، وفي العمق المراحيض التي كانت تصلها المياه الجارية عبر قناة صغيرة آتية من نبع موجود وراء السور تماماً.  
شَكْلُ الجامع مربع ومقسم إلى ثلاث "بلاطات" متعامدة مع حائط القبلة وإلى ثلاثة أساكيب. وترتبط الدعامات ذات القواعد المربعة ببعضها البعض بعقود متجاوزة. تغطي "البلاطات" منحدرات مزدوجة من القرميد المجوف، على طبقات من جذوع العرعار المقشورة، وغطيت القبة أمام المحراب بسقف من القرميد المجوف ذو أربع انحدارات. تذكر هذه المئذنة بمآذن الجوامع خلال فترة بني عبد الواد من حيث أبعادها، ولكن ليس من حيث زخرفتها التي تتلخص في بعض البروزات من الآجر المطلي بالكلس كما هو الحال في باقي المئذنة.  
يستند العقد المتجاوز للمحراب على عمودين يحملان تاجين على شكل قاعدة هرمية، وبُني الكل وغُطِّيَ بالكلس. تُوجَ عقد المحراب بشريط على شكل عقد مفصص قليل البروز، يُحيط به شريط آخر على شكل عقد غير مفصص. يقوم فوق هذا الأخير شريط أفقي بارز بنفس سماكة العقدين، متعامد مع شريطين عموديين، ويشكلون – الشريط الأفقي والشريطان العموديان - إطاراً لواجهة المحراب. كانت الركنيات وشرائط العقود والشرائط المستقيمة والقائمة المتواجدة ضمن هذا الإطار مجردة من أي زخرفة. وتوجد في الحائط المقابل للمحراب مشكاتان مزخرفتان جزئياً بعناصر أصلها غير محدد. وفي الأصل، كان عقد المشكاة اليمنى مجرداً من فصوصه البارزة، ولم تكن الزاوية اليمنى العليا من الإطار تحمل أي زخرفة.

يتقدمُ المسجدَ صحنٌ، ويتخذُ شكل مربع مقسم إلى ثلاث بلاطات متعامدة مع جدار القبلة وثلاث أساكيب. السقف جملوني من القرميد؛ والدعامات ذات قاعدة مربعة، وتتصل فيما بينها بواسطة عقود متجاوزة. وغُطيت القبةُ بسقف من القرميد ذي أربع انحدارات؛ وشيِّدت المنارة من الآجر المطلي بالجير. يرتكز العقدُ المتجاوز للمحراب على عمودين تكللهما تيجان، وغطي المجموع بملاط من الجير.
dates: نهاية القرن 5 - بداية القرن 6 الهجري / القرن 12 الميلادي؛ أو نهاية القرن 7– بداية القرن 8 الهجري / القرن 14 الميلادي؛ ونهاية القرن 9 الهجري / القرن 16 الميلادي كأقرب تاريخ.
dynasty: أسرة بني عبد الواد، 633 – 926 هجري / 1236 - 1555 ميلادي.

en.name: Sidi ‘Abdallah Ibn Djafar Mosque.
description:
Tafessera's mosque is named after Sidi ‘Abdallah Ibn Djafar. Oral tradition maintains that the mosques of the Bani Snous were founded on the order of ‘Abdallah ibn Djafar, nephew of the Caliph ‘Ali and companion of ‘Uqba ibn Nafi. One enters the mosque via a courtyard, the left side of which is used as a *mossalla* (place of occasional prayer), with its *mihrab* dug out of the surrounding wall, and at the back of which are latrines that were provided with running water via a small duct leading from the source just behind the surrounding wall.  
The mosque is built on a square plan, divided into three *balatat* (naves), which are perpendicular to the *qibla* wall, and into three bays. The square-based pillars are interlinked through semi-circular arches. The *balatat* are covered by double-slope roofing composed of roman tiles on sheets of thuja (an evergreen tree) logs. A four-slope roman-tiled roof covers the dome in front of the *mihrab*. The minaret is reminiscent of those belonging to mosques of the ‘Abd al-Wadid period in its proportions but not in its decoration, which amounts to a few brick ledges rendered in lime like the rest of the minaret.  
The semi-circular arch of the *mihrab* rests on two columns surmounted by capitals in the shape of pyramidal drums. The whole structure is made of stone covered in lime mortar. This *mihrab* archway is surmounted by a band in the form of a foiled arch that slightly juts out. This is in turn framed by another arching band that is not foiled. A horizontal band sits above the latter and projects out to the same distance as the two arches, while sitting perpendicular to the two vertical bands, thus forming the frame of the *mihrab*. The cornerstones, the arched bands, and the vertical and horizontal bands of this frame are bereft of all decoration. Two niches situated in the wall facing the *mihrab* were partially decorated with motifs whose origins were difficult to identify. The arch of the niche on the right was initially without its relief foils; the upper right corner of the frame was also undecorated.

The square mosque, standing behind a courtyard, is divided into three naves perpendicular to the *qibla* wall and covered with a ridged tile roof. The square pillars are interlinked with horseshoe arches. The dome is covered by a tiled pyramidal roof. The minaret is built of lime-coated bricks. The horseshoe arch of the *mihrab* rests on two columns with capitals, with the whole built of masonry covered with lime mortar.
dates: Hegira end of 5th–beginning of 6th century (AD 12th century) or AH end of 7th–beginning of 8th century (AD 14th century) and AH end of 9th century (AD 16th century).
keywords: Religious architecture; minaret

es.name: Mezquita de Sidi Abd Allah ibn Yafar
description:
La mezquita de Tafessera lleva el nombre de Sidi Abd Allah ibn Yafar. La tradición oral relata que las mezquitas de los Beni Snous fueron fundadas por orden de Abd Allah ibn Yafar, sobrino del califa Ali y compañero de Uqba ibn Nafi. Se accede a la mezquita por un patio cuya parte izquierda sirve de *musalla* (lugar de oración ocasional) con su *mihrab* abierto en la muralla y, al fondo, las letrinas, a las que suministraba agua corriente un pequeño canal que partía del el manantial situado justo detrás de la muralla.  
La planta de la mezquita es cuadrada; está dividida en tres naves perpendiculares al muro de la *qibla* y en tres galerías. Los pilares de base cuadrada están unidos entre sí por arcos de herradura. Tejados a dos aguas sobre vigas de troncos de tuya cubren las naves. La cúpula situada delante del *mihrab* está cubierta por un tejado a cuatro aguas. El alminar evoca los de las mezquitas del periodo abdalwadí por sus proporciones, pero no por su decoración, que se limita a algunos salientes en ladrillo encalado, como el alminar entero.  
El arco de herradura del *mihrab* descansa sobre dos columnas rematadas con capiteles en forma de tronco de pirámide. El conjunto es de mampostería recubierta de mortero de cal. Este arco del *mihrab* está resaltado con una banda en forma de arco lobulado en relieve. Una segunda banda en forma de arco de herradura apuntado enmarca el anterior. El conjunto se inscribe en un alfiz en relieve cuyas bandas y enjutas muestran una decoración vegetal. En su origen, tanto el alfiz y las enjutas como las dos franjas que ciñen el arco del *mihrab* carecían de ornamentación. En el muro situado frente al *mihrab* se encuentra un nicho geminado que estaba parcialmente ornamentado con motivos de origen incierto. En principio, el arco del nicho situado a la derecha no presentaba estos lóbulos en relieve; el ángulo superior derecho del marco no tenía decoración.

La mezquita, de planta cuadrada y precedida por un patio, está dividida en tres naves perpendiculares al muro de la *qibla* y en tres galerías. La cubierta es un tejado a dos aguas. Los pilares, de base cuadrada, están unidos entre sí por arcos de herradura. La cúpula situada delante del *mihrab* está cubierta por un tejado a cuatro aguas. El alminar está construido con ladrillos encalados. El arco de herradura del *mihrab* descansa sobre dos columnas rematadas con capiteles en forma de tronco de pirámide. El conjunto es de mampostería recubierta de mortero de cal.
dates: Finales del siglo V-principios del VI de la Hégira / siglo XII d. C. o bien finales del VII-principios del VIII / XIV; finales del siglo IX / XVI como fecha más reciente.
keywords: Arquitectura religiosa; alminar

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Abdellah Ben Djafar.
description:
La mosquée de Tafessera porte le nom de Sidi Abdellah Ben Djafar. La tradition orale veut que les mosquées des Beni Snous aient été fondées sur ordre d'Abdellah Ben Djafar, neveu du calife Ali et compagnon de Okba Ben Nafi. On accède à la mosquée par une cour dont la partie gauche sert de *mossalla* (lieu de prière occasionnel) avec son *mihrab* creusé dans le mur d'enceinte et, au fond, les latrines, qui étaient alimentées en eau courante par un petit canal venant de la source située juste derrière le mur d'enceinte.  
  
Le plan de la mosquée est carré, il est divisé en trois *balatat* (nefs) perpendiculaires au mur de la *qibla* et en trois travées. Les piliers à base carrée sont reliés entre eux par des arcs outrepassés. Des doubles-pentes en tuiles canal, sur des nappes de rondins en thuya, couvrent les *balatat*. La coupole au-devant du *mihrab* est couverte par une toiture en tuiles canal à quatre pentes. Le minaret évoque ceux des mosquées de la période abdalwadide par ses proportions, mais non par son décor, qui se résume à quelques saillies en briques enduites à la chaux, comme, du reste, le minaret tout entier.  
  
L'arc outrepassé du *mihrab* repose sur deux colonnes surmontées de chapiteaux en tronc de pyramide. L'ensemble est en maçonnerie recouverte d'un mortier de chaux. Cet arc du *mihrab* est surmonté d'un bandeau en arc lobé légèrement saillant. Un autre bandeau en arc, non lobé, encadre le précédent. Sur ce dernier repose une bande horizontale, en saillie de la même épaisseur que les deux arcs, perpendiculaire à deux bandes verticales formant ainsi l'encadrement de la face du *mihrab*. Dans cet encadrement, les écoinçons, les bandes des arcs et les bandeaux verticaux et horizontaux étaient dépourvus de tout décor. Dans le mur qui fait face au *mihrab* se trouvent deux niches qui étaient partiellement décorées de motifs dont l'origine reste mal définie. Initialement, l'arc de la niche de droite était dépourvu de ces lobes en relief ; l'angle droit en haut de l'encadrement ne portait pas de décor.

La mosquée, précédée d'une cour, est carrée, divisée en trois nefs perpendiculaires au mur de la *qibla* et trois travées. La couverture est une double-pente en tuiles. Les piliers à base carrée sont reliés entre eux par des arcs outrep assés. La coupole est couverte par une toiture en tuiles à quatre pentes. Le minaret est construit en briques enduites à la chaux. L'arc outrepassé du *mihrab* repose sur deux colonnes à chapiteaux, l'ensemble étant en maçonnerie recouverte d'un mortier de chaux.
dates: Fin Ve-début VIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.) ou fin VIIe-début VIIIe siècle H (XIVe siècle J.-C.) et fin IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.) pour la date la plus récente.
keywords: architecture religieuse ; minaret

de.name: Verklärung der hl. Gordianus und Epimachus
description:
Anhand ihrer raumerweiternden Scheinarchitektur erinnern die Deckenfresken an diejenigen des Andrea Pozzo in Sant‘Ignazio in Rom, welche Franz Georg Herrmann dort 1712/13 während eines Studienaufenthalts besichtigt haben muss.  
Die im Langhaus dargestellte Apotheose des Hl. Epimachus mit Verweis auf dessen Tod im Feuerofen ergänzt im Chor diejenige des Hl. Gordian samt Darstellung des zuvor Enthaupteten. Rundumlaufende Kartuschen enthalten Grisaille-Bilder der vier Kirchenväter und Zwölf Apostel. Am unteren Rand der Scheinkuppel erscheint Pfarrer Klein in Begleitung des Kirchendieners als Beobachter auf einem Balkon, sozusagen als Vermittler zwischen Himmel und Erde. Dem gläubigen Betrachter wird somit die Möglichkeit aufgezeigt, auch in den Himmel zu gelangen, für den symbolisch die (Schein-)Kuppel steht. Durch das geöffnete Butzenscheibenfenster links neben dem Balkon fliegt ein Vogel, ironischerweise ein Dompfaff, in das Kuppelinnere, was durch Evozierung von Lebendigkeit dem Illusionistischen zusätzliche Wirklichkeitsnähe verschafft.

en.name: Transfiguration of St. Gordian and Epimachus
description: By means of their space-extending illusory architecture, the ceiling frescoes are reminiscent of those of Andrea Pozzo in Sant’Ignazio in Rome, where Franz Georg Herrmann must have visited during a study sojourn in 1712/13. The apotheosis of St. Epimachus with reference to his death in a furnace of fire illustrated in the nave compliments that of St. Gordian including a representation of this previously beheaded martyr. Circular cartouches contain grisaille images of the Four Church Fathers and Twelve Apostles. Parish priest Klein appears, accompanied by the sacristan, on the lower band of the illusory cupola as an observer on a balcony, that is to say, as mediator between heaven and earth. Thus, the devout observer is shown the possibility of reaching heaven for which the illusory cupola symbolically stands. Through the open crown glass window, a bird (whose German compound name “Dompfaff” [bullfinch] ironically alludes to the dome as well as to the priest)  flies to the left of the balcony into the interior of the cupola which provides the illusion of additional closeness to reality by evoking liveliness.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: ثوب امرأة(إنتاري)
description: كانت الملابس العثمانية التقليدية تصمم لتخفي الأشخاص (تغطي كامل الجسم) وهو ما يفسر استخدام العديد من الألبسة فوق بعضها البعض. من ناحية أخرى هذه الطبقات المتعددة أكدت على التنوع الكبير للأقمشة وتباين الألوان المدهش و البنية الغنية للقطع المطرزة. والإنتاري هو مميز كلباس نسائي عثماني : طوله من الكتفين حتى العقب أو أقصر ،ويكون مفتوح عموما من الأمام و يملك أكمام طويلة مفتوحة عند المرفق لكشف المناطق المطرزة وأيضا الألوان والتزيين على الأكمام لأسفل الثوب. والتطريز الحريري الكثيف يغطي كل سطح الإنتاري. والنماذج المزهرة والتفاصيل المعمارية المميزة للطراز مشابهة للتزيين الغني لمطرزات معينة المستخدمة يوميا من نفس الفترة.
dates: القرن 12 –بداية القرن 13 هجري / اواخر القرن 18   ميلادي
keywords: إنتاري

en.name: Woman’s robe (*entari*)
description: Traditional Ottoman clothing was designed to conceal the figure, which explains the use of several superimposed garments. On the other hand, these multiple layers emphasized the great variety of fabrics, the striking colour contrasts, and the rich texture of the embroidered pieces. The *entari* is typical for the Ottoman female dress: ankle-length or shorter, generally open down the front, it has long, narrow sleeves slit at the elbow to reveal the embroidered areas, as well as the colours and decoration on the sleeves of the garment underneath. Dense silk embroidery covers the entire surface of this *entari*. The floral patterns and the architectural details are stylistically similar to the rich decoration on certain embroideries of daily use dating from the same period.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
dates: Hegira late 12th – early 13th century / AD late 18th century
keywords: Entari
materials: Wool embroidered with silk, silver-gilt thread and strips, sequins
tags: Wool embroidered with silk, silver-gilt thread and strips, sequins

en.name: Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861)
short_description: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861). When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.
keywords: Abdul-Mejid, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Syria, Palestine; Hungarian refugees

ar.name: مصحف
description: بدأت المخطوطات العثمانية المزينة بطراز متأثر بالطراز الأوربي في الظهور في النصف الأول من القرن الثامن عشر واستمر إنتاجها في السنوات الأولى من القرن العشرين. وقد أثر بشكل خاص طراز الباروك والروكوكو الفني في القرنين السابع عشر والثامن عشر على طراز التذهيب للمصاحف العثمانية مثل هذا المصحف. والشخص الذي قام بتذهيب هذه المخطوطة – اسمه عطا – قد شمل بكل فخر توقيعه عليه ( وحق له ذلك) بين التزيينات للصفحة النهائية.أيضا من المرئي جدا على هذه الصفحة النهائية أثر وخز الذهب المنفذ بإبرة رفيعة ذات رأس غير مدبب والمراد به تحقيق أثر عميق و تحديد وحتى إعطاء إحساس بالحركة لسطح الذهب وبالتالي الرفع من قيمة التذهيب ككل.

en.name: Qur'an
description: Ottoman manuscripts decorated in a European-influenced style began to appear in the first half of the 18th century and continued to be produced into the early years of the 20th century. It was specifically the Baroque and Rococo styles of European art of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries that influenced the illumination style of Ottoman Qur’ans such as this. The illuminator—named ‘Ata—has proudly (and rightly so) included his signature amongst the decoration of the final folio. Also very visible on this final folio is the pricking of the gold, executed with a fine, blunt-tipped needle and intended to add depth, definition and even a sense of movement to the surface of the gold and thus to enhance the illumination as a whole.
keywords: koran; calligraphy; script; illumination; floral decoration; arabesque; religious manuscript
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper
tags: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

en.name: Zamzam Water Bottle
description:
This plastic bottle of Zamzam water, purchased during the pilgrimage (*‘Umrah*), represents how sacred traditions coexist with modern systems of production and distribution. Drawn from the Zamzam Well in Mecca, this water holds deep spiritual significance for Muslims worldwide, symbolising divine mercy and blessing.  
  
Today, Zamzam water is bottled and sealed in modern factories to ensure hygiene and facilitate safe transport. Pilgrims can purchase it directly at airports or distribution centres, allowing them to carry home a sacred element of their journey. In Mecca itself, public coolers and dispensers provide pilgrims with direct access to the holy water, continuing a practice of hospitality and devotion that has endured for centuries.  
  
This object embodies how faith, modern technology, and global mobility intersect, preserving tradition in contemporary life.

en.name: *The Necropolis, Petra, March 9th, 1839*
short_description: The Necropolis' of Petra appears in Volume 3 of 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia' from drawings made on the spot by David Roberts, lithographed by Louis Haghe and published in six volumes by F.G. Moon in London between 1842-1845. Situated at the beginning of the steep ravine or siq that leads into the heart of Petra, both the so-called 'obelisk tomb' shown in the centre and the Triclinium situated to its lower right still exist today, even if much eroded since the days Roberts visited Petra in 1839. In the 19th century, Petra was one of Europe's most enduring Orientalist fascinations, but it also played a part in the region's more modern history. In October 1917, T. E. Lawrence, to divert Turkish military resources away from the British advance before the Third Battle of Gaza, led a small force of Syrians and Arabs in successfully defending Petra against a combined force of Turks and Germans. Bedouin women from the Petra area - under the leadership of their Sheikh's wife - were recruited to fight in the defense of the city.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
keywords: siq; Triclinium

en.name: She the fresh
description: In 2014, Rostislav Materka (1982) presented this piece as an entry into the competition organised by the European Glass Experience. According to the artist, the concept that governs the creation of this piece was following “the basics of craftmanship”. Specifically, it drew on the technical abilities of the craftspeople in workshops in the Czech Republic. The challenge was to create the piece without moulds or other external aids, in search of the shape created as a result of the physical properties of the glass itself. Once this shape was achieved, the artist managed to reshape it by sculpting, redefining its visual appearance. It can be said that he upturned the initial idea.
holder: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja
keywords: Glass sculpture; Materka; European Glass Experience; Czech Republic
partner: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja

es.name: She the fresh
description: Rostislav Materka (1982), presentó, en 2014, esta obra al concurso organizado por la European Glass Experience. Según el artista el concepto que presidió la elaboración de esta obra fue seguir "los principios de la artesanía". Concretamente las habilidades técnicas de los artesanos de los talleres de la Republica Checa. El reto era realizar la peiza sin moldes niayudas externas, buscar la forma que resulta de las propiedades físicas del vidrio. Una vez conseguida esta forma, el artista por medio del tallado consigue reconfigurarla, redefiniendo su apariencia visual. Por lo que se podría concluir que da la vuelta a la idea inicial.

en.name: Prayer chain
description: Islamic prayer beads (*misbaḥa*) consist of three sections of beads separated from each other by two larger marker beads (*imām*) for easier counting. The last bead, which is usually a much larger piece in the shape of a bottle neck, is called "minaret imam" (*yad*) and stands for the greatest and secret hundredth name of Allah. The *misbaḥa* is meant for reciting prayers, praising Allah, and as a talisman.
materials: Glass beads, cotton string, silk tassel
