en.name: Cup of early-Christian inspiration
short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century. In the second half of the 19th century the tradition of Murano glass experienced a revival and a museum in Murano was created with an archive to offer models to artisans to copy. Objects included archaeological glasses of Phoenician, Egyptian, Alexandrian, Roman and Byzantine origin. Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. In Venice, one of the most popular glass factories was the Salviati Society, which was awarded with several prizes at National and International Exhibitions. The Venice-Murano Company made the smoked glass cup with gold leaf and biblical scenes (Inv. n.3046) recalling Early Christian tradition dating to the second half of the 19th century. Aquamarine glass and gold leaf medals are applied on the cup.
holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini
keywords: Applied arts; minor arts; reproduction; model; manufacture; craftsmanship; museums of applied arts; motifs; collection; collector; glasswork; Murano glass; early Christian art; Romanticism; gold leaf; smoked glass
partner: MIBACT | Collection of former Museum of Industrial Art (M.A.I.)

ar.name: سجادة لوتو
description:
تُظهر السجادة في الحقل الأوسط شبكة من الأرابيسك المنمق باللون الأصفر والمرتبة على شكل صلبان ومثمنات على أرضية حمراء. هذه الزخرفة هي سمة من سمات ما يسمى بسجاد "لوتو"، الذي سمي على اسم رسام عصر النهضة لورنزو لوتو (1480-1557 م / 885-963 هجري)، الذي رسم مثل هذه السجادة على لوحة المذبح الشهيرة عام 1542.  
  
عادةً ما يكون لحدود سجاد "اللوتو" زخارف على شكل احرف عربية بالخطوط الكوفية الزائفة، والتي يتم تفسيرها أحيانًا على أنها مزيج من حرفي اللام والألف. ومن ناحية أخرى، يوجدلفائف بسيطة على أرضية زرقاء متوسطة، وربما يعود إلى النماذج الفارسية.  
  
تم إنتاج سجاد "لوتو" في الورش التجارية في غرب تركيا منذ حوالي عام 1516 إلى حوالي 1700.
dates: القرن 11  - بداية القرن 12 هجري /القرن 17 - بداية القرن  18 ميلادي

en.name: *Lotto* carpet
description:
In the central field, the carpet shows a network of yellow stylised arabesques arranged in crosses and octagons on a red ground. This decoration is characteristic of so-called Lotto carpets, named after the Renaissance painter Lorenzo Lotto (AD 1480-1556/57 / Hegira 885-963), who immortalised such a carpet on a famous altarpiece in 1542.  
  
‘Lotto’ carpets usually have a border in pseudo-kufi, which is sometimes interpreted as a combination of the letters lam and alif. Here, on the other hand, it is a simple leaf tendril on a medium blue ground, which perhaps goes back to Persian models.  
  
‘Lotto’ carpets were produced in commercial workshops in western Turkey from about 1516 to about 1700.

ar.name: تل أبو سربوط.
description: يقع تل أبو سربوط في غور الأردن الأوسط على بُعد 70 كم إلى الشمال الغربي من عمّان،  ويبعد 1.5 كم عن تل دير علا.  الموقع عبارة عن تل قليل الارتفاع أبعاده 250 م من الشرق إلى الغرب، و 125 م من الشمال إلى الجنوب، وهو ينخفض 252 م عن مستوى سطح البحر.  جرت في الموقع ثلاثة مواسم من الحفريات الأثرية بين عامي 1988- 1990، وذلك بالتعاون بين دائرة الآثار العامة في الأردن، وجامعة لايدن والمعهد الهولندي لدراسات الشرق الأدنى.  كشفت الحفريات عن بناء يتألف من عدة غرف وساحات مكشوفة، في واحدة منها فرن للخبز (طابون).  أما البناء فقد بُني من الطوب الطيني المجفف في الشمس على أساسات حجرية، وغطيت واجهة جدرانه وأرضيته بالقصارة.  دلت الحفريات الأثرية على أن الموقع كان مرتبطاً بإنتاج السكر في العصر المملوكي، حيث كان مركزاً لخزن وتوزيع السكر الذي كان يُنتج في المنطقة المحيطة بالموقع.

تقع تلَّة أبو سربوط في وادي الأردن الأوسط، على بعد 70 كم شمال غرب عمَّان. إنها تلَّة متواضعة، بطول يبلغ نحو 250 م، وعرض 125 م، وأعلى نقطة فيها هي 252 م، دون مستوى سطح البحر. عليها منشآت مبنيَّة بالطوب الصلصالي المُجفَّف، فوق أساسات من الحجر. كان الموقع جزءاً مهماً من صناعة إنتاج السكر في المنطقة، نظراً لأن صناعة السكر كانت مصدراً رئيسياً من مصادر الواردات في وادي الأردن، أيام المماليك. وعلى الرغم من أنها لم تكن مرتبطة ارتباطاً مباشراً بعملية تكرير السكر الفعلية، فإنها بقيت مركزاً مهماً لتخزين السكر المنتج في المنطقة وتوزيعها.
keywords: أساس حجري؛ إنتاج سكَّر؛ طوب طيني؛ غور الأردن؛ موقع صناعي؛ وادي الأردن.

en.name: Tall Abu Sarbut.
description:
Tall Abu Sarbut is located in the Central Jordan Valley about 70 km northwest of Amman, 1.5 km from Dayr Alla. It is a low hill that measures 250 m east to west and about 125 m from north to south. The highest point of the tall is at 252 m below sea level.  
Three seasons of archaeological investigations were conducted at the site between 1988–90 as a joint venture between the Department of Antiquities of Jordan, the University of Leiden and the Netherlands Institute for the Near East. The main objective of the project was to verify the nature and the extent of the site.  
Archaeological excavations uncovered a large Mamluk multi-roomed building with courtyards. In one of the courtyards a bread oven (*tabun*) was found. The walls were built of sun-dried mud bricks on stone foundations. The walls and the floors were plastered. Archaeological investigations demonstrated that the site was an important part of the sugar-production industry in the area; the sugar industry being a main source of revenue in the Jordan Valley during the Mamluk period. The nature of the archaeological finds discovered during the excavations showed that the site was not associated directly with the actual refinery of sugar but it was an important storage and distribution centre for the sugar that was produced in the area.

es.name: Tall Abu Sarbut
description:
Tall Abu Sarbut es una colina poco pronunciada que mide 250 m de este a oeste y 125 m de norte a sur. Su altitud máxima es de 252 m por debajo del nivel del mar.  
Entre 1988 y 1990 se llevaron a cabo en el lugar tres fases de estudios arqueológicos, en una labor conjunta del Ministerio de Antigüedades de Jordania, la Universidad de Leiden y el Instituto Holandés para Oriente Próximo. El principal objetivo del proyecto era verificar la naturaleza y extensión del sitio.  
En estas excavaciones se halló un gran edificio mameluco con varias salas y patios, en uno de los cuales se encontró un horno de pan (*tabun*). Los muros se construyeron sobre cimientos de piedra con ladrillos de adobe secado al sol. Las paredes y los suelos estaban enlucidos.  
La industria azucarera fue una de las principales fuentes de ingresos del valle del Jordán durante el periodo mameluco, y los estudios arqueológicos han demostrado que este lugar fue un importante centro de producción de azúcar. No obstante, los hallazgos arqueológicos realizados dejan patente que Tall Abu Sarbut no se dedicó al refinado, sino a la distribución y almacenaje del azúcar que se producía en la zona.

Tall Abu Sarbut está en el valle central del Jordán, 70 km al noroeste de Ammán. Es una loma de 250 × 125 m. Su altitud máxima es de 252 m por debajo del nivel del mar.  
Presenta varias estructuras construidas con ladrillos de adobe secados al sol sobre cimientos de piedra. Fue un eslabón importante de la cadena de producción azucarera en la zona, una actividad que llegó a ser la principal fuente de ingresos de este valle durante el periodo mameluco. Aunque no está relacionado directamente con el refinado, fue un importante centro de distribución y almacenaje.
dates: Siglos VII-IX de la Hégira / XIV-XV d. C.
keywords: Centro industrial; valle del Jordán; ladrillos de adobe; cimientos de piedra; producción de azúcar.

fr.name: Tall Abou Sarbout.
description:
Le Tall Abou Sarbout est situé dans la vallée centrale du Jourdain, à 70 km environ d'Amman et 1,5 km de Dayr Alla. C'est une petite colline de 250 m de long d'est en ouest sur 125 m de large environ du nord au sud. Son altitude maximum est de 252 m.  
Trois campagnes de fouilles archéologiques ont été conjointement menées sur place entre 1988 et 1990 par le Département des antiquités de Jordanie, l'Université de Leyde et l'Institut néerlandais pour le Proche-Orient. Leur objectif principal était de vérifier la nature et l'étendue du site.  
Ces fouilles ont permis la mise au jour d'une importante construction mamelouke à plusieurs salles et cours. Dans l'une de celles-ci, un four à pain (*taboun*) a été découvert. Les murs ainsi que les sols étaient en briques de terre cuites au soleil posées sur des fondations en pierre et plâtrées. Ces recherches ont démontré que le site jouait un rôle important dans la production sucrière de la région, principale source de revenus de la vallée du Jourdain pendant la période mamelouke. Le lieu n'était pas concerné par la raffinerie du sucre mais par sa conservation et sa distribution.

Tall Abou Sarbout est situé dans la vallée centrale de la Jordanie à environ 70 km au nord-ouest d’Amman. C’est une colline basse mesurant 250 x 125 m environ, son point culminant étant à 252 m sous le niveau de la mer. Il comporte des structures construites de briques de terre séchée au soleil sur des fondations de pierre. Le site jouait un rôle important dans la production sucrière de la région, l’industrie sucrière étant la principale source de revenus de la vallée du Jourdain pendant la période mamelouke. Bien que n’ayant pas de rapport direct avec la raffinerie de sucre à proprement parler, ce fut un important centre de stockage et de distribution du sucre produit dans la région.
dates: VIIIe-IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XIVe-XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: site industriel ; vallée du Jourdain ; briques de terre crue ; fondations en pierre ; production de sucre

en.name: Bottle
description: Glass vessels embellished using the relief-cut technique hold a special place in the history of Islamic glasswork. Though many such vessels were produced, only a few exceptional examples with complex cutting patterns survive today. One such example is this bottle in the Aga Khan Museum Collection. It can be dated to the 9th or 10th century, for outstanding examples of geometrical relief-cut decoration only emerged during this relatively brief period. Iranian glasshouses seem to have specialized in these patterns.
keywords: Bottle; glass; vessel; iridescent; geometric
materials: Glass, colourless, silvery-white iridescence; blown, relief cut, tooled, worked on the pontil

en.name: Tarf I
description: Driven by Taruffi, the Tarf I debuted with an uncompressed Guzzi 500 twin- cylinder engine developing 44 horsepower at 7,000 revolutions per minute: six records were set from 1948 to 1949. In 1953 the Guzzi engine was replaced by an air-cooled 4four-cylinder Gilera developing 60 HP at 10,500 rpm. This set seven records in 1953 and six in 1954. In 1956, the engine was again replaced by a 550 cc displacement and developed 65 HP at 10,500 rpm. With this engine the Tarf I achieved three records for the 750 class on the track at Monza. In 1957, with a four-cylinder Gilera 350 cc engine developing 40 HP at 11,500 rpm, seven new records were set. The 1957 model, on display here, is capable of traveling at up to 212km/h.
keywords: Historic Car; Engine; Prototype

en.name: Castle
description: The importance of Pombal during the early years of the kingdom of Portugal derived from its position between the River Mondego and the Muslim lands on the route of the Tagus. The castle was built or rebuilt in 1161, by Gualdim Pais and held by the Knights Templar. In 1319, it was handed over to the Order of Christ, which maintained it as head quarters of one of its commanderies. D. Manuel I, Administrator General of the Order, restored the castle at the beginning of the 16th century, and granted the town a charter in 1512.

en.name: Tile Plate
description: The surface is covered in white clay and slip decorated in cobalt blue, coral red and green with black contours under a transparent colourless glaze. The plate’s surface is decorated with symmetrically distributed branches of tulips and red carnations with blue spots rising vertically from a single stem. Two tulips and carnations in the centre of the composition are held in place by a bracket. The composition is embellished with tulip and carnation buds, small stylised flowers, with cobalt blue Chinese-style clouds interspersed throughout the design. The use of bud and clover motifs in the decoration of plates was common during this period. A narrow border of white half-rosette flowers with red centres is framed by cobalt blue inside the rim. A double tulip and open rose motif alternate on the back.

en.name: Palais Kobbet el-Nhas
short_description: This palace is located at the end of a great courtyard, lined with trees and featuring a large elevated façade and gallery, sitting above an annex, accessed via a grand staircase. The full beauty of this palace is evident even from the patio, which leads to a double driba (vestibule), with a vaulted ceiling embellished with Andalusian motifs carved in stucco, and paved with marble and decorated with earthenware tiles, which leads to a great hall. The wall decorations are made from luxurious earthenware and refined marble, and the floor is decorated as a black and white checkerboard. The domed ceilings, like the vaulted ceilings, are decorated with carved stucco with geometric and arabesque patterns. Other rooms are attached to every corner of this great hall, which, like the second reception hall in the right wing of the palace, has a wooden ceiling painted gold in an Italian style.
history: To the West of Bardo the fresh air and cultivated fields of the Manouba plain attracted royalty and nobility who were moving to their springtime residences. The presence of a revered saint, Lalla Manoubiya, added to the attraction of the area. The Palais Kobbet el-Nhas, built by Mohamed Errachid Bey (Muhammad al-Rashid Bey) c. 1756 and reorganised by Hammouda Pacha Bey in the late 19th century, is located amongst these residences. The palace itself is named after him, a reference to his brass domed pavilion which had originally been built for the beylical harem. The neighbouring Palais de la Rose, which seems to have been connected to it originally, is equally vast and luxurious.
keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Palais Kobbet-Ennhas
short_description: On découvre le palais au fond d’une grande cour d’honneur plantée d’arbres avec une large façade avec galerie surhaussée au-dessus des dépendances et à laquelle on accède par un large escalier d’honneur. Le palais dévoile toute sa richesse et sa somptuosité à partir du patio qui, précédé d’une double *driba* dallée de marbre et ornée de carreaux de faïence à fond bleu et plafonnée d’une voûte décorée de stuc sculpté en motifs morisco-andalous, donne accès, au fond, à la salle d’apparat. Revêtement mural en faïence de luxe et marbre raffiné en damier noir et blanc au sol. Les plafonds de la coupole ainsi que les voûtes offrent un ciselage de stucs en arabesque et décor géométrique. Les pièces se répartissent tout autour des angles externes de cette salle qui, comme la deuxième salle de réception dans l’aile droite du palais, est dotée de plafonds en bois peint et doré, ouvrages à l’italienne.
history: A l’ouest du Bardo, la plaine de la Manouba, avec ses terres cultivées et la salubrité de l’air, attirait les souverains et les dignitaires désireux d’installer leurs résidences de printemps. Cet attrait est encore renforcé par la présence en ce lieu d’une sainte très vénérée, Lalla Manoubiya. Parmi ces résidences, le palais Kobbet-Ennhas, qui fut construit par Mohamed Errachid Bey vers 1756, les principaux aménagements correspondent au règne de Hammouda Pacha Bey au début de XIXe siècle. Ce palais porte son nom par référence à son kiosque à coupole de cuivre construit à l’origine pour le plaisir du harem beylical. Avoisinant, le palais de la Rose, auquel il semble avoir été rattaché à l’origine, également vaste et luxueux.
keywords: Architecture; Art; Peinture; Stuc; Mosaïque; Marbre; Céramique
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: حوض نصف / شبه كروي
description: الرصيعة الوسطى في الداخل محفورة بشكل فيل مكسو الذي ينتهي جذعه برأس رجل ملتحي. ويحمل الفيل هودجا عليه ثلاثة أشخاص. ويوجد على رأس الحيوان سائق الفيل بينما في المؤخرة يوجد موسيقي. ويوجد عصابة داخلية من طيور السمان أو الحجل تتحرك لليمين وعصابة مركزية من الأرانب البرية طويلة الآذان تجري في الاتجاه المعاكس وتحيط بالمشهد المتحرك. والعصابة الخارجية على طول الإطار مزينة بنقش كتابي من تبريكات بالخط الكوفي مقابل خلفية بشكل حلقة مخرمة. ويملك السطح الخارجي نجمة محفورة في الوسط مشكلة بواسطة مثلثين متداخلين والمضلعات السداسي الناتج ونقاط النجوم مزينة بأشكال مزهرة. ويوجد نقش كتابي بتبريكات بالخط الكوفي حول الإطار.

en.name: Hemispherical basin
description: The central medallion on the interior is engraved with a caparisoned elephant whose trunk terminates in a bearded human head. The elephant bears a *howdah* with three figures. At the head of the animal there is the *mahout*, while at the tail is a musician. An inner band of quails or partridges moving to the right and a central band of long-eared hares running on the opposite direction surround the animated scene. The outer band along the rim is decorated with benedictory inscription in *kufic* against a ring-matted background. The exterior has a central engraved star formed by two interlaced triangles; the resulting central hexagons and the points of the stars are decorated with floral motifs. A band of benedictory inscription in *kufic* is around the rim.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
keywords: basin; high-tin bronze; Iran; metalwork; engraving; elephant; howdah; musician; kufic; Seljuq
partner: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art

en.name: Reconstruction of a late AH 13th – early 14th century / AD 19th – early 20th-century trading vessel
short_description: This reconstruction of a *baghla* was commissioned by His Highness Dr Shaikh Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi in 2004 to represent the most important and largest type of trading craft that plied the waters between the Gulf and India in the late 13th/ 19th century and the early 14th/ 20th century. Built by Emirati and Omani specialists, the vessel incorporates all the traditional elements of a baghla: a length of around 30 meters, two masts for lateen sails, its typically parrot-shaped stem head, its high square stern and its lavishly carved design. All these features were originally influenced by the design of Portuguese ships.
holder: Sharjah Maritime Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
keywords: baghla

en.name: *Saint Philip Benizi in Glory*
description: In 1697 Domenico Maria Viani was summoned to Imola by the Servite fathers in order to paint three pictures for their church. One of them, depicting “the Virgin Mary and the patron saints of Imola” is no more extant, however we still have the “Saint Philip Benizi in Glory” and “the Saint Pellegrino Laziosi Healed by the Crucifix.” Viani worked in Imola for a year and a half on these paintings. With his saint Philip Benizi, the Bolognese painter entered his mature phase, combining the style of Guido Reni learned in his father’s workshop with the baroque language of another Bolognese painter, Domenico Maria Canuti and employing a Venetian palette with warm colours. The group of the saint with the angels is seen from below and it gives the impression of the image continuing outside of the frame. The painting has always been mentioned by guides and art historians as very beautiful. The sumptuous gilded frame was carved in 1710 by the Imolese sculptor Giuseppe Giuliani.

The painting was made in 1697 by the Bolognese painter Domenico Maria Viani for the Servite fathers of Imola. It is a mixture of classical academic culture and a fully baroque style. The carved frame was made by the Imolese sculptor Giuseppe Giuliani.
holder: Church of Santa Maria dei Servi
dates: Second half of the seventeenth century
keywords: Domenico Maria Viani; Servite; religious orders Frame; Woodwork; religious/liturgical painting; Altarpiece
partner: Museums' System of the Province of Bologna

it.name: *San Filippo Benizi in gloria*
description: Nel 1697 Domenico Maria Viani venne chiamato a Imola dai padri Serviti per realizzare tre opere da porre in chiesa. Perduto il dipinto che raffigurava “Maria Vergine e i santi protettori di Imola”, rimangono i due dipinti con “San Filippo Benizi in gloria” e “San Pellegrino Laziosi sanato dal crocifisso”. Il lavoro a Imola occupò Viani per un anno e mezzo. Con il san Filippo Benizi, il pittore bolognese realizzò un'opera matura, che, partendo dalle reminescenze reniane conosciute alla scuola del padre Giovanni Maria Viani, anch'egli pittore, aggiornò sul linguaggio barocco del bolognese Domenico Maria Canuti e con l'utilizzo di una tavolozza neo veneta, dai toni accesi. Il gruppo del santo con gli angeli è caratterizzato da uno scorcio di sottinsù che suggerisce una spazialità aperta che sembra forzare i limiti del dipinto ed ambire alla grande decorazione. Il dipinto, nel corso dei secoli, viene ricordato unanimemente dalla storiografia come opera di alta qualità. E' posto in una sontuosa cornice dorata realizzata dall'intagliatore imolese Giuseppe Giuliani e dorata nel 1710.

Il dipinto venne realizzato nel 1697 dal bolognese Domenico Maria Viani per i padri serviti di Imola. E’ frutto della mescolanza tra una cultura figurativa ancora accademica, di stampo classicista e l’utilizzo di un linguaggio pienamente barocco. La cornice intagliata in cui è collocato è opera dell’imolese Giuseppe Giuliani.
holder: Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Servi
Chiesa di santa Maria dei Servi
place: Chiesa di santa Maria dei Servi
keywords: Domenico Maria Viani; Serviti; Cornice; Lavorazione del legno; pittura religiosa; pala d'altare; ordini religiosi

en.name: Bab Mrissa
description:
Without doubt the most ancient monument that is known to us from the Merinid period, this monumental gate was built between 658/1260 and 668/1270, allowing boats to pass through the enclosure via a canal which linked the Bu Regreg to a naval dockyard which is now silted up. Having partially eroded, it remains none the less striking, through the sheer scale of its arch, as wide as it is high, with an 8 m. diagonal rib entrance. Its construction was designed by a Sevillian architect, who knew how to adapt the structure of a traditional Moroccan gate in order to give it a new function, notably avoiding the angled bends which characterise gates used for defence. Flanked, in the same way as Almohad gates are, by two rectangular towers, but without a single arcature lining its smooth keystones, it features, on one of its facades, a rich floral decoration, whilst the other facade is totally bare.  
If Daniel Defoe’s novel *Robinson Crusoe*, published in 1719, is not considered a work of fiction, then it can be said that its hero was captured before the gates of Salé, and entered the town through Bab Mrissa, before escaping to then run aground on a desert island.

es.name: Bab Mrissa
description:
El monumento más antiguo conocido de la época meriní es, sin duda, esta puerta monumental, construida entre 658/1260 y 668/1270, que permitía la entrada de barcos intramuros a través de un canal que unía el Bu Regreg con un arsenal actualmente encenagado. Aunque parcialmente hundida, continúa siendo sorprendente por la amplitud de su arcada, tan ancha como larga, con una ojiva de 8 m de luz. Fue construida por un arquitecto sevillano que supo adaptar la estructura de la puerta marroquí tradicional a una nueva función; en particular, suprimiendo los recodos característicos de las puertas defensivas. Flanqueada por dos torres rectangulares, igual que las puertas almohades, pero sin ninguna arcada que venga a duplicar las dovelas lisas, tiene en una de sus fachadas una decoración floral muy rica, en tanto que la otra está totalmente desprovista de decoración.  
Si la novela de Daniel Defoe *Robinson Crusoe* (1719) no fuera una obra de ficción, diríamos que fue junto a Salé donde capturaron al protagonista, y que fue Bab Mrissa su puerta de entrada antes de huir para encallar en una isla desierta.

fr.name: Bab Mrissa
description: Sans doute le plus ancien monument connu de l’époque mérinide, cette porte monumentale a été construite entre 658/1260 et 668/1270 et permettait l’accès intra-muros aux bateaux par un canal qui reliait le Bou Regreg à un arsenal maintenant ensablé. Actuellement partiellement enfouie, elle n’en demeure pas moins frappante par l’ampleur de son arcade, aussi large que haute avec une ogive de 8 m d’ouverture. Sa construction est due à un architectes sévillan qui a su adapter la structure de la porte marocaine traditionnelle à une fonction nouvelle, évitant en particulier les coudes qui caractérisent les portes défensives. Flanquée de deux tours rectangulaires comme le sont les portes almohades, mais sans qu’aucune arcature ne vienne doubler les claveaux lisses, elle comporte sur l’une de ses façades un décor floral très riche alors que l’autre en est totalement dépourvue. Si le roman de Daniel Defoe, *Robinson Crusoé*, publié en 1719, n’est pas une fiction, c’est devant Salé que son héros a été capturé et c’est par Bab Mrissa qu’il est entré dans la ville avant de s’en évader pour échouer ensuite sur une île déserte.

en.name: Piccola Cuba
description:
The so-called Piccola Cuba (“Small Cuba”), built in the second half of the 12th century, during the reign of Guglielmo II, today forms part of the remaining citrus plantation of Villa Napoli, where the Norman construction, called Torre Alfaina, is also included.  
The pavilion is cubic shaped and is open on four sides by ogival arcades with triple lintels, of which the median is formed by a sequence of bossed ashlars, a decorative element also used, in Palermo, in the campanile of the Church of Santa Maria dell’Ammiraglio, the Church of Santo Spirito and the Church of the Magione (Di Stefano, 1955). It is covered with a raised hemispheric cupola resting on angular niches with arches *a rincasso*. The building faces towards the east of the Torre Alfaina (also known as Cuba Soprana), almost on an axis with it, at about 200 m. distant, and it is supposed that it would have formed part of the dam of Cuba (Valenti, 1936). In 1556, the historian Tommaso Fazello suggested it be used as a resting-place from hunting, also on account of the existence of a discontinued series of such pavilions, almost a link between Cuba Soprana and the big Cuba.

es.name: Pequeña Cuba
description:
La llamada Pequeña Cuba (Piccola Cuba), erigida en la segunda mitad del siglo XII, durante el reinado de Guglielmo II, se encuentra hoy en el huerto de cítricos de la desaparecida Villa Napoli, en la que se hallaba englobada la construcción normanda denominada “Torre Alfaina”.  
El pabellón tiene forma cúbica y está abierto en sus cuatro lados por arcos triples ojivales, de los cuales el central está formado por una serie de sillares almohadillados, elemento decorativo utilizado en Palermo también en el campanario de las iglesias de Santa María del Almirante, Santo Espíritu y La Magione (Di Stefano, 1955). Está cubierto por una cúpula hemisférica peraltada que se apoya sobre hornacinas angulares de arcos escalonados. La fábrica, que ha dado lugar a la hipótesis de que perteneciera al dique de la Cuba (Valenti, 1932), está orientada hacia la pared este de la Torre Alfaina (llamada también Cuba Soberana), de la que dista, en eje con ella, unos 200 m. En 1556, el historiador Tommaso Fazello sugirió su uso como lugar de descanso de la fatiga de las cacerías, entre otras cosas por la existencia de una serie discontinua de tales pabellones que casi formaban una unión entre la Cuba Soberana y la gran Cuba.

en.name: *Trip to Egypt*
short_description: Travelling abroad, particularly to Eastern countries, became a must after Napoleon’s campaigns. This photograph, taken by Prince D. Luis Filipe and handwritten by Queen D. Amélia, features the Queen’s journey to Egypt to develop the princes’ cultural and educational skills.
keywords: Photograph; trip to Egypt; Cultural education

ar.name: قميص طلاسم (تعاويذ).
description:
صدر القميص مفتوح حتى مستوى البطن، وله ياقة مدورة؛ وقسمه الأمامي مزدان بكامله بآيات قرآنية وابتهالات وصيغ سحرية وتعاويذ رقمية. أما القسم الخلفي فعليه رسوم لأزهار طبيعية نُفذت بأصباغ ملونة.  
  
إن معظم الكتابات الموجودة على قمصان الطلاسم تتألف من أجزاء وآيات من القرآن، إضافة إلى أسماء الله الحسنى، وأسماء كثير من الأنبياء، وأسماء الملائكة الأربعة، واسم خاتم الأنبياء محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقصائد تمجِّده وأحياناً سيرته. وفي بعض الأحيان تورد أسماء فاطمة وابنيها الحسن والحسين والخلفاء الراشدين الأربعة ورموز البروج. وهكذا فإن معظم قمصان الطلاسم تحتوي على تعابير سحرية وتعاويذ في علم الأرقام مؤلفة من أحرف وأرقام يُعتقد أن لها طاقات ومعانٍ سحرية. يوجد في المتحف قمصان طلاسم عديدة تعود لأضرحة مختلفة.

الآيات القرآنية، التي هي كلام الله، لم تكن تُرتَّل للصلاة وحسب، بل وكانت تُعدُّ رموزاً طلسمية، ذات قوة سحرية. أحياناً كانت تُحمل بوصفها قلادة تعويذية، وأحياناً أخرى كانت تُكتب على ملابس كاملة، معروفة باسم "قمصان طلسمية".
dates: نهاية القرن 8- أوائل القرن 9 / نهاية القرن 14 - أوائل القرن 15.
keywords: السلطان بايزيد الأول؛ طلسم؛ قميص.

en.name: Talismanic shirt.
description:
The front of the shirt has a round collar and is open down to the level of the abdomen. The entire surface of the shirt is decorated with Qur'anic verses, prayers, magic formulas and numerological charms. The back part of the shirt features a design of naturalistic flowers executed in coloured pigments.  
  
The inscriptions on talismanic shirts consist mostly of chapters and verses of the Qur'an. In addition to these, the names and epithets of God (the *Asma al-Husna*), the names of various prophets and the four major angels, the seal of the Prophet Muhammad and poems praising him, and occasionally the *hilya* (Description of the Prophet) are written. Sometimes the names of Fatima, her sons Hasan and Husayn, the first four caliphs and the signs of the zodiac are encountered. Almost all talismanic shirts have magic formulas and numerological charms made up of letters and numbers, which are thought to have magical powers and meanings. The Museum has many talismanic shirts from different tombs.

The Qur'anic verses, which are the words of God, were not only read for prayer but were also perceived as talismanic symbols. Sometimes they were carried as an amulet necklace and sometimes they covered entire costumes known as 'talismanic shirts'.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
dates: Hegira, end of the 8th–beginning of the 9th / AD end of the 14th–beginning of the 15th century.
keywords: Shirt; Sultan Bayezid I; talisman; calligraphy; costume; amulet
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Camisa talismán.
description:
La camisa de cuello redondo, abierto hasta la altura del abdomen. Toda la prenda está decorada con versículos coránicos, oraciones, frases mágicas y amuletos numerológicos. La parte posterior presenta un diseño de flores naturalistas pintadas con pigmentos de colores.  
Las camisas talismán suelen llevar inscripciones de suras y aleyas del Corán. Además, llevan escritos los nombres y epítetos de Dios (el *Asma al-Husna*), los nombres de diversos profetas y de los cuatro ángeles principales, la rúbrica del profeta Muhammad y poemas de alabanza a él y, en ocasiones, una *hilya* o historia de la vida del Profeta. Algunas veces se encuentran también los nombres de Fátima y sus hijos (Hasan y Husayn), el de los cuatro primeros califas y los signos del zodiaco. Casi todas estas camisas protectoras presentan frases mágicas y amuletos numerológicos a los que se atribuyen significados y poderes mágicos. El museo posee numerosas camisas talismán procedentes de diversas tumbas.

Los versículos coránicos, que son palabras de Dios, no sólo se leían durante la oración, sino que también se consideraban talismanes. A veces se llevaban como amuletos en collares y otras veces cubrían prendas enteras conocidas como “camisas talismán”.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
dates: Finales del siglo VIII–principios del IX de la Hégira / XIV–XV d. C.
keywords: Camisa; sultán Bayezid I; talismán.
partner: Museo de Artes Turcas e Islámicas

fr.name: Chemise talismanique.
description:
Chemise à col rond s'ouvrant jusqu'à l'abdomen. La totalité de la surface est décorée de versets du Coran, de prières, de formules magiques et de porte-bonheur numérologiques. Le dos est orné d'une composition de fleurs naturalistes, exécutée au pigment de couleur.  
Les inscriptions sur les chemises talismaniques consistaient essentiellement en chapitres et versets du Coran. Y figuraient également les noms et les qualificatifs de dieu (le *Asma al-Husna*), les noms de divers prophètes et des quatre anges principaux, le sceau du prophète Mahomet, des poèmes à sa louange et parfois la *hilya* (noble description du prophète). On peut aussi y rencontrer le nom de Fatima, de ses fils Hassan et Hussein, ceux des quatre premiers califes et les signes du zodiaque. Presque toutes les chemises de ce type comportent des formules magiques et des porte-bonheur numérologiques composés de lettres et de nombres censés posséder des pouvoirs et des significations magiques. Le musée possède de nombreuses chemises talismaniques provenant de divers tombeaux.

Les versets du Coran, qui sont les paroles de Dieu, étaient non seulement lus pour la prière mais également perçus comme symboles talismaniques. Ils étaient parfois portés en collier à titre d’amulettes, et quelquefois ils recouvraient entièrement des vêtements connus sous le nom de “chemises talismaniques”.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
dates: Fin du VIIIe siècle-début du IXe siècle de l’Hégire / XIVe-XVe siècle J.-C.
keywords: talisman ; chemise ; sultan Bayézid Ier
partner: Musée des arts turques et islamiques

tr.name: Tılsımlı Gömlek.
description:
Yuvarlak yakalı olan gömleğin önü göbek hizasına kadar açıktır. Gömleğin tüm yüzeyi Kur'an ayetleri, dualar, vefk ve cifrlerle bezelidir. Gömleğin ense-sırt kısmına gelen bölümünde renkli boya ile yapılmış natüralist çiçeklerden oluşan bir süsleme bulunmaktadır.  
  
Tılsımlı gömleklerin üzerine en çok Kur'an sure ve ayetleri yazılmıştır. Bunların yanı sıra Allah'ın güzel ad ve sıfatları (Esma-ül Hüsna), bazı peygamberlerin adları, dört büyük meleğin adları, Hz. Muhammed'in mührü ve onu yücelten şiirler, bazen de Hilye-i Resul yazılır. Gömleklerin üzerinde bazen Hz. Fatma'nın, oğulları Hasan ve Hüseyin'in, dört halifenin isimlerine ve burçların adlarına rastlanmaktadır. Tılsımlı gömleklerin hemen hepsinde sihirli güç ve anlamları olduğuna inanılan sayı ve harflerden oluşan vefk ve cifrler bulunmaktadır. Müze koleksiyonunda çeşitli türbelerden gelen birçok tılsımlı gömlek bulunmaktadır.

Tanrının buyruğu olan Kur'an ayetleri, ibadet amacıyla okunmasının yanı sıra koruyucu güç sembolü olarak da algılanmıştır. Bazen bir muska küçüklüğünde boyunlarda taşınmış, bazen bir giysinin tüm yüzeyini kaplamış ve ''Tılsımlı Gömlek'' olarak adlandırılmıştır.
dates: H. 8. / M. 14. yüzyılın sonu – H. 9. / M. 15. yüzyılın başı.
keywords: Tılsım; Gömlek; I. Bayezid

en.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
short_description: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.
keywords: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha; Egypt; Arabi (Urabi) revolution; Great Britain

en.name: Ruins of al-Ablaq Palace
description:
Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun was to commission his palace, called al-Ablaq Palace on the west side of the southern enclosure of the Citadel of Salah al-Din in 713/1313. On the basis of archaeological finds in the area, the palace is believed to have stretched from the outer wall of the Citadel to the entrance hall of al-Gawhara Palace. The palace was reserved for the Sultan to hold his daily audiences and above all, for the administration of State affairs, though special occasions were also celebrated there. Its name derives from the building technique known as *al-ablaq*, consisting of alternating courses of black-and-white stone (the white stone over time has yellowed).  
From archaeological finds we know that the floor plan comprised two *iwans* and a *durqa‘a*. This layout closely follows that of other palaces of the period such as the Alin Aq al-Husami and Bashtak Palaces (see Itinerary II). On evidence from other similar structures we can assume this palace had two *iwans* and a *durqa‘a*, its centre covered by a dome. From the northern *iwan*, larger than the southern *iwan*, the Sultan could look out over the imperial stables, the horse bazaar (*al-Khuyul*) in the Citadel Square and over the city of Cairo, and from the River Nile to Giza. Access to the remaining palace rooms and to the complex of buildings, such as the great *iwan* and the al-Guwaniyya Palaces, was gained through the southern *iwan*, built by al-Nasir Muhammad in the Citadel. The palace was subsequently abandoned. It was later turned into the *Kiswa* factory for the *Ka‘ba* in Ottoman times, and finally Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha (1220/1805-1265/1849 was to have his mosque built over the hypostyle hall of the palace. Alterations have left the building stripped of its original wealth and magnificence. Nevertheless, the works of the *Khitat* written by the historian al-Maqrizi bear testimony to its decorative features. He mentions floors and walls covered with marble and ceilings of gold and lapislazuli. On the lower part of one of the *durqa‘a* walls there are still vestiges of marble, and on the upper part of the same section a piece of gilt marble mosaic can be seen indicating that a panel of the same material once covered the entire wall. The mosaic contains floral and geometric designs very similar to those panels still visible today in the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus.

es.name: Ruinas del palacio al-Ablaq
description:
En el año 713/1313 el sultán al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun construyó su palacio, llamado al-Ablaq, en el lado oeste de la zona sur de la Ciudadela de Salah al-Din. Es probable que se extendiese desde el muro exterior de la Ciudadela hasta el recibidor del palacio al-Gawhara, ya que se encontraron en esta zona vestigios del mismo. El palacio estaba reservado a las recepciones diarias del sultán y, en particular, a la administración de los asuntos del país; también se celebraban en él las festividades especiales. En cuanto a su nombre, hace referencia a la técnica de construcción conocida como sistema *ablaq*, que consiste en la alternancia de hileras de piedras negras y blancas, color que con el tiempo se ha convertido en amarillo.  
A partir de los descubrimientos arqueológicos se ha podido conocer la organización de su planta, compuesta de dos *iwan*s y una *durqa‘a*, según la disposición de los palacios de la época, como el de Alin Aq al-Husami y el de Bachtak (Recorrido II). Esto permite afirmar que el palacio constaba, pues, de dos *iwan*s, y entre ellos se hallaba una *durqa‘a*, cubierta en su centro por una cúpula. Desde el *iwan* septentrional, mayor que el meridional, el sultán podía asomarse a los establos imperiales, al zoco de los caballos (*al-Juyul*) en la plaza de la Ciudadela y a la ciudad de El Cairo, y ver desde el Nilo hasta El Giza. A través del *iwan* meridional se accede al resto de las dependencias del palacio y al conjunto de edificios construidos por al-Nasir Muhammad en la Ciudadela, como el gran *iwan* y los palacios al-Guwaniyya. A pesar de que la apariencia de riqueza y suntuosidad del palacio ha desaparecido a causa del abandono —ya que fue transformado en la fábrica de la *kiswa* de la Ka‘ba en la época otomana, y que Muhammad Alí Pacha (1220/1805- 1265/1849) construyó su mezquita sobre la parte del palacio que ocupaba la sala de las columnas—, podemos conocer algunas características de la decoración a través de las *Jitat* del historiador al-Maqrizi, donde menciona que los suelos y las paredes estaban revestidos de mármol, y los techos de oro y lapislázuli. En la parte inferior de una de las paredes de la *durqa‘a* todavía se conservan fragmentos del revestimiento de mármol, y en la parte superior de la misma, un trozo de mosaico de mármol dorado indica que un panel completo cubría toda la pared. Este mosaico contiene elementos florales y geométricos muy similares a los paneles existentes en la mezquita omeya de Damasco.

fr.name: Ruines du palais al-Ablaq
description:
En 713/1313, le sultan al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun construisit son palais, appelé al-Ablaq, sur le côté ouest de la zone sud de la Citadelle de Salah al-Din. On peut supposer qu’il s’étendait du mur extérieur de la Citadelle jusqu’au vestibule du palais al-Gawhara, puisque cette zone a livré des vestiges appartenant au même palais. Celui-ci était réservé aux réceptions quotidiennes du sultan et, plus particulièrement, à la gestion des affaires du pays; il s’y tenait aussi des cérémonies spéciales. Quant à son nom, il fait référence à la technique de construction dite système *ablaq*, qui consiste à alterner des lits de pierres noires et blanches, couleur qui est devenue jaune au fil du temps.  
La mise au jour des vestiges archéologiques a permis de révéler l’organisation du plan, composé de deux *iwan*s et d’une *durqa‘a*, conformément à la disposition des palais de l’époque, tels ceux de Alin Aq al-Husami et de Bachtak (Circuit II). On peut donc établir que le palais comptait deux *iwan*s, entre lesquels se trouvait une *durqa‘a*, couverte au centre par une coupole. Depuis l’*iwan* septentrional, plus grand que l’*iwan* méridional, le sultan pouvait voir ses écuries impériales, le souk des chevaux (*al-Khuyul*) sur la place de la Citadelle et la ville du Caire, puis tout le panorama depuis le Nil jusqu’à Gizeh. Par l’*iwan* méridional, on accède aux autres dépendances du palais et à l’ensemble des édifices construits par al-Nasir Muhammad dans la Citadelle, tels le grand *iwan* et les palais al-Guwaniyya. Bien que le palais ait perdu de son apparence de richesse et de somptuosité pour cause d’abandon – l’époque ottomane le transforma en atelier réservé à la confection de la *kiswa* de la *Ka‘ba*, et Muhammad Ali Pacha (1220/ 1805-1265/1849) éleva sa mosquée sur la partie du palais qui était occupée par la salle des colonnes –, nous sommes tout de même documentés sur quelques caractéristiques de la décoration grâce aux *Khitat* de l’historien al-Maqrizi, dans lesquels il précise que les sols et les murs étaient dallés de marbre, tandis que les toits étaient revêtus d’or et de lapis-lazuli. La partie inférieure de l’une des parois de la *durqa‘a* conserve encore quelques fragments du revêtement de marbre; sur la partie supérieure de la même paroi, des vestiges de mosaïque de marbre doré indiquent que c’est bien un panneau complet qui recouvrait tout le mur. Cette mosaïque présente des éléments floraux et géométriques très proches des panneaux que l’on peut voir dans la mosquée omeyyade de Damas.

en.name: Summer carpet
description:
Wool carpets had little fashion in India during the heat of summer and damp of the monsoon season. Wool may smell or feel sodden underfoot in humid environments and a heavy pile may be unwanted in hot climates. At such times, summer carpets were preferred for furnishing domestic spaces. Usually made of cotton and silk threads, they varied in size and elaborateness depending on the means of the patron.  
This summer carpet features very fine, chain-stitched flora and fauna motifs in shades of pink, green and yellow floss silk on a pale pink cotton ground. A lobed rosette medallion at centre is repeated in quadrants at each corner. The arrangement calls to mind the layout of medallion carpets. Interspersed among the larger floral motifs are smaller floral motifs of great variety, size, and form. Secreted among the floral motifs are small animals such as rabbits, deer, and birds. They are repeated in the wide border.  
Much of the carpet’s charm derives from the embroiderers’ minute attention to detail. An intriguing variety of flowers, primarily sewn in pink threads, is offset by yellow threads differentiating petals and parts of the flowers. Green threads become leaves and stems which weave around the blossoms and form the medallions’ lobed borders. There is interest in naturalism, but it is offset by idealism. Every petal is in full bloom, a defiance of nature’s limitations. The carpet offers to the viewer’s imagination the most beautiful summer garden with prancing animals delighting in a display more perfect than nature.  
The textile is characteristic of Mochi embroidery of the 18th century from the Kutch region of Gujarat, India. Many beautiful examples are known to have been made during this period. A large one such as this may have been made at an urban or court workshop in the region. An inscription embroidered inside one border is now too degraded to read. To preserve the fragile carpet, netting has been gently tacked to the textile.
holder: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art
keywords: Floor spread; animal decoration; floral decoration; collector; cotton
partner: Shangri La, Doris Duke Foundation for Islamic Art

en.name: Tesla Roadster
description: An electric sports car developed by Tesla Motors and based on the Lotus Elise, the Tesla Roadster is the first electric car to use lithium-ion battery packs. Under the banner of his SpaceX project, Elon Musk scored a lot of publicity when he launched a Tesla Roadster into space in 2018 as ballast for a Falcon Heavy rocket demonstration.
keywords: Electric; carbon fiber; high performance; lithium battery

en.name: A Khorsabad barrel
short_description: During the archaeological mission led in Khorsabad by French consul Victor Place (1851–1854), fourteen Assyrian barrels were discovered. However, only four were preserved, since most of Place’s findings were lost in a shipwreck that took place in April 1855 on the Shatt el-Arab. As a reward for his archeological activity, the French government offered Place one of the barrels. Between 1855-1863 he was a consul in Moldavia, where he settled and started a family. In 1987 the Romanian state bought the barrel from one of Place’s descendants after the authorities found out that he was trying to sell it abroad. The barrel is made of clay, is nine-sided and bears an inscription recounting the reign of Assyrian king Sargon II, founder of a new capital, Dur-Sharrukin (Khorsabad).
dates: 721–705 BC (reign of Sargon II); discovered in 1851–1854

en.name: Gold medal awarded to l'École Emile-Loubet
short_description: This certificate for a gold medal was awarded to the vocational college l'École Emile-Loubet in Tunis at the Paris International Trade Fair in 1900 for the training it provided particularly in carpentry, metalwork and book binding. The school was founded in 1898 by 'Ali Bey for teaching the basics of manual occupations. The bey, accompanied by the French President, placed the first stone of its new building in 1900, which then became the Lycée Technique Emile-Loubet.

fr.name: Médaille d’or décernée à l’école Emile-Loubet

Cette école professionnelle a été fondée en 1898 par Ali Bey pour enseigner les principaux métiers manuels. Le bey, accompagné par le président français Emile Loubet, avait posé la première pierre du nouveau bâtiment consacré en 1900 au lycée technique Emile-Loubet.

ar.name: إبريق.
description:
إبريق كبير مصنوع من صفائح النحاس الأصفر المطرقة والمطعمة بالفضة، له فتحة متسعة، وجسم مستدير، وقاعدة عريضة، بالإضافة إلى عروة تربط بين العنق والجسم، أما المصب فهو طويل ورفيع وله فتحة متعددة الأضلاع، وهناك عنصر بصلي مرتبط بالعنق ربما أضيف لاحقاً. عدا عن الحلقة البارزة ذات التصميم الثلاثي الفصوص حول أسفل العنق، تتألف الزخرفة بشكل عام من النقوش والفضة المطعمة، وفي حين تم تزيين العروة والمصب بأرابيسك بسيط إلا أن أغلب العنق والجسم مزين بمشاهد صغيرة مميزة تظهر فيها الحيوانات الحقيقية والخرافية كالسباع والأيائل والأرانب والطيور وحتى الأفيال بين أشجار النخيل والنباتات شديدة الزخرفة. يذكر النقش الكبير حول الجزء العلوي من الجسم أن الإبريق قد صنع لصالح زوجة السلطان قايتباي التي كان اسمها فاطمة. وعلى عكس باقي الزخارف، لم يتم تطعيم النقش بالفضة بل تم ترك الأحرف ملساء ومصقولة، وملء الفراغات بين الأحرف بأرابيسك كثيف بسيط مما يعطي أرضية متباينة. ويوجد نقش آخر موجود أسفل القاعدة يذكر أن الإبريق صنعه حرفي اسمه أحمد.  
تتباين الزخارف التصويرية على الإبريق بشكل رائع مع نوع الزخرفة التي تظهر عادة على القطع المصنوعة خلال حكم قايتباي المتدين، والتي تحمل عادة زخرفة كتابية بارزة أو زخارف مجردة دون أية زخارف تصويرية من تلك التي كانت مكروهة حسب مذهبه. وتشمل الأمثلة حوض النحاس الأصفر المصنوع للسلطان (UK2 13) والمنبر الذي تم ذكر اسمه عليه (UK2 10). تدل المشاهد التصويرية على إبريق فاطمة حتماً على أنه نفذ بناء على طلب خاص للاستعمال الشخصي، وتعكس مشاهد الحيوانات بين الأشجار الصور التي تذكرها الأشعار العربية، وقد يكون المقصود منها إيجاد الرابط الديني مع الجنة.

ابريق من النحاس، مُزخرف، ومُطعَّم بالفضة، بأشكال وتصاميم لحيوانات خرافية، وأشجار، ونباتات. يوضح النقش الموجود عليه، بأنه كان قد صنع خصيصاً لزوجة السلطان قايتباي، ويُستدلُّ من الزخارف والتصاميم، بأنه كان لاستخداماتها الخاصة.
keywords: زخرفة تصويرية؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ ماء؛ حيوان وهمية
materials: نحاس أصفر مطعم بالفضة وربما بالنحاس الأحمر.
tags: نحاس أصفر مطعم بالفضة وربما بالنحاس الأحمر.

en.name: Ewer.
description:
A large ewer, made of hammered sheet brass inlaid with silver, with a flaring mouth, rounded body, and spreading foot; a curved handle is joined to the neck and body, and the spout is long and thin with a polygonal end. A bulbous element, which may be a later addition, is attached to the neck. Other than the ring of raised (*repoussé*) trefoil motifs around the base of the neck, the decoration consists mostly of engraving and inlaid silver. While the handle and spout are adorned with simple arabesques, most of the neck and body of the ewer are given over to remarkable little scenes in which real and fantastic animals – including lions, deer, rabbits, birds, and even elephants – are depicted amidst palm trees and luxuriant plants. A large inscription around the top section of the body says that the ewer was made for the wife of Sultan Qaytbay, whose name, we know, was Fatima. Unlike the rest of the decoration, the inscription is not inlaid with silver; rather, the letters are left plain and polished, and the spaces between the letters are filled with simple, if tightly coiled, arabesques which provide a contrasting background. A second inscription, found on the underside of the foot, records that the ewer was made by someone named Ahmad.  
The figural decoration on the ewer provides a fascinating contrast with the kind of decoration normally found on objects made during the reign of the pious Qaytbay, which tend to have bold calligraphy and/or abstract decoration, but no figural representation in keeping with the strictures of the orthodox. Examples include the brass basin made for the Sultan (UK2 13) or the *minbar* with his name on it (UK2 10). The figural imagery on Fatima's ewer surely indicates that it was a private commission, meant for her personal use. The scenes of animals amidst trees reflect imagery found in contemporary Arabic poetry and may be meant to evoke religious associations with the verdancy of Paradise.

A large brass ewer with decoration in inlaid silver. The decoration includes real and imaginary animals amidst trees and plants. The inscription states that the ewer was made for the wife of Sultan Qaytbay, and the presence of figural decoration suggests that it was for her private use.
keywords: figurative decoration; floral decoration; water; imaginary animal; zoomorphic imagery
materials: Brass inlaid with silver and possibly copper.
tags: Brass inlaid with silver and possibly copper.

es.name: Aguamanil
description:
Aguamanil hecho con láminas de bronce batido, con incrustaciones de plata. Tiene boca abocinada, cuerpo redondeado, pie acampanado, asa curva que va del cuello al cuerpo y un largo pitorro de sección poligonal. Probablemente, el elemento bulboso del cuello es un añadido posterior. Se ha decorado mediante grabado e incrustaciones de plata, salvo un anillo de tréboles repujados en los hombros. El asa y el pitorro están adornados con sencillos arabescos, mientras que en la mayor parte del cuello y el cuerpo se han representado pequeñas y cuidadas escenas de animales reales y fantásticos –leones, ciervos, conejos, aves e incluso elefantes– entre palmeras y plantas exuberantes. Rodea la parte superior del cuerpo una gran inscripción que indica que el aguamanil se hizo para la esposa del sultán Qaytbay, de la que sabemos que se llamaba Fátima. Esta inscripción, a diferencia del resto del aguamanil, no tiene incrustaciones de plata; las letras se dejaron lisas y pulidas, y contrastan con el fondo, rellenado con apretados arabescos. Una segunda inscripción, en la superficie de apoyo del pie, informa del nombre del artesano, Ahmad.  
La decoración figurativa de este aguamanil que data del sultanato del piadoso Qaytbay contrasta con la que suele encontrarse en los objetos de la época, en la que predominaban, siguiendo las restricciones ortodoxas, los motivos caligráficos o abstractos. Ejemplos similares son el cuenco de bronce hecho para el sultán (UK2 13) o el *minbar* con su nombre (UK2 10). La presencia de figuración en el aguamanil de Fátima hace pensar que se trataba de un encargo para su uso personal. Las escenas de animales entre árboles se corresponden con las imágenes de la poesía árabe de la época y su intención era evocar asociaciones religiosas con la vegetación del paraíso.

Aguamanil con incrustaciones de plata, decorado con animales reales e imaginarios entre árboles y otras plantas. Según la inscripción, se hizo para la esposa del sultán Qaytbay. La presencia de decoración figurativa indica que era para su uso privado.
keywords: decoración figurativa; decoración floral; agua; animal imaginario
materials: Bronce batido con incrustaciones de plata y posiblemente de cobre.
tags: Bronce batido con incrustaciones de plata y posiblemente de cobre.

fr.name: Aiguière.
description:
Grande aiguière à ouverture évasée, panse arrondie et pied écarté, faite d'une feuille de cuivre martelé incrusté d'argent. Une poignée incurvée relie le col et le corps. Le bec long et fin se termine par un verseur polygonal. Addition peut-être tardive, un élément bulbiforme est fixé à son col. En dehors du cercle de motifs repoussés en forme de trèfle à la base de celui-ci, le décor se compose essentiellement de gravure et d'argent incrusté. Si la poignée et le bec sont ornés de simples arabesques, la plus grande partie du col et de la panse est recouverte de remarquables petites scènes d'animaux vrais ou fabuleux – lions, cerf, lapins, oiseaux et même éléphants – parmi des palmiers et des plantes luxuriantes. Une grande inscription autour de la partie supérieure du corps précise que cette aiguière a été fabriquée pour l'épouse du sultan Qaytbay, dont on sait qu'elle s'appelait Fatima. À la différence du reste du décor, l'inscription n'est pas incrustée d'argent : les lettres sont pleines et polies et les espaces de l'interlettrage sont ornés d'arabesques simples, mais étroitement enlacées, qui forment un fond contrastant. Une seconde inscription, trouvée sous le pied, précise que l'objet a été réalisé par un certain Ahmad.  
Ce décor figuratif offre un contraste fascinant avec le type de décoration généralement trouvée sur les objets exécutés sous le règne du pieux Qaytbay, qui tendent plutôt à adopter un décor calligraphique et/ou abstrait, mais non figuratif, en accord avec les règles de l'orthodoxie religieuse. Parmi d'autres exemples, on peut citer le bassin de cuivre réalisé pour ce sultan ou le *minbar* sur lequel figure son nom. L'imagerie figurative de cette aiguière prouve certainement qu'il s'agissait d'une commande privée à usage personnel. Les scènes d'animaux parmi les arbres reflètent des thèmes de la poésie arabe de l'époque et peuvent évoquer des associations religieuses avec le jardin du Paradis.

Grande aiguière de cuivre jaune à décoration incrustée en argent figurant des animaux réels ou fabuleux parmi des arbres et des plantes. L'inscription indique que l'aiguière a été faite pour la femme du sultan Qaytbay, et la présence d'une décoration figurative suggère que le récipient était destiné à un usage privé.
keywords: Décoration figurative ; décoration florale ; eau ; animal imaginaire
materials: Cuivre jaune incrusté d’argent et peut-être de cuivre.
tags: Cuivre jaune incrusté d’argent et peut-être de cuivre.

en.name: Glass Model
description: In 1863, the Bohemian-based glassmaker Leopold Blaschka started making models of sea invertebrates at the instigation of an admirer of his glass botanicals. These initial models were based on the illustrations of Philip Henry Gosse published in his treaty ‘A History of the British Sea-Anemones and Corals’, later observations were taken from live specimens shipped directly to the studio and kept in aquariums on site. Around 1880, Rudolf began to assist his father, and over the years they produced models of anemones, cephalopods, mollusca, nudibranchs, and protozoans as well as the vast collection of botanicals held by Harvard University. In 1866, the Edinburgh Museum of Science and Art was one of the first UK institutions to order invertebrate models from Leopold Blaschka after its Director Thomas Archer had viewed the then Natural History section of the British Museum’s collection. A set of actinia arrived in 1866, followed by a batch of 58 medusae and mollusks in 1868. In 1910, Ewen Kennedy, a private collector, donated his collection of 123 Blaschka models. The Blaschka models are now highly regarded for their beauty and realism and are still considered ‘an artistic marvel in the field of science and a scientific marvel in the field of art’.
artist: Leopold Blaschka (1822, Český Dub, Bohemia - 1895, Dresden); Rudolph Blaschka (1857, Dresden, Saxony - 1939, Dresden)
keywords: Blaschka; lampworked glass; glass models

en.name: A copy of the Tower of Galata made for the Genoa Exhibition, 1914
names: *Genova. Esposizione Marina e Igiene Marinara. La Torre di Galata*
short_description: "International Exhibition of Marina and Igiene Marinara. Italian colonial exhibition", organised in Genoa in 1914 and curated by the architect Gino Coppede. ar.name: جزئين من مصحف ذو 30 جزءا
description: يتألف النص من سورة البقرة وهي السورة الثانية في القرآن  وذلك للآيات 142-252. وكامل الافتتاحية ( الصفحتين1b–2a) والخاتمة (الصفحتين 97b–98a) مذهبة بالكامل. والتصاميم المختلفة من الممكن أنها مستوحاة من فسيفساء قديمة جدا وما تزال معمول بها في القرن الثامن في سوريا الأموية وحتى لفترة أطول في العصر البيزنطي.يراعي بلوك النص تناسبات القسم الذهبي وهو ½(1+√5) والذي اكتشف من قبل الفيثاغورثيين ويتبع مبدأ اللولب /الحلزون متساوي الزوايا والأشكال الهندسية الأساسية الأخرى. والرياضيون المسلمون والحرفيون كانوا عارفين جيدا للمبدأ بالرغم من أنه كان هناك حالات قليلة تظهر أنه كان يعتبر كمثالية للجمال في الفن الإسلامي. وقد تم استخدامه في مصاحف أخرى وبشكل خاص في مخطوطة رائعة (موجودة الآن في المكتبة الوطنية في باريس) التي أمر بكتابتها أماجور وهو حاكم دمشق لصالح المسجد الجامع في صور، لبنان في عام 262 هجري (875-6 ميلادي).

en.name: Part Two of a 30-part Qur’an
description:
The text consists of *sura* *al-Baqara* (II), verses 142–252. The opening (folios 1b–2a) and closing spreads (folios 97b–98a) are fully illuminated. The different designs are possibly inspired by Late Antique mosaics, still fashionable in 8th-century Umayyad Syria and even longer in Byzantium.  
The text block observes the proportions of the Golden Section, ½(1+√5), which was discovered by the Pythagoreans and follows the principle of the equiangular spiral and other basic geometrical figures. Islamic mathematicians and craftsmen were well acquainted with the principle, although there are few cases to demonstrate that it was regarded as an ideal of beauty in Islamic art. It has been used in other early Qur’ans, notably a fine manuscript (now in the Bibliothèque Nationale in Paris) commissioned by Amajur, the governor of Damascus, for the Great Mosque of Tyre, Lebanon, in AH 262 (AD 875–6).

en.name: Edward Dodwell, *View in Greece* (London 1830)
short_description: Edward Dodwell recorded the trasformation of the ancient Tower of the Winds into a dervish teke and in the early 19th century it wqas particularly popular with the travellers. Scenes from the city of Athens. Over the lintel, which faces the north-east, upon a red ground, is inscribed the Arabic *La Illah, Allah, Mahamed u resoul ullah* declaring there to be no God but God, and Muhammad to be his prophet. The wooden floor of the interior rests upon the lower cornice, many feet above the ancient pavement. The marble walls are washed with a uniform white. The *mihrab*, painted in perpendicular stripes of green and red, indicates by its position the direction of the Kaaba, or oratory of Mecca; each side of this is a wax candle, and the green flag of the prophet has also its place. The Qur'an is deposited within this niche, and an imitation of the two-edged sword of 'Ali is attached to the adjoining wall. Before these is performed the circularly whirling dance of the Dervishes, witnessing which, the spectator will find it as difficult to remain serious, as it would be dangerous to appear otherwise.
keywords: travels; Dodwell; Athens

en.name: *Bindallı entari*
short_description: The attire of Ottoman women included dresses for the outdoors and the indoors. Starting from early 19th century, dresses called *üçetek* (dress with three skirts) and *dörtetek* (dress with four skirts) became fashionable. As relations with Europe increased, women in Istanbul started to use imported European textiles for their new dresses. This *entari* (dress) is made of purple velvet embroidered in the *bindallı* (dress that has embroidered flowers on the branches) style with garlands and flowers in vases in the *dival* (gold or silver embroidery on velvet) technique using silver-gilt thread. It has a short front opening, round neck and fitted sleeves. The skirt is widened by triangular gores and is longer at the back.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: fashion, traditional dress, textile
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

ar.name: صورة جانبية للسطان سليمان الثاني
description: هذه البورتريه للسلطان العثماني سليمان (1494/5- 1566) تنسب عموما لدائرة تيتيان وهذا بشكل أساسي بسبب النقش على ظهر اللوحة. ولا يوجد بورتريه أصلي لسليمان من قبل تيتيان الذي بقي حتى الآن ومن بينها يوجد اثنتان معروفتان بشكل مبدئي على أنهما بورترية جانبية. والمقارنة مع أنواع أخرى للبورتريه المسجلة تظهر أن تكوينها مرتبط بنوع أولي نشر من قبل باولو جيوفيو (1483-1552) ميلادي وبعد 1543 عندما  ضم عددا من النسخ لبورتريهات السلاطين لمجموعة البورتريهات لديه في كامو. وهذا العام يحدد التاريخ الممكن الأول لهذه اللوحة.
keywords: سليمان ، تيتيان ، باولو جيوفيو

de.name: *Sultan Süleyman II im Profil*
description: Die Zuweisung des osmanischen Herrscherporträts Sultan Süleyman (900–974 H. / geb. 1494/95 – 1566 n. Chr.) in den Umkreis Tizians resultiert u. a. aus der auf der Rückseite des Gemäldes befindlichen Bezeichnung. Von Tizian selbst ist keine Einzeldarstellung Süleymans im Original erhalten. Doch belegen Inventare vier Einzelbildnisse von der Hand des Malers, darunter zwei, hinter denen ein Profilbildnis vermutet wird. Der Vergleich mit überlieferten Bildnistypen Süleymans zeigt, dass die Entstehung mit dem seit AD 1543 von Paolo Giovio (AD 1483–1552) verbreiteten Typus in Verbindung zu bringen ist. Dieser hatte in jenem Jahr eine Serie von Sultansbildnissen für seine Porträtsammlung in Como kopieren lassen. Das Jahr stellt einen Terminus post quem für die Entstehung des vorliegenden Porträts dar.
keywords: Süleyman; Titian; Paolo Giovio

en.name: *Sultan Süleyman II in profile*
description: This portrait of the Ottoman Sultan Süleyman (AD 1494/5– 1566) is generally attributed to Titian’s circle, mainly because of the inscription on the back of the painting. No original portrait of Süleyman by Titian has survived, but inventories document four portraits by him, among them two tentatively identified as portraits in profile. Comparison with other recorded portrait-types of Süleyman shows that its genesis is connected with a prototype disseminated by Paolo Giovio (AD 1483–1552) after AD 1543, when he commissioned a number of copies of portraits of sultans for his portrait collection at Como. This year marks the *terminus post quem* for this painting.
keywords: Portrait; Süleyman; Ottoman; collection; Museum; Paolo Giovio; Titian; Italy; Renaissance; Ottoman-Venetian relations

en.name: Yıldız Palace State Apartments Kiosk
short_description: This is the most magnificent kiosk of the palace. It was commissioned by Sultan Abdulaziz in 1866 and built by the architects of Balyan family. The exterior siding of the kiosk is decorated with fluted and composite capitals, columns, corbel and sectional architraves. The inner plan of the kiosk is based on the old architectural tradition. It is famous with the Divanhane with pool downstairs and the stairs with the crystal handrails to the second floor. While the upper floor was used by the sultan, other sections were used by senior officials of the palace. Ghazi Osman Pasha, Commander of Plevne War served as Marshal of the Court in this building. Having served as the administration headquarters of the state during the reign of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909), the kiosk was used for important receptions and feasts both in the Ottoman Empire and after the Declaration of the Republic.
artist: Balyan family – Sarkis Balyan (1835, Istanbul – 1899, Istanbul)
history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
keywords: Photography; Istanbul; History of architecture

en.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

en.name: Madrasat al-Firdaws
description:
Madrasat al-Firdaws, built by the regent queen Dhayfa Khatun in 633/1235, is without doubt Syria’s most important Ayyubid religious building. Its size (43.5 m x 55 m), with 11 undulating domes and an exterior *iwan*, which once faced a garden, further contribute to its uniqueness. The entrance is on its eastern side through a *muqarnas* portal, shot through by a long inscriptional frieze that starts with Qur’anic descriptions of Paradise and continues with honorific titles to Dhayfa Khatun. Unfortunately, later encroachments have marred this entrance along with the other facades of this important building.  
The glory of this building is its pristine rectangular courtyard, which is surrounded by arched porticos on the east, south and west sides, and by a large *iwan* to the north. The porticos lead to three long chambers, each with three domes, the southern one of which serves as a mosque. This mosque contains a splendid marble *mihrab*, surmounted by a polychrome interlaced spandrel, which is the largest and finest of several examples from Aleppo. It should be noted that these interlaces  
were not superficial inlay work but rather deeply engaged stonework, whose visible surfaces have been manipulated into various geometric swirls. Perhaps because of its ingenuity and  
spectacular effect, this decorative feature was subsequently exported from Aleppo to Anatolia, Palestine and Egypt.  
The Madrasat al-Firdaws is a heavily inscribed Ayyubid building,  
with exterior and interior inscriptions that total more than 150 m in length. The religious inscriptions are some of the most outstanding in all Islamic architecture. Using prose, poetry and  
Qur’anic references, it vividly and passionately describes the actions and aspirations of the Sufis who worshipped at al-Firdaws. Their night vigil and ecstatic worship would be rewarded by  
entry to Paradise and by a vision of God we are told. Although called a *madrasa*, al-Firdaws was most likely a *khanqa* that, in its time, housed deep forms of Sufi practice, and  
hence the use of the word, *madrasat* to indicate that it was both a shrine and religious school.

en.name: Monument to the brothers Giovan Battista and Ippolito Fornasari
description: This double portrait depicts two brothers, both Law professors in the University of Bologna. It hangs over the door, on one side of the Bulgari chapel and dominates the great allegorical fresco representing Dawn and Sunset, Justice and Right, a typical expression of baroque complicated symbolism. It is a typical example of the variety of materials employed to build this sort of monument: pictorial decoration, plaster, metal and sandstone.
place: Palazzo of the Archiginnasio, ground floor
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Monumento ai fratelli Giovan Battista e Ippolito Fornasari
description:
Questa memoria è un tipico esempio della diversità di materiali impiegati per costruire questo tipo di monumenti (decorazione pittorica, gesso, metallo e arenaria).  
Il doppio ritratto dei fratelli, entrambi professori di Diritto è appeso sopra la porta a fianco della cappella dei Bulgari e domina il grande affresco allegorico rappresentante l'Aurora e il Tramonto, la Giustizia e il Diritto, tipica espressione del complesso simbolismo barocco.
