en.name: Yıldırım Complex
description:
In this complex built by Sultan Bayezid I there is a mosque, a *madrasa*, a *darüşşifa*, an *imaret*, a *hammam*, and a *türbe*; all the structures except the *imaret* have survived to the present day. The whole complex is called “Yıldırım” based on the epithet of Sultan Bayezid I who is also known as Sultan Yıldırım Bayezid. Yıldırım means lightning or thunderbolt in Turkish, suggesting that the sultan was able to move his armies “as quick as lightning” in order to crush his enemies. Hence the name and most of the edifices he had built are called Yıldırım Mosque, Yıldırım Complex, etc. This complex is located on a hill, some way away from the town centre and stands in a lovely park, set on terraces due to the slope. The *hammam* hidden among the houses is still in use.  
  
**Yıldırım Mosque**  
The mosque, the central building of the complex, is built with cut stone. The mosque’s present minaret is a later addition; the original minarets in the northeast and northwest corners collapsed at an unknown time. The five-bayed portico in the front is also built with cut stone and surmounted with domes. The two loggias above the outdoor *mihrab*s located on either side of the portal were to provide light for the staircase to the original minarets. Passing through the plain portal *iwan* topped with a tiny dome, one emerges into the inner court covered by a soaring dome and flanked with *iwan*s on both sides. These *iwan*s are also flanked on both sides with rooms covered with flattopped cross-vaults but only the ones to the south, also flanking the prayer hall, have furnishings of spectacular stucco fireplace and shelving enhanced with embedded tile pieces. The mosque was designed to respond to the needs of the *Ahi dervishe*s by providing them with meeting and boarding places; hence the rooms with the fireplace and shelving are the *tabhane*s. There is a monumental arch separating the inner court from the prayer hall; this is the first example of a “Bursa arch” with its top flat and recessed, another beautiful example of which can be seen in Yeşil Mosque. There is no record of construction, but it is believed that building must have taken place sometime between Bayezid I’s ascension to the throne in 1389 and the preparation of the *waqf* charter in 1399.  
  
**Yıldırım Madrasa**  
The *madrasa*, on a lower terrace to the northwest of the mosque, is today used as a health centre. The attractive walls built with alternating courses of stones and bricks are enhanced with the decoration in the tympana of the windows. The presence of a pair of small niches placed together on the side walls of the entrance to the *iwan*, rising higher than the rest of the structure, is a rarely seen characteristic and its dome is very attractive with its Turkish triangles. The dome covering the portico is very striking with its *muqarnas* decoration. There were latrines in the corner to the right of the entrance, but they were removed during recent repair work. Behind the vaulted porticos are student cells surrounding the courtyard on three sides, and the large *iwan* opposite the entrance fully protrudes and was used as a summer *dershane*. Strangely enough, there is not a winter *dershane* in this *madrasa* as there is in other *madrasa*s of this period; in such *madrasa*s, during the winter, either the front of the *iwan* was closed with wooden panes or classes were held in the complex’s mosque.  
  
**Darüşşifa**  
The *darüşşifa*, one of the most important buildings in the complex, has been restored in recent years. It is important for it is one of the few Ottoman *darüşşifa*s that have survived up to the present day. Built on a steep slope to the east of the mosque, the cells and porticoes on the side wings are graded with steps and the brickwork is noteworthy.  
  
**Türbe**  
The *türbe* in this complex belongs to Bayezid I, who was defeated and taken prisoner by Tamerlane at the Battle of Ankara (1402). Some historians say he committed suicide; others maintain that he fell ill and died in Akşehir in central Anatolia. After his death, he was buried in Akşehir in the *türbe* of Seyyid Mahmud Hayran, but later his body was handed over to his son Musa Çelebi and sent to Bursa at the order of Tamerlane. Because it was his will to be buried near the mosque he had built, his body was buried near the mosque in 1403-1404; in 1406, his son Emir Süleyman Çelebi had the present *türbe* constructed over his grave. During his siege of Bursa in 1413, Karamanid Bey Mehmed II took vengeance on his father’s murderer, Bayezid I, by removing his body from the grave and burning it.  
The *türbe* of Bayezid I is a simple square building surmounted by a dome and the three-bayed portico in front served as a model for later Ottoman türbes with porticoes.

es.name: Complejo Yıldırım
description:
Mezquita, *madrasa*, *darüşşifa*, *imaret*, *hammam* y *turbe* componían este complejo que debemos al sultán Bayezid I; todos estos edificios, salvo el *imaret*, han llegado a nuestros días. El complejo se llama Yıldırım por el sobrenombre del sultán, que en turco significa “rayo” o “trueno”, y se supone que el sultán era capaz de desplazar sus ejércitos “como un rayo” para aplastar a sus enemigos. La mayoría de las construcciones que levantó se llaman mezquita Yıldırım, complejo Yıldırım, etcétera. Este complejo está situado en un cerro algo apartado del centro de la ciudad y en medio de un encantador parque en terrazas, debido a la pendiente. El *hammam*, oculto entre las casas, sigue en funcionamiento.  
  
**Mezquita**  
La mezquita, edificio central del complejo, está construida en piedra. El actual alminar es un añadido posterior, pues los alminares primigenios de las esquinas noreste y noroeste se vinieron abajo en fecha desconocida. El pórtico frontal de cinco crujías es también de piedra y está coronado por cúpulas. Las dos logias que hay encima de los dos *mihrab*s del exterior, uno a cada lado del portal, servían para dar luz a las escaleras de los alminares originales. Pasando el sencillo *iwan* del portal, cubierto por una diminuta cúpula, se entra en el patio interior, techado con una cúpula alta y con *iwan*s a ambos lados. A su vez, los *iwan*s están rodeados por habitaciones cubiertas con bóvedas de crucería planas por arriba, pero solo las del sur, que flanquean la sala de oración, están acondicionadas con un espectacular hogar de estuco y estantes reforzados con azulejos incrustados. El plano del edificio se proyectó para responder a las necesidades de alojamiento y reunión de los *derviches ahi*, luego las habitaciones con hogar y estantes son *tabhanes*. Hay un arco monumental que separa el patio interior de la sala de oración; es el primer ejemplo de “arco de Bursa”, que tiene la parte superior plana y retranqueada, otro hermoso ejemplo del que vimos en la mezquita Yeşil.  
No hay ninguna fecha de construcción, pero se cree que debió de levantarse en algún momento entre la ascensión al trono de Bayezid I, 1389, y el acta fundacional del *waqf*, 1399.  
  
**Madrasa**  
La *madrasa*, en una terraza inferior al noreste de la mezquita, es ahora un centro de salud. Los atractivos muros con franjas alternadas de piedra y ladrillo están realzados con la decoración de los tímpanos de las ventanas. La existencia de un par de pequeños nichos juntos en las paredes laterales del *iwan* de entrada, más alto que el resto de la estructura, es una rara característica, y llama la atención también la cúpula con *triángulos turcos*. Realmente sorprendente es la decoración de *muqarnas* del interior de la cúpula del pórtico. Había unos servicios en la esquina derecha de la entrada, pero se quitaron en las últimas reformas. En el interior de la *madrasa* están las celdas abovedadas detrás de pórticos también con bóveda en tres de los lados del patio, y el gran *iwan* del lado opuesto a la entrada sobresale completamente; se usaba como *dershane* estival. Es bastante extraño que no haya un *dershane* invernal, como en otras *madrasa*s de la época; en ellas, en invierno se tapiaba el *iwan* con tablas de madera o se daban las clases en la mezquita del complejo.  
  
**Daruşşifa**  
El *daruşşifa*, uno de los edificios principales del complejo, ha sido restaurado en los últimos años. Su importancia reside en que es uno de los pocos *daruşşifa*s otomanos que han sobrevivido hasta hoy. Levantado en un terreno inclinado al este de la mezquita, las habitaciones y pórticos de las alas están en gradas con escalones. Resulta notable el trabajo de albañilería.  
  
**Turbe**  
Se trata del mausoleo de Bayezid I, que fue derrotado y hecho prisionero por Tamerlán en la batalla de Ankara (1402). Algunos historiadores afirman que se suicidó, otros sostienen que enfermó y falleció en Akşehir, en Anatolia central. A su muerte se le dio sepultura en Akşehir, en el *turbe* de Seyyid Mahmud Hayran, pero posteriormente, por orden de Tamerlán, sus restos fueron entregados a su hijo Musa Çelebi y llevados a Bursa. Así, en 1403-1404 pudo cumplirse su última voluntad: ser enterrado cerca de la mezquita que había construido; en 1406, su hijo, el emir Süleyman Çelebi, hizo levantar sobre su tumba el actual *turbe*. Durante el asedio de Bursa de 1413, el *bey* karamaní Mehmet II, para vengarse de Bayezid I, que había matado a su padre, robó el cuerpo y lo quemó.  
El *turbe* es un simple edificio cuadrado, cubierto con una cúpula y con un pórtico frontal de tres crujías, que sirvió de modelo para posteriores mausoleos otomanos con pórtico.

en.name: Blagovestenska (Annunciation) Church of the Blessed Virgin
description:
The main facade of the one-nave church – articulated with wall columns and emphatic mouldings – is crowned with a tower. The main gate, framed by garlands and topped with a heavily projected drip moulding, is embraced by columns decorated with leaves and spirals that support a stone balcony. Behind the balcony, the blind, oval choir window with an arched moulding is visible, both sides of which there are two blind windows with staggered mouldings. Above its shoulder, the facade is decorated with volutes, vases and obelisks. In front of the bell windows, arched and *ajouré* stone balconies can be seen.  
The side facades of the church are articulated by pairs of wall columns and oval, arched and square-shape windows.  
To the left of the main gate is the red marmor tomb (with an inscription in Greek) of Demeter Tolojanne, a Greek merchant from Vác, who came to Szentendre from Macedonia and died in 1759 at the age of 48. Above the entrance are portraits of *St. Constantine* and *St. Helena* in an arch-shaped frame.  
The three vaulted sections of the church are covered by net-vaults, and the stone choir is covered by a sail vault.  The arcade under the choir is topped by a barrel vault. The walls of the nave are articulated by semi-columns, and decorated with frescoes of the *Life of Jesus*. The gilded pulpit of the bishop is decorated with a portrait of St. Nicholas.  
The Rococo iconostasis (icon screen), which separates the nave and the sanctuary and rises as high as the nave, is a painted oak structure. It is the work of Mihailo Živković (Mihály Zsivkovics), a Serbian painter from Buda and protégé of Dionisziosz Popović Bishop of Buda. The iconostasis dates to the 1790s (or c. 1802–1804 according to some scholars), and is separated in the middle by a moulding which creates two main parts. The lower part is further separated by columns into five fields, each holding a painting by Zsivkovics in a richly gilded frame. In the middle, on the Gate of the Tsars, are scenes from the *Annunciation*, and above the gate is a painting of the *Last Supper*. On the left-hand side above the Gate of the Tsars is the *Virgin Mary with the Infant Jesus*. At the bottom are scenes from the *Life of Jesus*. To the right, above the Gate of the Tsars, is *Jesus Giving Blessings* and at the bottom are more scenes from the *Life of Jesus*. On other sections of the iconostasis are *St. Stephen the Deacon*, the *Annunciation*, and *St. John the Golden Mouth*. In the upper section (above the moulding) are paintings of the *Holy Trinity* and *Virgin Mary*, framed by volutes. Portraits of the 12 Apostles are contained in gilt and *ajouré* medallions.  
The altar table in the sanctuary, which closes off three sides of a trapezium, is made from red marble; the preparatory table for receiving the sacrament is of coloured stone (1754). The gilt *Zopfstil* candleholder, the painted cross of the altar table and the church Evangeliary (the work of a goldsmith from Moscow) are outstanding works.  
The Neo-Classical (1797) Serbian Orthodox school building adjoins the northern side of the church. The building used to serve as a teacher-training school between 1812 and 1816, but was then converted into a museum.

The Blagovestenska (Annunciation) Church of the Blessed Virgin was built between 1752 and 1754, and represents an outstanding example of Serbian Orthodox architecture in Hungary. Featuring elements of the Baroque and Rococo styles with a one-tower western façade, the church has an interior appropriate for Byzantine liturgy. The paintings of the richly carved and gilded iconostasis (icon screen) are the works of Mihailo Živković (Mihály Zsivkovics), a Serbian painter from Buda.
artist: Dionisije Novaković; Dionisziosz Popović, Bishop of Buda; Serbian Orthodox Church
Architect: András Mayerhoffer? (1690–1771); painter: Mihailo Živković (Mihály Zsivkovics, 1776–1824)
history:
The expansion of Turkish influence in the Balkans propelled waves of Greek, Dalmatian, Bosnian and Serbian refugees to the Hungarian Kingdom. In 1691, King Leopold I issued a “letters patent” for the sake of the Serbs who fled and settled in Hungary. King Leopold wished them to settle only temporarily in Hungary while their country was under Turkish rule, but the occupation dragged on for an unexpectedly long period. By the end of the 18th century the number of Serbs began to decrease both in terms of the population and the magistracy of Szentendre, while at the same time, the proportion of Hungarians and Germans increased, so a Catholic town magistrate was selected for a year and replaced by an orthodox magistrate the following year.  
In the 17th century some 800 fugitive families, including several merchants, sought refuge in Szentendre. They constructed a church in 1690 under the supervision of Arsen Crnojević Patriarch of Ipek. The iconostasis of the simple wooden church paid homage to the *Blagovestenska* (Annunciation) and was painted by masters from the Balkans in 1721. The iconostasis was later transferred to the Church of Izbég.  
The foundation stone of today's church was laid in 1752 and was consecrated in honour of the Annunciation by Dionisije Novaković Bishop of Buda in 1754. The design of the church is attributed to András Mayerhoffer, on account of its similarity to the Serbian Church of Pest and the Cathedral of Kalocsa, both of which were designed by him. The iconostasis was completed between 1802 and 1804.  
The 1787 decree of King Joseph II made German the compulsory language in schools, and thus the town council of Szentendre had to provide German language education for both Catholic and Greek Orthodox schools. Construction of the schools was slow, however, and there was a suggestion that Blagovestenska Church be converted into a school, but King Joseph II rescinded his language decree before he died rendering the conversion unnecessary.
keywords: Turks, Eastern Orthodox Church, Arsen Crnojević (Arzén Csernojevics), Dionisije Novaković, Dionisziosz Popović, András Mayerhoffer, Mihailo Živković (Mihály Zsivkovics), Szentendre

en.name: Subterranean Passage to Fountain of the Virgin, Jerusalem
description: A local Silwani woman carries a water jug and candle down to the Fountain of the Virgin to collect water. Another figure in the background is emerging into the daylight, having completed a similar trip. The Fountain of the Virgin, or Gihon Spring, is a freshwater spring in the Kidron Valley that represents the only local water source for Jerusalem. Other pools, like the Bethesda pool in the north of the city, held water transported from the springs at Artas, near Bethlehem. It is part of a complex and ancient water management system dating back at least to the Middle Bronze Age (c 2,000 BCE) that continued to represent a major source of fresh water for the Silwani and Jerusalem community until recent years.
keywords: Fountain of the Virgin Gihon Spring, Silwan, Jerusalem
materials: Watercolour and pencil on paper. Created in the studio from a pencil and ink sketch made on site.

en.name: Italian postcard of colonial propaganda: "Dawn of civilization"
names: Italian postcard of colonial propaganda at the time of the Italo-Ottoman war of 1911–12 over Libya
short_description: This postcard explicitly states a key element of colonial propaganda: the notion that the colonisers brought “civilisation” to the newly conquered territories. Italian navy ships in the background are intended to convey the notion of Italy’s military might, but nothing reminds viewers of the violence of the colonial enterprise: the military man in the forefront does not carry weapons, but only the Italian flag.
holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
partner: MIBACT | State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

ar.name: حامل قنديل.
description: حامل قنديل كبير من النحاس الأصفر، له قاعدة مسدسة الشكل ترتفع إلى الأعلى وتضيق حتى الوصول إلى بنية علوية كانت تحمل قبة مفقودة الآن، وكانت سلاسل التعليق مربوطة بها. حمل الجزء السفلي من البنية العديد من قناديل الزيت الزجاجية التي كان يمكن الوصول إليها عبر باب كان موجوداً على أحد الجوانب الستة. لقد تم ثقب الجوانب للسماح لضوء القناديل بالمرور عبرها، كما تم حفرها وتطعميها بتصاميم ذات رصائع كتابية تمجد السلطان قايتباي بين الزخارف الزهرية. يظهر على أسفل الحامل طوق كتابي عريض يتكرر بأحرف أصغر بشكل موازٍ في الأعلى، ويذكر "عز لمولانا السلطان الملك الأشرف سلطان الإسلام والمسلمين محيي العدل في العالمين قامع الفجرة والمتمردين سلطان العرب والعجم ملك البحرين خادم الحرمين الشريفين سيد الملوك والسلاطين أمير المؤمنين أبي النصر قايتباي خلد الله تعالى ملكه". من غير المحتمل أن تكون الزخارف مرئية عند تعليق حامل القناديل في المسجد، إلا أنها تدل مع ذلك على نوعية الفنون خلال فترة قايتباي.

حاملة مصباح، مصنوعة من النحاس، جوانبها مُخرَّمة لتمرير الضوء من خلالها، وتحتوي على مصابيح زيت مُثبَّتة في قعرها. زُخرفت بتصاميم وتقنيات عديدة، وتحتوي على عدة نقوش لاسم السلطان قايتباي. وعلى الأغلب فإن هذا المصباح كان مُعلَّقاً في أحد المساجد التي قام ببنائها، أو إعادة إعمارها.
keywords: قطعة ذات استعمال ديني؛ زخرفة زهرية.
materials: نحاس أصفر محفور ومطعم بالفضة والذهب.
tags: نحاس أصفر محفور ومطعم بالفضة والذهب.

en.name: Lamp holder.
description: A large brass lamp holder; a hexagonal base tapers upward to an upper structure which once supported a dome, now lost, to which the suspension chain would have been attached. The bottom of the structure would have held several small glass oil lamps, accessed through a door in one of the six sides which is now missing. The sides are pierced to let the light from the lamps through, as well as engraved and inlaid with designs in which an inscription medallion praising Sultan Qaytbay is nestled among floral decoration. A large inscription band at the bottom of the lamp holder, repeated in smaller calligraphy in a parallel band at the top, declares: 'Glory to our lord the Sultan, the most noble ruler, sultan of Islam and the Muslims, reviver of justice in the world, suppressor of the immoral and rebellious, sultan of the Arabs and Persians, lord of the two seas, servant of the Two Holy Shrines, master of kings and sultans, Commander of the Faithful, Abu'l-Nasr Qaytbay, may God Almighty make his reign long'! When this lamp holder hung in a mosque it is unlikely that its decoration would have been visible; still, it is indicative of the quality of the arts under Sultan Qaytbay.

A large brass lamp holder, the sides of which are pierced to reveal the light supplied by oil lamps held in its bottom. The decoration, executed in several techniques, includes several inscriptions naming Sultan Qaytbay. The lamp holder must originally have hung in a mosque he founded or renovated.
keywords: religious object; floral decoration; Mosque interior decoration; calligraphy; inscription
materials: Brass, engraved and inlaid with silver and gold.
tags: Brass, engraved and inlaid with silver and gold.

es.name: Lámpara.
description: Gran lámpara de bronce de base hexagonal que va estrechándose hacia arriba y que originalmente terminaba en una cúpula, hoy perdida, a la que iría sujeta la cadena de la que colgaba. En la parte inferior de la estructura habría varios quemadores de aceite que se encenderían por una puertecita en alguno de los lados y que tampoco se ha conservado. Los laterales están perforados para dejar salir la luz y presentan labrados e incrustaciones con motivos decorativos, entre ellos un medallón caligráfico en alabanza del sultán Qaytbay rodeado de ornamentos florales. Dos franjas caligráficas paralelas, con el mismo texto, decoran la parte inferior y superior, esta última en caracteres menores: “Gloria a nuestro señor el Sultán, el gobernante más noble, sultán del Islam y de los musulmanes, restablecedor de la justicia en el mundo, supresor de lo inmoral y rebelde, sultán de los árabes y persas, señor de los dos mares, servidor de los Dos Sagrados Sepulcros, maestro de reyes y sultanes, Comandante de la fe, Abu l-Nasr Qaytbay, ¡que Dios todopoderoso alargue su reinado!”. La decoración de esta lámpara –que sería imposible de apreciar cuando colgaba del techo de alguna mezquita– demuestra la calidad de las artes en la época del sultán Qaytbay.

Gran lámpara de bronce con laterales perforados para que saliese la luz de los quemadores de aceite que estarían sujetos a su parte inferior. La decoración, ejecutada con varias técnicas, incluye varias inscripciones que nombran al sultán Qaytbay. Originalmente, colgaba en alguna mezquita de nueva planta o reformada por este sultán.
keywords: objetos religiosos; decoración floral
materials: Bronce grabado y con incrustaciones en plata y oro.
tags: Bronce grabado y con incrustaciones en plata y oro.

fr.name: Porte-lampes.
description: Grand porte-lampes en cuivre jaune. Sa base hexagonale se rétrécit vers une structure supérieure qui supportait un petit dôme, aujourd'hui perdu, auquel la chaîne de suspension était attachée. Le bas de l'ensemble pouvait contenir plusieurs lampes à huile, accessibles par une porte (manquante) ménagée sur l'un des six côtés. Ceux-ci sont percés pour laisser passer la lumière des lampes, ainsi que gravés et incrustés de motifs au milieu desquels, nichée dans un décor floral, figure une inscription en médaillon à la gloire du sultan Qaytbay. Un large bandeau épigraphique à la base du porte-lampes, répété en calligraphie plus petite sur un bandeau parallèle en partie supérieure, dit : “Gloire à notre seigneur le Sultan, le plus noble des souverains, sultan de l'Islam et des Musulmans, Celui qui ranime la justice dans le monde, Destructeur de l'immoralité et de la rébellion, sultan des Arabes et des Perses, seigneur des deux mers, serviteur des Deux Nobles Sanctuaires, maître des rois et des sultans, Commandeur des Croyants, Abou'l-Nasr Qaytbay, que Dieu tout-puissant lui assure un long règne !” Lorsque ce porte-lampes était suspendu dans une mosquée, il est peu probable que son décor ait été visible, mais il reste néanmoins indicatif de la qualité de l'activité artistique sous le sultanat de Qaytbay.

Grand porte-lampes en cuivre jaune, dont les côtés sont percés pour laisser se diffuser la lumière des lampes à huile placées en bas. La décoration, qui fait appel à plusieurs techniques, comprend plusieurs inscriptions désignant le sultan Qaytbay. Le porte-lampes était vraisemblablement suspendu, à l'origine, dans une mosquée fondée ou restaurée par lui.
keywords: Objets religieux ; décoration florale
materials: Cuivre jaune gravé et incrusté d’or et d’argent.
tags: Cuivre jaune gravé et incrusté d’or et d’argent.

ar.name: كشكول
description: طاسة على شكل قارب عليه زخارف لأشكال حيوانات وسط زخارف نباتية. على الحواف توجد كتابات خطية عريضة بخط الثلث. حملوها الهائمين الروحيين الفقراء مثل هذه الطاسات في أياديهم أو علقوها على أكتافهم لجمع التبرعات. وكانوا يتبرعون أحيانا لغيرهم من المحتاجين. الكشكول كلمة فارسية من الكلمات كش (تعني السحب) وكلمة كول (تعني الكتف).

en.name: *Kashkul*
description: Boat-shaped begging bowl etched with small animals amidst interlocking floral and vegetal decoration and two human motifs. Below the shoulder is a wide band of *thuluth* calligraphy. Dervishes carried these bowls in their hands or hung them over their shoulders to collect charitable donations. On occasion they shared some of the donations with others in need. *Kashkul i*s a Persian word from *kish* (to drag) and *kul*(shoulder).
keywords: Kashkul; begging bowl

ar.name: حلية متدلية
description: إن شكل الزمرد في مركز هذه الحلية المتدلية كان يحدد بواسطة بنيته البلورية والتي هي مثمنة بشكل طبيعي. والتصميم الأخير صنع بشكل خاص ليتمم الشكل السداسي الأضلاع للزمرد وهو محاط بألماس ذو أشكال وقياسات متعددة في تشكيلات فردية للذهب. وفي أعلى الحلية يوجد ست تيجان من اللؤلؤ وكل منها يتضمن لؤلؤة كبيرة يعلوها خرزة خضراء وحيدة. وفي أسفل الحلية هناك ثلاث حلقات من الذهب التي تعلق منها ثلاثة زمردات بشكل الدمعة.

en.name: Pendant
description: The shape of the emerald at the centre of this pendant was determined by its crystallography, which is naturally hexagonal. The later setting was custom-made to complement the emerald's six-sided shape. It is surrounded by variously shaped and sized diamonds in individual gold settings. The top of the pendant features six pearl crowns, each including a large pearl topped with a single green bead. At the bottom of the pendant are three gold loops, from which hang three teardrop-shaped emeralds.

en.name: *Der wunderbare Fischzug (The Miraculous Draught of Fish)*
description: In 1515/16, on commission to Pope Leo X, Raphael produced ten large-format preparatory drawings for tapestries which were intended for the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican. These tapestries, which are among the most outstanding achievements of the High Renaissance in Rome, were woven in the manufactory operated by Pieter van Aelst in Brussels (they are now held in the Pinacoteca Vaticana, Città del Vaticano). Designed for use in celebratory masses, they depict scenes from the life of the two chief apostles, saints Peter and Paul. A few of Raphael's cartoons turned up in Genoa in 1623 and were purchased by the Prince of Wales, the later King Charles I. The designs were used again at the Mortlake Tapestry Works in England. The Mortlake works not only wove a series for Charles I but also produced the one that later came into the collection of Augustus the Strong in Dresden. Three of the six tapestries in Dresden are dedicated to Saint Peter, the other three to Saint Paul. The depiction of the Miraculous Draught of Fish (Luke 5, 1-11) begins the series devoted to Saint Peter: although Peter has been fishing all night without success, he follows Jesus’ instruction to put out into the Sea of Galilee and cast his net once again. This time the fishermen are so successful that their two boats return to the shore overloaded with fish. Peter and his companions James and John recognise the greatness of Jesus, fall at his feet and worship him. Jesus then summons them to become his disciples and follow him. The dynamic, monumental figures reveal a stylistic proximity to Michelangelo. The restoration of the entire series between 1991 and 1997 was made possible by a generous donation from the businessman Rudolf Augustus Oetker.
type: Tapestry; after a cartoon by Raphael
holder: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery), Dresden State Art Collections
dates:
Design: c. 1515;  
Execution: 2nd quarter of the 17th century (from 1623)
keywords: Tapestry; Christianity; Bibel; New Testament, Cartoon; Renaissance

cs.name: Půdorys
description: Základem je kompozice pěticípé hvězdy (pěticípý půdorys, pět vchodů, pět oltářních výklenků, dvakrát pět kaplí kolem centrálního prostoru, pět hvězd a pět andělů na hlavním oltáři), symbol nejen pěti ran Kristových, ale také pěti písmen v latinské slově „tacui“ (mlčel jsem) a především pěti hvězd ve svatozáři mučedníka sv. Jana Nepomuckého, které se podle legendy objevily ve Vltavě po jeho utonutí.

en.name: Ground plan
description: The principal compositional element is a five-pointed star (five-pointed ground plan, five entrances, five altar niches, ten chapels surrounding the central space, five stars and five angels on the high altar), symbolising the five wounds of Christ, five letters in the Latin word *tacui* (“I was silent”) and, in particular, five stars in the halo of St. John of Nepomuk. Legend has it that the stars appeared in the River Vltava after the martyr had been drowned in it.

ar.name: قصر آلكوتيم العتيق (كاستيلو فيلهو دي آلكوتيم).
description: يقع قصر آلكوتيم العتيق على قمة يبلغ ارتفاعها 96 متراً وتطل على نهر غواديانا. القصر عبارة عن قرية (ألكاريا) ذات مخطط رباعي الزوايا (34 على 22 متر مع مساحة داخلية تصل إلى 700 متر مربع)، ومحمية بثلاثة خطوط من الأسوار الدفاعية. يحتوي المخطط الإجمالي على منطقة مركزية يشغلها بناء لانعرف وظيفته، وثلاثة شوارع، وعدة بيوت سكنية، وبقايا يحتمل أن تكون لمحرز للحرس، وخزان ماء ومراحيض. طُليت الأسوار المبنية من حجر النضيد الفج والحصى بالملاط مع تراب وطبقة من الكلس، ودُعمتْ بثلاثة أبراج ضخمة مربعة ومستطيلة. يتم الدخول إلى السور التحصيني عبر بابين، عرف المدخل الرئيسي تغيييرات في بداية القرن 4 الهجري / منتصف القرن 10 الميلادي عندما أضيف له مدخل مُكوّع مشيّد على شكل برج صغير (بريج). سمحت الحفريات الأثرية بالكشف عن آثار حرائق وتهدم البناء في القرن 4 الهجري / القرن 10 الميلادي، وقد تم ذلك على الأغلب في الفترة التي سبقت بسط سلطة الخلافة. وفي نهاية القرن 5 الهجري / القرن 11 الميلادي، خلال فترة الطوائف، هُجِرَ الموقع بأكمله. كان هذا القصر يأوي سكاناً يكرسون وقتهم للعمل بالزراعة وفي المناجم داخل المواقع القريبة، وكانوا يستخدمون نهر غواديانا كطريق رئيسي للمواصلات وللتجارة.

يقع حصن آلكوتيم القديم فوق رابية تشرفُ على نهر جواديانا؛ وهو منشأة تنتظم في تصميم مستطيل، وتحتمي بثلاث خطوط من الأسوار الدفاعية تغطي مساحة يبلغ طولها 34 متر وعرضها 22 متر. تشتمل المجموعةُ على فضاء مركزي يشغله مبنى نجهل وظيفته، وثلاثة أزقة، ومساكن وخزانٍ مائي. بُنيت الأسوار بحجر النضيد وبالتراب؛ وهي مجاورة لأبراج ضخمة عديدة، مربعة ومستطيلة الشكل. يتم الدخول إلى القصبة عبر بابين؛ وجرى هجرُ الموقع في نهاية القرن 5 الهجري / القرن 11 الميلادي.
dynasty: الفترة الأموية، مرحلة الإمارة والخلافة (139 – 422 هجري / 756 – 1031 ميلادي)، ومرحلة ملوك الطوائف (422 – 488 هجري / 1031 – 1095 ميلادي).
keywords: آلكوتيم؛ أمويو الأندلس؛ تجارة؛ خزان؛ عمارة عسكرية؛ غواديانا؛ مدخل مكوع، ملاط؛ مواد بناء؛ نضيد.
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: Old Castle of Alcoutim.
description: The Old Castle of Alcoutim stands on the top of a hill at an altitude of 96 metres, overlooking the River Guadiana and the border. It corresponds to a fortified village, rectangular in plan, protected by three rows of defensive walls. This group which measures 34 x 22 metres encloses an area of 700 square metres, including a central area occupied by a building of unknown function, three streets, various dwellings, a possible guardroom, a cistern and a latrine. The walls are built of coarse masonry of schist and greywackes (variety of sandstone) mortared with earth and plastered with lime, against which a number of substantial square and rectangular towers are built. Two doors gave access to the fortified enclosure. The main entrance was altered in the AH early 4th / AD mid-10th century, the right-angled access having been enlarged and a large *bartizan* (overhanging turret) constructed. The archaeological excavations carried out have also revealed that the buildings suffered fires and destruction in the AH 4th / AD 10th century, probably during the period prior to the establishment of caliphal power. The whole complex was abandoned at the end of AH 5th / AD 11th century, during the Taifa period. The population that lived in this castle focused its agricultural and mining activities on the surrounding region, using the River Guadiana as their main route for communication and trade.

The Old Castle at Alcoutim sits on a hill overlooking the Guadiana River. It is a rectangular settlement defended by three lines of walls and covers an area measuring 34 m by 22 m. It includes a central area with a building of unknown purpose, three streets, houses and a cistern. The walls are made of schistose brick and earth, and adjoin a number of solid square or rectangular towers. Two gateways afforded access to the fortified enclosure. The site was abandoned in the late AH 5th / AD 11th century.
dates: Hegira middle of 3rd–end of 5th / AD 9th–11th centuries.
dynasty: Umayyad of al-Andalus, Emirate and Caliphate periods.
keywords: Alcoutim; Umayyads of al-Andalus; Guadiana; masonry; schist; mortar; right-angled entrance; cistern; military architecture; trade

es.name: Castillo Viejo.
description: El Castillo Viejo de Alcoutim se alza en un cerro de 96 metros de altitud, dominando el río Guadiana y la margen fronteriza. Corresponde a una alquería de planta rectangular, defendida por tres líneas de murallas. Forman el conjunto, de 34 x 22 m y un área de 700 m², una zona central ocupada por un edificio de función desconocida, tres calles, varias viviendas, un posible alojamiento para la guardia, una cisterna y una letrina. A las murallas, que son de albañilería basta de pizarra y grava con argamasa de tierra y masilla de cal, están adosadas varias torres macizas de planta cuadrada o rectangular. El acceso al recinto fortificado se hace por dos puertas. La entrada principal sufrió alteraciones a principios de siglo IV / mediados del X: se añadió el acceso en codo y se construyó un torreón. Las excavaciones arqueológicas realizadas han permitido también descubrir indicios de incendios y destrucción de edificios en el siglo IV / X, probablemente durante la fase que precedió al establecimiento del poder califal. El abandono del conjunto se produjo a finales del siglo V / XI, durante el periodo de los reinos de taifa. En este castillo vivió una población que desarrollaba actividades agrícolas y mineras en los alrededores, y utilizaba el río Guadiana como principal vía de comunicación y comercio.

El Castillo Viejo de Alcoutim se alza en un cerro de el que se domina el río Guadiana. Corresponde a una alquería de planta rectangular, defendida por tres líneas de murallas. Forman el conjunto, de 34 x 22 m, una zona central ocupada por un edificio de función desconocida, tres calles, casas y una cisterna. Las murallas son de albañilería de pizarra y tierra. A ellas están adosadas varias torres macizas de planta cuadrada o rectangular. El acceso al recinto fortificado se hacía por dos puertas. El abandono del lugar data de finales del siglo V / XI.
dates: Siglo III–finales del V de la Hégira / IX–XI d. C.
dynasty: omeyas de al-Andalus (periodos emiral y califal), taifas
keywords: Guadiana; albañilería; pizarra; argamasa; acceso en acodo; cisterna; arquitectura militar; comercio
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Castelo Velho de Alcoutim (vieux château d’Alcoutim)
description: Le vieux château d'Alcoutim est situé sur un sommet de 96 mètres d'altitude, surplombant le fleuve Guadiana. Il correspond à une *alcaria* (hameau) de plan rectangulaire (34 x 22 m pour une superficie intérieure de 700 m2) protégée par trois lignes de murailles défensives. L'ensemble comprend une zone centrale occupée par un édifice dont on ignore la fonction, trois rues, plusieurs habitations, un possible réduit pour la garde, une citerne et des latrines. Les murailles, en maçonnerie grossière de schistes et gravats enduits au mortier avec de la terre et du crépi de chaux, sont renforcées par plusieurs tours massives carrées et rectangulaires. L'accès à l'enceinte fortifiée se fait par deux portes. L'entrée principale a connu des altérations au début du IVe siècle H (milieu du Xe siècle J.-C.), lorsqu'on lui a ajouté un accès coudé édifié en tourelle. Les fouilles archéologiques ont permis de déceler des incendies et la destruction de bâtiments au IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.), probablement pendant le moment qui a précédé l'installation du pouvoir califal. L'ensemble a été abandonné à la fin du Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.), pendant la période des Taïfas. Ce château a abrité une population qui se consacrait aux activités agricoles et minières dans les environs et qui utilisait le fleuve Guadiana comme principale voie de communication et de commerce.

Le vieux château d'Alcoutim est situé sur une colline surplombant le fleuve Guadiana. C'est un établissement de plan rectangulaire protégé par trois lignes de murailles défensives couvrant une surface de 34 m de longueur sur 22 m. L'ensemble comprend une zone centrale occupée par un édifice dont on ignore la fonction, trois rues, des habitations et une citerne. Les murs sont constitués de briques schisteuses et de terre, et sont contigus à plusieurs tours massives carrées et rectangulaires. L'accès à l'enceinte fortifiée se fait par deux portes. Le site fut abandonné à la fin du Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.).
dates: Milieu IIIe-fin Ve siècle de l’Hégire (IXe-fin XIe siècle J.-C.).
dynasty: Omeyyade, périodes émirale et califale (139-422 H / 756-1031 J.-C.) et période des Taïfas (422-488 H / 1031-1095 J.-C.).
keywords: Alcoutim ; Omeyyades d’al-Andalus ; Guadiana ; maçonnerie ; schiste ; mortier ; entrée coudée ; citerne ; architecture militaire ; commerce
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Castelo Velho de Alcoutim.
description: O Castelo Velho de Alcoutim localiza-se num cabeço a 96 metros de altitude, dominando o rio Guadiana e a margem fronteira. Corresponde a uma alcaria de planta rectangular, defendida por três linhas defensivas de muralhas. Este conjunto com as dimensões de 34 x 22 metros e uma área interna de 700 m2, integra uma zona central ocupada por um edifício de função desconhecida, três ruas, várias habitações, possível compartimento da guarda, uma cisterna e latrina. As muralhas são de alvenaria grosseira de xistos e grauvaques argamassados com terra e reboco de cal, às quais estão adossadas várias torres maciças de planta quadrada e rectangular. O acesso ao recinto fortificado é feito por duas portas. A entrada principal sofreu alterações nos inícios séc. IV AH /meados do séc. X AD, sendo acrescentado o acesso em cotovelo e construído um torreão. As escavações arqueológicas realizadas permitiram ainda observar incêndios e destruição de edifícios no séc. IV AH / séc. X AD, provavelmente durante a fase que antecedeu o estabelecimento do poder califal. O abandono do conjunto verificou-se nos finais do séc. V AH / finais do séc. XI AD, durante o período das taifas. Neste castelo viveu um grupo populacional que centrava as suas actividades agrícolas e mineiras no território envolvente, utilizando o rio Guadiana como principal via de comunicação e comércio.

O Castelo Velho de Alcoutim localiza-se num cerro de onde se domina o rio Guadiana. Corresponde a uma alcaria de planta rectangular, defendida por três linhas defensivas de muralhas. Este conjunto com 34 x 22 metros integra uma zona central ocupada por um edifício de função desconhecida, três ruas, habitações e uma cisterna. As muralhas são de alvenaria de xisto e terra. Estão-lhes adossadas várias torres maciças de planta quadrada e rectangular. O acesso ao recinto fortificado era feito por duas portas. O abandono do sítio data de finais do séc. V H./finais do séc. XI d.C.
dates: Meados séc. III-finais séc. V AH / séc. IX-finais séc. XI AD.
dynasty: Omíadas, períodos emiral e califal (139-422 AH / 756-1031 AD) e período das taifas (422-488 AH / 1031-1095 AD).

en.name: Church of Santa María de Arbás
description:
The Church of Santa María de Arbás is a National Monument not only because of the carpentry work, but also for the plasterwork. Mentioned as San Nicolás de Arbás, in 1537, this church, along with the primitive Church of San Andrés documented since 1191, formed part of the Parish of Santa María. It has two aisles, the principal one with the characteristic semicircular apse with cob walls, while on the Epistle side are the Chapel of San Andrés and the portico.  
The church is covered with a wooden armadura of the *par y nudillo* type, and in the *arrocabes* there are Renaissance devices such as triglyphs, arches and rosettes. The Gospel side aisle has a roof of single *limas* with cross braces, which ends in the sanctuary in a threepart coffer-shaped wooden ceiling inlaid with metals and unpainted. At the entrance to the nave there is a coat of arms depicting an eagle with outspread wings and a heraldic device of two chequered vessels with the heads of serpents. These may relate to a daughter of the fifth Count of Benavente, who was married to Juan Fernández Manrique, third Marquis of Aguilar. What is strange, though, is that while the coats of arms of the Aguilar appear those of the Pimentel do not.  
Perhaps the most representative work of the church is the Chapel of San Andrés on the Epistle side, with an inlaid coffered ceiling of double *limas* with strapwork and cone shaped pendentives. The frieze or *arrocabe* that runs around beneath it is a good example of 15th-century plasterwork in the area. The arms and inscription refer to don Pero García Dévila Gómez and his wife, who ordered this chapel to be built in 1422.  
The use of geometric motifs with multifoil arches, diamond-shaped networks and plant motifs of Hispano- Muslim and Christian origin seems to have originated in Seville in the early 15th century. From here it reached Castile, either through the influence of the Velasco family in their palace in Medina de Pomar and the Tower of Lomana (both in the province of Burgos) or perhaps through the examples in Mayorga (1422), Valladolid (1429) and Sahagún (1455), in this latter case in the valley of the River Cea in León.

es.name: Iglesia de Santa María de Arbás
description:
La iglesia de Santa María de Arbás es Monumento Nacional no sólo por su carpintería, sino por su obra de yesería. Aparece citada como San Nicolás de Arbás en 1537. Esta iglesia, al igual que una primitiva iglesia de San Andrés, documentada desde 1191, vinieron a formar parte de la parroquia de Santa María. Tiene dos naves y la principal posee el característico ábside semicircular de tapial, mientras que del lado de la epístola se levantan la capilla de San Andrés y el pórtico.  
La iglesia se cubre con *armadura* de madera *de par y nudillo*, en cuyos *arrocabes* hay artificios renacentistas como triglifos, arquillos y rosetas. La nave del evangelio lleva una cubierta de limas simples con cuadrales, que termina en su cabecera con una techumbre ataujerada de madera sin pintar en forma de artesa con tres paños. En el paso a la nave hay un escudo con un águila de alas explayadas y dos calderos ajedrezados con sierpes, que podría estar en relación con una hija del quinto conde de Benavente, casada con Juan Fernández Manrique, III marqués de Aguilar. Lo extraño es que, apareciendo el escudo de los Aguilar, no aparezca el de los Pimentel.  
La obra más representativa de la iglesia tal vez sea la denominada capilla de San Andrés, en el lado de la epístola. Se cubre con una artesa ataujerada de limas dobles con lacería y piñas. El friso o *arrocabe* que corre por debajo es un buen ejemplo de yesería del siglo XV en la zona. Los escudos y la inscripción aluden a don Pero García Dévila Gómez y su mujer, que mandaron hacer esta capilla en 1422.  
La utilización de motivos geométricos con arcos lobulados, redes de rombos y motivos vegetales hispano-musulmanes y cristianos parece tener su origen en la Sevilla de inicios del siglo XV, de donde llegó a Castilla, bien por influjo de la familia Velasco en su palacio de Medina de Pomar y la torre de Lomana (ambas en la provincia de Burgos), bien a través de los ejemplos de Mayorga (1422), Valladolid (1429) y Sahagún (1455), en este segundo caso hasta la comarca leonesa del Cea.

ar.name: أبو يحيى زكريا ابن محمد القزويني / تحفة الغرائب
description:
إن الكتاب الشهير عجائب المخلوقات وغرائب الموجودات كتب بالعربية من قبل أبو يحيى زكريا ابن محمد القزويني ( 600 - 682 هجري / 1203 – 1283 ميلادي). وهذه النسخة الفارسية من القرن السابع عشر تدعى بتحفة الغرائب والتي وضعت في قزوين في إيران من قبل الخطاط علي الحافظ خلال عصر سلالة العائلة الصفوية الحاكمة في شهر شوال من عام 984 هجري كما هو مبين من قبل معلومات الناسخ. وتوافق هذه الفترة شهر ديسمبر – يناير من عام 1576 – 77.ويبين وجود خاتمين لمالكين عربيين وأيضا كتابات لفينزسلاف ريزوفسكي (1765 – 1831) أنها كانت جزءا من مجموعات سابقة قبل أن تحوز عليها المكتبة الوطنية النمساوية في عام 1831.  
ومن المحتمل أن يكون للمخطوطة تجليد معاصر مطلي بالورنيش / اللكر من العصر الصفوي. والنص المكتوب بخط النستعليق يسبقه زخرفة غنية لفاتحة / مقدمة مزدوجة ويليه منمنمات بحجم نصف صفحة أو اصغر عددها 488 وهذه الرسوم يمكن نسبتها للعديد من الرسامين وتعكس مزيج من الطراز الامبراطوري و البسيط. والمخطوطة غير منتهية حيث يوجد عناصر معينة تتضمن مجموعة ألوان مختلفة وجودة الرسوم تكشف عن انها ربما رممت وجمعت في تركيا العثمانية.  
ولكن من حيث الطراز فإنه يمكن القول بأن أصلها هو من قزوين التي صارت العاصمة الصفوية وربما يمكن تحديد تاريخها بالفترة التي كان فيها الحاكم شاه طهماسب قد فقد الاهتمام بالنواحي الفنية في الكتب والذي أدى لتحول في رعاية هذا النوع من الفن للنبلاء. وبسبب هذا فإنه من المحتمل أن هذه المخطوطة قد أمر بنسخها للافتخار وإن عناصر طراز الرسم الشيرازي أيضا ملحوظة وهي تشابه مخطوطة تعود لعام 1549 لسعيد ( مقتنيات المكتبة البريطانية 24944 ، الصفحة 2v-3r ).
materials: حبر ، لون وذهب على ورق. تخطيط بالنستعليق بـ 17 سطر في الصفحة الواحدة
tags: حبر ، لون وذهب على ورق. تخطيط بالنستعليق بـ 17 سطر في الصفحة الواحدة

en.name: Abu Yahya Zakariyya' ibn Muhammad al-Qazwini, *Tuhfat al-Ghara'ib* (The Gift of Oddities)
description: The famous *“'Aja'ib al-Makhluqat wa Ghara'ib al-Mawjudat”* (The Wonders of Creatures and the Marvels of Creation) was written in Arabic by Abu Yahya Zakariyya' ibn Muhammad al-Qazwini (600-682 AH / 1203-1283 AD). This 17th-century Persian copy referred to as *“Tuhfat al-Ghara'ib”* (The Gift of Oddities) was possibly created in Qazwin, Iran, by the scribe 'Ali al-Hafiz during the Safavid dynasty in the month of ‘Sawwal’ in 984 AH as indicated by the colophon. This period corresponds to December-January 1576–77. Two Arabic ownership stamps as well as ownership inscriptions of Wenzeslav Rzewuski (1765–1831) reveal that it was part of previous collections before it was acquired by the Austrian National Library in 1831. The manuscript has a likely contemporaneous Safavid lacquer binding. The text, penned in *nasta’liq* script, is preceded by a richly decorated double-frontispiece and followed by various 488 half-page or smaller miniatures. These paintings can be attributed to several painters and reflect a mix of an imperial and provincial style. The manuscript is unfinished, yet particular elements including the varying colour palette and quality of the illustrations reveal that it was possibly restored and appended to in Ottoman Turkey. Stylistically, however, it can be related to Qazwin, the then Safavid capital, and perhaps dated to the period when the ruler Shah Tahmasp had lost interest in the artistic qualities of the book, which resulted in a shift of patronage to the nobility. As such, it is likely that this manuscript was commissioned by a dignitary. Elements of the Shirazi painting style are also noticeable, comparable to a 1569 manuscript of Sa’di (British Library Add. 24944, fol.2v–3r).
keywords: Bilqis; creation; King Solomon; nasta'liq; Qazwin; Queen of Sheba; wonders
materials: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic *nasta'liq* of 17 lines per page.
tags: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic nasta'liq of 17 lines per page.

en.name: Carpet
description:
Rectangular carpet from the Crown or Laurel series, derived from the Holbein series.  
Field: The field consists of crowns with an octagonal shape formed by foliage and shapes reminiscent of stylised cobs. Spread out cruciformly within the octagonal shapes are plant motifs that are curled into decorative scrollwork and ataurique motifs. The green coloured foliage stands out on the orange-red background.  
Border: The border consists of vegetal candlestick motifs.  
A two-strand Franciscan knot strip separates the field from the border. All the decorative motifs of the carpet are outlined in yellow.  
The warp is of naturally coloured linen and the weft is of naturally coloured wool. The decorative aspects are defined by woollen knots of green, yellow and orange red.  
This carpet is similar to one published by Ferrandis Torres, J. 1933, Catalog of the Exhibition of Ancient Spanish Carpets. Madrid, No. 36, Plate XXVIII, p. 112, presented by Count Welczeck. It is the carpet that appears in the Weissberger collection with the number 7.  
In the Holbein series the octagons were separated by registers, whilst in this one such a demarcation is only suggested in the intersection of the columns by a partial cruciform design.  
On the other hand, the decoration of the border and the field corresponds to the renovating models of the Renaissance period.
artist: Workshops of Alcaraz (Old Kingdom of Murcia, Spain)
keywords: Alcaraz

es.name: Alfombra
description:
Alfombra rectangular de la serie de coronas o laureas, derivada de la serie Holbein.  
Campo: Coronas en las que se adivina una forma octogonal formada por abundante hojarasca y formas que recuerdan a mazorcas estilizadas. En su interior, repartido de forma cruciforme, los motivos vegetales se enroscan en tornapuntas y atauriques. La decoración verde resalta sobre el fondo rojo anaranjado.  
Marco: Motivos vegetales continuos en forma de candeleri.  
Una franja de nudo franciscano de dos cabos separa el campo del marco. Todos los motivos decorativos de la alfombra aparecen perfilados en color amarillo.  
Urdimbre en lino en su color y trama en lana en su color. La decoración está realizada en lana en dos tonos de verde, amarillo y rojo anaranjado.  
Similar a una publicada por Ferrandis Torres, J. 1933, Catálogo de la Exposición de Alfombras Antiguas Españolas. Madrid, nº 36, lámina XXVIII, p. 112, expuesta por el Conde Welczeck. Es la alfombra que figura en la relación de adquisición Weissberger con el número 7.  
Los registros que en la serie Holbein separaban los octógonos, en esta sólo están insinuados en la intersección de las calles por la cuarta parte de un diseño cruciforme.  
Por otro lado, la decoración del marco y el campo corresponde a los modelos renovadores del Renacimiento.
keywords: Alcaraz
materials: Urdimbre: Lino en su color. Trama: Lana en su color
tags: Urdimbre: Lino en su color. Trama: Lana en su color

de.name: Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche Mariae Himmelfahrt
description: Die Wallfahrtskirche zu Mariae Himmelfahrt in Kaltenbrunn ist im Wesentlichen ein Werk einheimischer Tiroler Kräfte, was charakteristische Einflüsse der Volkskunst mit sich bringt, etwa bei den Deckenbildern. Die ursprünglich spätgotische Saalkirche mit eingezogenem Chor ist noch an den Spitzbögen der Fenstern und des Chorbogens zu erkennen, die Ausstattung wird dagegen vom beginnenden Spätbarock geprägt. Der feine Deckenstuck Wessobrunner Prägung rahmt verhältnismäßig kleine Freskofelder, die in kräftigen Farben gemalt wurden. Auch die Altarausstellung ist von beachtlicher Qualität; so stammt das Gemälde des linken Seitenaltars, eine Darstellung der Verkündigung, von Peter Candid aus München (um 1610/20), ein Geschenk von Kurfürst Max Emanuel von Bayern.

Die Wallfahrtskirche Kaltenbrunn im Kaunertal, landschaftlich reizvoll an einem steilen Hang gelegen, ist ein besonders schönes Beispiel für eine Gnadenstätte aus dem Mittelalter, die im Spätbarock von meist einheimischen Künstlern in ein neues Gewand gekleidet worden ist. Dabei erhielt der spätgotische Bau eine barocke Gewölbeform mit vielteiligem Freskenzyklus und zeitgemäßem Bandelwerkstuck. Für das Gnadenbild selbst wurde inmitten des Langhauses eine eigene Kapelle errichtet.
artist:
Architektur (Gnadenkapelle): Gallus Gratl (1684-1751)  
Stuck: Anton und Augustin Gigl (Zuschreibung)  
Deckenbilder und Altargemälde: Franz Laukas (1690-1765)  
Hochaltarfiguren: Andreas Kölle (1680-1755)
history: Die Ursprünge der Wallfahrt von Kaltenbrunn, von denen eine Legende berichtet, dürften bis ins 12. Jahrhundert zurückreichen. Ein Ritter von Schenkenberg soll 1285 eine steinerne Kirche geweiht haben, die 1438 abgebrannt ist. Ende des 15. Jahrhunderts wurde ein Neubau begonnen, der 1502 (Chor) bzw. 1592 (Langhaus) geweiht worden ist. Der Turm vollendet 1668. Im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert erfolgten Barockisierungen, das Innere ist im wesentlichen geprägt durch die Ausstattung um 1720/30. Zur Pfarre 1891 erhoben. Restauriert 1977-82.
keywords: Wallfahrtskirche

en.name: Parish and Pilgrimage Church of the Assumption
description: The Pilgrimage Church of the Assumption is essentially a work of local Tyrolean craftsmen, which brought with them a certain folk art influence, for example in the ceiling pictures. The original Late Gothic hall church with retracted choir can still be seen in a number of pointed arches. In contrast, the interior work is characterised by the beginnings of the Late Baroque style. The delicate ceiling stucco, influenced by the Wessobrunn school, frames relatively small fresco panels which are painted in bright colours. The ensemble of altars is also of striking quality, in particular the painting of the left hand-side altar from Peter Candid from Munich (c. 1610/20).

The Kaltenbrunn Pilgrimage Church in Kaunertal, delightfully situated on a steep incline, is an especially beautiful example of a medieval site of pilgrimage which was given a new face in the Late Baroque period, largely by local artists. The Late Gothic building received a Baroque vault with a multi-part cycle of frescos and strapwork stucco. A chapel was specially built for the miraculous picture in the centre of the nave.
artist: Architecture (Chapel of Mercy): Gallus Gratl (1684–1751); stuccowork, attributed to: Anton Gigl (1700–1769), Augustin Gigl (dates unknown, active in the first half of the 18th century); ceiling and altar paintings: Franz Laukas (1690–1765); high altar figures: Andreas Kölle (1680–1755); crucifix: attributed to Andreas Thamasch (1639–1697)
history: The origins of the pilgrimage, which is recounted in a legend, presumably date back to the 12th century. A knight from Schenkenberg is purported to have consecrated a stone church on the site in 1285 which burnt down in 1438. At the end of the 15th century, work on a new building was started and consecrated in 1502 (choir), i.e. 1582 (nave). The tower was completed in 1668. A Baroque redesign was carried out in the 17th and 18th century, the interior is essentially characterised by the fittings from about 1720/30. Elevated to the status of a parish in 1891, it was restored between 1977 and 1982.
keywords: Pilgrimage; Church

en.name: Qal‘at Ja‘bar
description:
Qal‘at Ja‘bar uses a natural elevation as a strategic setting, surrounded by defensive walls and a ditch. The strategic importance of the site is still obvious, overlooking as it does the Euphrates. Now situated on the shore of Lake Asad, its visual impact has increased and it currently forms a peninsula surrounded by the intensely blue waters of the artificial lake.  
The fortification stretches 320 m from north to south and 70 m from east to west, surrounded by two curtain walls both provided with more than 35 salient towers. In the lower part, the towers are of limestone. The upper parts – largely restored after 1972 – are made of baked bricks of semi-circular, semi-octagonal or rectangular shapes. The walls between the towers are provided with niches containing arrow slits.  
The entrance at the south-west corner of the walls, topped by a small arch, has two towers that guard it. Integrated into the south- western curtain wall, a large building with a particularly well-preserved brick decoration rises immediately above the entrance. The huge inner-vault construction is partly preserved.  
A cylindrical minaret on a 5 m-high square base rises from the middle of the fortress. Constructions attached to its east side were probably from a mosque that was later during the Mamluk period converted into workshops. An inscription dating to 569/1173, and naming Nur al-Din who was the patron of vast restoration works at the site, marks the upper part of the minaret. The inscription, flanked by two bands of continuous saltire crosses, is topped by a row of dogtooth moulding. Four arched windows, connected by pearl borders alternating with inlaid lozenges of patterned brick, appear on the upper part of the minaret.

en.name: Banknote
short_description: 50 piasters from the days of Khedive `Abbas Hilmi II. During this time, a collection of Ottoman coins made of silver and copper circulated, valued at one, five and ten piasters. They were minted in AH 1327 / AD 1909 and bore the name of the Ottoman Sultan Muhammad V. However, the most important monetary event took place in 1898, when Khedive `Abbas Hilmi II granted a franchise to Raphael Suares to establish the National Bank of Egypt. This franchise gave him the right to produce securities that were accepted to pay domanial money, and the right to cash this money as gold upon demand.
keywords: Egyptian currency; money minting; coin; paper money; Abbas Helmy II

en.name: Muslim soldiers of an Austro-Hungarian infantry-regiment from Bosnia-Herzegovina worshipping in a mosque

The quota of Muslim soldiers in the k.u.k. army reached 0.8 per cent.

description: الإبريق مغطى بزجاج فيروزي شفاف وله مقبضن بشكل مخاتل ومسكبتين بشكل رأس ثور والتصاميم هي تشكيلات شاقولية لأشكال أوراق مواجهة لريشات طاووس منحنية. ويوجد عصابتين من النقوش محصورة على خلفية سوداء وتقول شعرا بشكل رباعي الذي كان نوعا شائعا من الشعر المؤسس في نهاية القرن العاشر. والسطح الداخلي عليه مجموعة من الأسماك.

el.name: Κούπα
description: Το κανάτι καλύπτεται με τιρκουάζ διαφανή εφυάλωση και έχει δύο λαβές και δύο στόμια σε σχήμα αιλουροειδούς και κεφαλής ταύρου αντίστοιχα. Ο διάκοσμος σχηματίζεται από κάθετες φυλλόσχημες συνθέσεις διάσπαρτες με καμπύλα φτερά παγωνιού. Δύο επιγραφικές ζώνες, σε μαύρο βάθος αναγράφουν περσικό ποίημα σε μορφή *ρουμπάι* (τετράστιχο) που ήταν εξαιρετικά δημοφιλής και καθιερωμένη από τον 10ο αιώνα. Στο εσωτερικό υπάρχει ομάδα ψαριών.

en.name: Spouted jug
description:
The jug is covered with a transparent turquoise glaze and has two feline-shaped handles and two bullhead-shaped spouts. The designs are vertical compositions of leaf motives intercepted by curving peacock feathers.  
Two bands of inscriptions, *en reserve* on a black background read a Persian poem in the form of a *ruba\`i* (quatrain) that was a popular type of verse established by the end of the 10th century. The interior is with a group of fish.
keywords: Jug; Iran; Glaze; Persian poetry; Calligraphy motifs; Fish motifs
materials: Frit ware, underglaze painted in black
tags: Frit ware, underglaze painted in black

en.name: Coin
description: This gold Hashimi dinar was struck in Makkah around 1924, in the eighth year of the reign of Sharif Hussein bin Ali. Hussein, leader of the Arab Revolt, ruled the Hijaz from 1916 to 1924. The coin bears the date 1334 AH, the year of his accession and of the revolt, together with regnal year eight, making 1916 the founding moment of his rule. Its inscriptions name Makkah as the capital of the Arab Government and describe Hussein as the one who raises up the Arab lands. An earlier version of the coin had called him King of the Arab Lands, a title that angered rival rulers, especially Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud of Najd, and was later softened. In 1924, the same year this coin was struck, Abd al-Aziz began the conquest of the Hijaz that ended Hussein's reign.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
keywords: Mint; Coinage; Currency; Hijaz
partner: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection

en.name: Beirut Railway Station
description: This railway station, built during the Ottoman period, was the first railway station in Lebanon. It was a public station, intended for both for the transportation of passengers and trading goods.
artist: “Société des chemins de fer Ottomans économique de Beyrouth-damas-Hauran”
history: The Beirut-Damascus railway line, opened in 1895, was built across mountainous terrain to a 1,050 mm gauge. The second line from Riyaq to Aleppo, via Lebanon's eastern Beqaa valley, was also approved around this time. This was built to a standard gauge, even though it was only intended to provide a service between Damascus and Aleppo. The northern city of Tripoli was also connected via railway to Homs.
keywords: Commerce; Train station; Railway; Transportation; Trading

de.name: Tierteppich
description: Die Feldgestaltung dieses Teppichs ist einzigartig. Vier doppelköpfige Wesen dominieren das senkrechte Zentrum des Feldes. Eingebettet sind sie in cremefarbene Sternenformen. Die freien Flächen zwischen den Sternen sind mit mehrfarbigen Oktogonen gefüllt. Durch die spitz nach außen weisenden Sternenspitzen und die jeweils nach außen gerichteten Tierköpfe entwickelt der Teppich eine besondere Dynamik. Zwei technische Besonderheiten finden sich in diesem Stück. Zum einen sind die Knoten teilweise um eine Kette versetzt angeordnet, vermutlich, um die gewünschte Steigung der Diagonale zu erzielen. Ein weiterer Tierteppich (KGM 1888,112) des Museums für Islamische Kunst Berlin zeigt diese Technik. Eine Besonderheit sind die gelben Schüsse, die in regelmäßigen Abständen zusätzlich eingefügt wurden. Es wird vermutet, dass sie das Tagewerk einer Knüpferin / Knüpfers markieren. Diese Markierungen sind auch im sogenannten Drache-Phönix-Teppiche (I.4) des Museums für Islamische Kunst Berlin nachgewiesen.
holder: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Animal carpet
description: The field design of this carpet is exceptional. Four double-headed creatures dominate the vertical centre of the field. They are embedded in cream-coloured star forms. The free spaces between the stars are filled with multicoloured octagons. The star points directed outwards and the animal heads each also pointing outwards lend a special dynamic to the carpet. This piece displays two technical peculiarities. On the one hand, the knots are partly offset, presumably in order to achieve the desired incline of the diagonals. A further animal carpet (KGM 1888,112) in the Museum of Islamic Art in Berlin displays this technique. A special feature are the yellow wefts which are additionally inserted at regular intervals. It is assumed that they mark the day’s work of the weaver. These marks are also found in the so-called Dragon-Phoenix carpet (I.4) in the Museum of Islamic Art in Berlin.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Carpet; Animal Carpet; Bird; Wilhelm von Bode
materials: Wool, knotted pile carpet; symmetrical knot
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Qsar Ouled Soltane
description:
The Ouled Soltane are a faction of a sedentary Bedouin tribe. In imitation of the Jebaliya mountain dwellers who occupied the crests and isolated mountain-peaks, they ended up building their own collective grain loft. It is situated at a height about 20 km. south-east of Tataouine in the southern part of the Jabal Abiedh. From there one can make out from afar the remains of three pedestrian-only villages – Tazeghdanet, Banu Oussine and Techout – which all had citadel-lofts that have now fallen into ruin. As it was more accessible, the Qsar Ouled Soltane had come to replace them.  
The *qsar* is composed of a group of storage rooms, *ghorfas*, which are vaulted, over 300 in number, and piled one over the other across three or four levels around two central courtyards linked via a covered passageway. The first courtyard is over four centuries old whereas the second, clearly of a more recent date, was built on the eve of the Protectorate in 1881. The small ensilage cavities are deep and compartmentalised, allowing for the conservation of various kinds of foodstuffs like olives and grains. They are protected by low doors made of palm wood which are locked and bolted shut with wooden pegs; in order to open them, the key, also made of wood, must break the pegs. This ingenious device is commonly used in this region. Very steep cantilevered stairs lean procariously against the wall offering access to the *ghorfa*s on the floors above. To reach those not served by a staircase, one had to make do with several slabs of stone, cut so as to project outwards like steps, or simply planks of wood fixed onto the wall. Other planks fixed above the doors allow, through the pulling of a cord, for the containers, baskets or sacks of grain to be lifted up to the higher *ghorfa*s, to be conserved there. Hiding-places built into the vaults of adjoining rooms are accessible through small doors that open from outside, in the courtyard.  
Although partially deserted, the Qsar Ouled Soltane continues to attract the region’s inhabitants, whether they be mountain folk or men from the plain, so much so in fact that today it constitutes the centre of an embryonic village, which has progressively been building up around its double enclosure; a recently built mosque consecrates this birth. This *qsar*, which is periodically afforded restoration work, has been converted into a cultural centre which holds the annual festival of the *qsur*s, whatever its manifestation.

es.name: Ksar Ulad Soltan
description:
Los Ulad Soltan son una fracción de una tribu beduina sedentarizada. Al igual que los montañeses (*yebaliya*) que ocupan las crestas y los penachos, han terminado por construir su propio granero colectivo. Éste se sitúa sobre un alto a 20 km al sureste de Tatawin, en la parte sur del Yebel Abied. Desde lejos, se pueden entrever los vestigios de tres pueblos, Tazegdanet, Banu Ussin y Techut, provistos de graneros-ciudadelas derruidos. Más accesible, el *ksar* de los Ulad Soltan ha venido a reemplazarlos.  
Se trata de un conjunto de más de 300 celdas, *gurfa*s abovedadas apiladas unas sobre otras en tres o cuatro niveles, alrededor de dos patios centrales que se comunican por un paso cubierto. La primera, la del fondo, debe ser la más antigua, de más de cuatro siglos, mientras que la segunda, claramente más reciente, ha debido ser construida poco antes del Protectorado de 1881.  
Los alveolos del ensilado son profundos y compartimentados, lo que permite conservar diversos productos, como aceitunas o granos. Están protegidos por puertas bajas en madera de palmera, que se cierran con unos cerrojos con hebillas de madera. Para abrir, con una llave de madera, deben deshacerse las hebillas. Este ingenioso sistema es corriente en la región. Las escaleras son muy estrechas y están adosadas a los muros, o bien en puertas falsas que permiten acceder a las *gurfa*s de los pisos superiores. Para poder alcanzar aquellas *gurfa*s que no estén comunicadas de esta forma, se han añadido algunas piedras planas, en saliente de albañilería, o simplemente unas barras de madera fijadas al muro. Otras barras fijadas encima de las puertas permiten, tirando de una cuerda, subir los cofres o sacos de grano, destinados a ser conservados en las *gurfa*s superiores. Algunos pequeños escondrijos, dispuestos en las bóvedas de las celdas contiguas, son accesibles por pequeñas puertas que se abren al exterior en el patio.  
Aunque parcialmente reutilizado, el *ksar* Ulad Soltan continúa recibiendo gente de la región, ya sean montañeses u hombres de la planicie, aunque constituye actualmente el embrión del pueblo, que progresivamente se desarrolla alrededor de un doble recinto. Recientemente se ha construido una mezquita, lo que ha venido a consagrar el nacimiento de este pequeño pueblo. Este *ksar*, al que se han dedicado periódicamente esfuerzos de restauración, se ha convertido en un espacio cultural que alberga el festival anual de los *ksur*.

fr.name: Ksar Ouled Soltan
description:
Les Ouled Soltane sont une fraction de tribu bédouine sédentarisée.A l’instar des montagnards Jebaliya qui occupaient les crêtes et les pitons, ils ont fini par construire leur propre grenier collectif. Celui-ci est situé sur une éminence à 20 km au sud-est de Tataouine dans la partie sud du Djebel Abiedh.Au-delà, on entrevoit de loin les vestiges de trois villages piétonniers, Tazeghdanet, Beni Oussine et Techout, pourvus de greniers-citadelles, tombés aujourd’hui en ruine. Plus accessible, le ksar des Ouled Soltan est venu les remplacer.  
Il s’agit d’un ensemble de cellules d’engrangements, *ghorfa*s, voûtées, plus de 300, empilées les unes sur les autres sur trois ou quatre niveaux autour de deux cours centrales communiquant par un passage couvert. La première, celle du fond, serait âgée de plus de quatre siècles, alors que la seconde, nettement plus récente, aurait été construite à la veille du Protectorat, en 1881.  
Les alvéoles d’ensilage sont profondes et compartimentées, ce qui permet de conserver diverses denrées telles olives, grains... Elles sont protégées par des portes basses en bois de palmier, qui ferment par des verrous à chevilles en bois; pour ouvrir, la clé, également en bois, doit effacer les chevilles. Ce système ingénieux est courant dans cette région. Des escaliers très raides adossés aux murs ou en porte-à-faux permettent d’accéder aux *ghorfa*s des étages. Pour atteindre celles qui ne sont pas ainsi desservies, on se contente de quelques pierres plates saillant de la maçonnerie, ou tout simplement de barres en bois fichées dans le mur. D’autres barres fixées au-dessus des portes permettent, en tirant sur une corde, de soulever les contenants à grains, couffins ou sacs, destinés à être conservés dans les *ghorfa*s supérieures. Des cachettes ménagées dans les voûtes des cellules accolées sont accessibles par de petites portes qui ouvrent à l’extérieur, dans la cour.  
Bien que partiellement désaffecté, le Ksar Ouled Soltan continue d’attirer les habitants de la région, qu’ils soient montagnards ou hommes de la plaine, si bien qu’il constitue aujourd’hui le noyau d’un embryon de village qui s’est progressivement constitué autour de sa double enceinte; une mosquée, de construction récente, est venue consacrer cette naissance. Ce *ksar* auquel un effort de restauration est périodiquement consenti, s’est converti en espace culturel, abritant l’une ou l’autre manifestation du festival annuel des *ksour*.

en.name: *Keswa kabbous (wedding outfit)*
short_description: Worn by the bride during the wedding ceremony, the keswa kabous el-Jaraq weighs more than ten kilograms. It consists of a large, billowing pair of trousers secured at the waist by a tekka (similar to a ribbon), with a matching top, short enough to leave the waist uncovered, both made of silk taffeta. Its air of great wealth and elegance comes particularly from the contrast between the floral motifs, embroidered with a flat silver thread, and the sequins, also sewn on with a gold and silver thread. When worn by a seated bride, the trousers resemble a large hoop-skirt, connected to a low-necked bodice, which together give the impression of being a robe de cour (grand habit). The upper section of these trousers, hemmed at the waist but open at the front, consists of almost four metres of fabric, and the legs alone have a circumference of one and a half metres and are a metre long. The end of the legs is hemmed with some robust percale fabric, which contains the hemming and rises up the leg to create an even larger swell around the ankle.
keywords: Wedding outfit; embroidery with silver thread.
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Costume de mariage (*keswa kabbous*)
short_description: Porté par la mariée lors de la cérémonie nuptiale, ce grand costume appelé *keswa kabbous el-Garaq* pèse plus d’une dizaine de kilos. Il est composé d’un pantalon large, bouffant, serré à la taille par une *tekka*, sorte de cordon, accompagné d’un haut séparé laissant la taille dégagée, tous deux en taffetas de soie. Les broderies en fils d’argent dessinent des motifs floraux. L’association du fil d’argent plat brodé en relief et des paillettes cousues avec de la cannetille produit un effet de richesse et d’élégance. Porté par une femme assise, il prend l’allure d’une ample jupe à paniers raccordée au corsage décolleté, ce qui lui donne l’aspect d’une robe de cour. L’ampleur du haut du pantalon coulissé à la taille mais ouvert devant atteint les 4 mètres, les jambes à elles seules ont un tour de 1,50 mètre et 1 mètre de haut. Le bas des jambes est coulissé avec de la percale robuste qui maintient la coulisse et remonte assez haut sur la jambe pour provoquer le gonflement maximum autour de la cheville.
keywords: Costume de mariage; Broderie en fils d'argent
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: *The Railway Station at Jaffa*
short_description: *The Railway Station at Jaffa* is a drawing included in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. In the chapters about Jaffa and Jerusalem, the description of the geography, religious history and climate focuses on the route of the Jaffa–Jerusalem railway. It provides an interesting report on this communication route, built by the French and opened on September 1892, connecting Jaffa to Jerusalem and various villages in between.

ar.name: البركة الدائرية في جبل القلعة.
description: تقع البركة الدائرية إلى الشرق من البوابة الكبرى التي تؤدي إلى المجمع الأموي.  يبلغ عمق البركة 6 م وقطرها حوالي 17.5 م، وبالتالي يمكنها خزن 1300متر مكعب من المياه.  كانت البركة تزوَّد بمياه الأمطار عبر قنوات مغطاة يمكن مشاهدة بقاياها مع مصفاة في الجزء الواقع إلى الغرب من البركة.  ويلاحظ في بناء البركة وجود أسطوانات أعمدة وتيجان يبدو أنها أخذت من أبنية سابقة وأعيد استخدامها.  كذلك كان يغطي أرضية البركة وواجهات جدرانها المحيطة طبقة سميكة من المونة الكلسية العازلة للماء، بينما كان ينتصب في وسط البركة عمود لقياس ارتفاع المياه .  وبمحاذاة الواجهة الغربية للبركة تنحدر سلالم حجرية. إلى الشمال من البركة يوجد بئر عميق يبدو أنه كان واحداً من المصادر المائية التي تزود الحمام الواقع إلى الشرق من البوابة الكبرى بالمياه.  تذكرنا هذه البركة بالخزانات الدائرية الأغلبية في القيروان.

يقع صهريج الماء العائد لقلعة عمَّان، إلى الشرق من مجمع القصور الأموي. إنه دائري، بعمق 6 م، وقطر 17.5 م، وقابل لتخزين 1300 م3، من الماء. هذا الصهريج الذي يتغذَّى بقنوات إضافية موصولة بشبكة لجمع مياه المطر، كان المصدر المائي الأهمّ بالنسبة للقلعة. بعض العناصر المعمارية الأقدم، تمَّ إدخالها في جدار الصهريج، وهناك إسفين حجري عمودي أُعيد استخدامه مُفصّلاً في العمق. الجدار الداخلي مطلي بطبقة سميكة من الجصّ الهيدروليكي. ثمَّة درجات نافرة من الجانب الغربي، تقود إلى عمق الصهريج.
dates: غير معروف على وجه التأكيد، ربما ترجع إلى الفترة 105- 125 / 724 - 743.
artist: ربما يكون الخليفة هشام بن عبدالملك (حكم في الفترة 105- 125 / 724 - 743).

en.name: Citadel of Amman (Water Reservoir).
description: Within the Umayyad Citadel to the east of the palatial complex is a round water cistern, 6 m deep with a diameter that exceeds 17.5 m, and which could hold up to 1300 cu m of water. This cistern was the most important source of water at the Citadel. It was fed through inlet channels connected to a system for the collection of rainwater. These channels and the associated settling tank are partially preserved to the west of the cistern. Some earlier architectural elements including columns, shafts and capitals were incorporated into the wall of the cistern as building materials, such as the shaft of a stone column which was placed in the centre of the cistern and re-used as a depth gauge. The base and the walls were covered with a thick layer of hydraulic plaster which can still be seen. Stone steps along the western side lead down into the cistern. This access was necessary in order to clean the interior from the debris collected with the run-off water and to prepare the cistern for the rainy season. A deep well adjacent to the cistern from the north may be part of the water installations necessary to feed water to the bath complex located to the west of the citadel. This round cistern is closely related architecturally and stylistically to the local tradition of rectangular cisterns, despite the superficial similarity to the round Aghlabid cisterns found at Kairouan Tunisia

The water cistern on the Amman Citadel lies to the east of the Umayyad palatial complex. It is round, 6 m deep with a diameter of over 17.5 m, and could hold up to 1300 cu m of water. This cistern, fed by inlet channels connected to a rainwater collection system, was the most important source of water at the Citadel. Some earlier architectural elements were incorporated into the cistern wall, and a column shaft was re-used as a depth gauge. The interior was covered with a thick layer of hydraulic plaster. Stone steps along the western side led down into the cistern.

es.name: Aljibe de la ciudadela de Ammán.
description: Dentro de la ciudadela omeya, al este del complejo palaciego, hay un aljibe circular, de seis metros de profundidad y más de 17,5 m de diámetro, con capacidad para más de 1.300 metros cúbicos de agua. Este aljibe fue el principal recurso acuífero de la ciudadela; se llenaba a través de canales conectados a un sistema de recogida del agua pluvial. Estos canales y el depósito de filtrado aún se conservan parcialmente al oeste del aljibe. Algunos elementos arquitectónicos anteriores (columnas, fustes y capiteles) se usaron para construir el aljibe, como el fuste de una columna de piedra que se encontraba en el centro del aljibe y que se reutilizó como medidor de la profundidad. La base y las paredes se cubrieron con una fina capa de escayola hidráulica de la que aún quedan vestigios. Los escalones de piedra situados en el lado occidental conducen al fondo del aljibe, al que se bajaba para realizar labores de limpieza y extraer desechos durante las épocas del año en que el aljibe se preparaba para la estación de las lluvias. Al norte del aljibe hay un profundo pozo adyacente, que debió de formar parte de las instalaciones que suministraban agua a los baños ubicados al oeste de la ciudadela. Este aljibe circular está estrechamente relacionado, arquitectónica y estilísticamente, con los aljibes rectangulares tradicionales de la zona, a pesar de las similitudes superficiales que guarda con las cisternas aglabíes circulares de Kairuán (Túnez).

El aljibe de la ciudadela de Ammán, al este del complejo palaciego omeya, es circular, tiene 6 m de profundidad y un diámetro de 17,5 m. Su capacidad es de 1.300 m³. Se llenaba a través de canales conectados a sistemas de recolección de agua pluvial y era el principal suministro acuífero de la ciudadela. En la pared del aljibe se usaron elementos arquitectónicos anteriores; un fuste de columna se reutilizó como medidor de profundidad. El interior del aljibe estaba cubierto con una gruesa capa de escayola hidráulica. En el lado oeste hay escalones de piedra que conducían al fondo del aljibe.
dates: Alrededor del año 110 de la Hégira / 728 d. C.
keywords: Ciudadela de Ammán; complejo de baños; escayola hidráulica; complejo palaciego; medidor de la profundidad del agua; instalaciones hidráulicas.
