en.name: Ratification document of the Congress of Vienna (29 September 1814 – 9 June 1815)
short_description: At the Congress of Vienna (29 September 1814 to 9 June 1815), Austria fully restored its position as one of the great powers in Europe. It renounced the former Austrian territories in the Netherlands and South Germany and regained a number of North Italian possessions. The Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia, together with smaller North Italian territories like Tuscany, Modena, Piacenza, Parma and Guastalla – which came under control of Habsburg Archdukes – confirmed Austrian predominance in Northern and Central Italy.

en.name: Convent of the Lóios, or Convent of São João Evangelista
description:
"D. Rodrigo de Melo, the first Governor of Tangiers and Count of Olivença, began building work in 1485. At the end of 1491, he took Holy Orders, although the building work continued and was essentially completed in the first phase, when its patronage was taken over by the first Count of Tentúgal.  
The history of the Monastery and the deeds of its founder are inscribed on a stone in the form of an elegant tentshaped canopy held open by two angels to display the armorial bearings of the family and the inscription, which is to be seen on the left of the axial door, under the open portico.  
Both the main door and the atrium are Late Gothic, superbly executed and clearly inspired by Batalha.The Church, with depressed Gothic vaulting and bosses, has one single nave and five bays, the first of which coincides with the upper choir, where there is an exhibition of works of art belonging to the Cadaval family, which owns the church and town house next to it. In the apse chapel, the ribbed vaulting is denser for aesthetic reasons.  
As well as various Renaissance tombs, the church also contains a unique series of bronze memorials, specially commissioned for family graves, while others are in stone or in both stone and bronze. Those of D. Rodrigo de Melo and D. Isabel de Meneses are the oldest, both of them being depicted with great realism.  
The Capela de Nossa Senhora do Rosário contains the memorials of D. Branca de Vilhena and Rui de Sousa, the former with an architectural framework imitating a Late Gothic niche, and the latter with foliage around the inscription. The most beautiful memorial, depicting Rui Pais and his wife praying, was undoubtedly made in Hainaut and is currently to be found in the upper choir.  
The Monastery is built round a twostorey, vaulted cloister and was constructed in the first two decades of the 16th century; it is now largely occupied by a *pousada*.The emblematic, Alentejo *Mudejar* doorway to the Chapter House with its double tracery horseshoe arches is on the ground floor. It is surmounted by a representation of a stockade set in a medallion, the device of D. Rodrigo de Melo, which refers to his successful military campaigns in North Africa.  
Other Luso-Moorish elements are also to be seen in other parts of the building, such as the *lavabo* (wash room) and refectory."

en.name: *Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum*
short_description: Fantasy in Egyptian Gallery, the British Museum, by Duncan. A group of sculptures come to life. Closely modelled on the sculptures displayed in the British Museum. Assyrianising figures at rear left. At front right Ry yawns and rubs his eye.

en.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
short_description: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment in varying lengths and split on the front made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This knee-length piece comes from the Veles Region. It is abundantly adorned with embroidery above the lower hem and at the breasts. Embroidery was an inevitable part of decorating the majority of Macedonian folk costumes. The exquisite, meticulously executed embroidery applied on this tunic makes it a real work of art.
keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; costume; wedding; marriage
materials: Thick twill-weave woollen fabric decorated with braids

en.name: *Madonna and Child with St. Anne (dei Palafrenieri)*
description:
The painting was conceived as an altarpiece for the Chapel of the Confraternity of the Papal Grooms (who following the abolition of horseback retinues had the privilege of accompanying the Pope during ceremonies) located in Saint Peter's Basilica. Commissioned in 1605, it was delivered shortly afterward and placed on the altar, before being immediately removed and transferred to the nearby Church of St. Anne, protector of the Confraternity.  
Caravaggio was paid a meagre sum, which was increased by Cardinal Scipione Borghese, who purchased the canvas for his city residence. This masterpiece was famously refused by the Confraternity, which disapproved of the realism used in the portrayal of their patron, whose name (“Anne”) means “Grace” in Hebrew, her daughter Mary and the Baby Jesus, all in a simple background barely illuminated by a single ray of light.  
The painting highlights the role of Anne as the creator; she who destroys “evil” and the role of the Virgin Mary who, with Jesus, crushes the head of the serpent, the symbol of sin. The subject also touched on the debate of the Immaculate Conception, in relation to Mary as a person, conceived without original sin (the dogma was not settled until 8 December 1854) and was therefore central to the dispute that split Catholics and Protestants at the time. The combination of these elements, in particular the extreme humanisation with which Caravaggio depicted the Holy Family, resulted in the judgement that the work was not sufficiently decorous for a representation of holy subjects, particularly at the time of the Counter-Reformation.  
A recent restoration has thrown new light on the technique used by the artist, who did no preparatory drawings. Indeed, the analyses carried out have shown some limited traces of incisions around the figures.

This painting was commissioned by the Confraternity of the Papal Grooms for the Sant’Anna Chapel located in Saint Peter’s Basilica. Considered to be lacking in decorum, it was removed after a month to the nearby Church of St. Anne in the Vatican, and later displayed in Cardinal Scipione Borghese’s collection. The religious theme is dealt with in an innovative, strongly humanised way. Caravaggio’s use of light greatly influenced his contemporaries, even the more classical painters. This work is an example of the contrast between the artistic views of the Counter-Reformation and uninhibited taste of the collector.
keywords: Confraterniy; realism; Counter-Reformation; altarpiece; Christian themes; religious object

it.name: Madonna dei Palafrenieri
description:
Il dipinto fu concepito come pala d'altare della cappella dell'Arciconfraternita dei Palafrenieri (coloro che, prima dell'abolizione degli equipaggi a cavallo, avevano il privilegio di accompagnare il pontefice nelle cerimonie), situata nella basilica di San Pietro. Commissionata nel 1605, l'opera venne consegnata poco dopo; collocata sull'altare venne immediatamente rimossa, per essere trasferita  nella vicina chiesa di S. Anna, protettrice dell'Arciconfraternita. A Caravaggio venne corrisposta una somma esigua, incrementata dal cardinale Scipione Borghese che acquistò la tela per il suo palazzo di città. Il capolavoro è legato al celebre rifiuto da parte dell'Arciconfraternita, che non apprezzò il realismo reso nella raffigurazione della patrona *–* il cui nome 'Anna' ha in ebraico il significato di 'Grazia' -, di Maria sua figlia e del Bambino Gesù, inseriti in un semplice ambiente appena rischiarato da un raggio di luce. Il dipinto sottolinea dunque sia il ruolo di Anna come generatrice di colei che distrugge il 'male', sia quello di  Maria Vergine, che con Gesù schiaccia la testa del serpente, simbolo del peccato. Il soggetto inoltre interferiva con il dibattito sull'Immacolata Concezione, relativo a Maria come persona, concepita senza peccato originale (il dogma si concluderà solo l' 8 dicembre 1854) ed era dunque al centro delle dispute che all'epoca impegnavano i cattolici contro i protestanti. L'insieme di questi elementi, e soprattutto l'estrema umanizzazione con cui Caravaggio aveva rappresentato la Sacra Famiglia, determinarono il giudizio che l'opera fosse priva del sufficiente 'decoro', ritenuto necessario alla rappresentazione dei soggetti sacri, soprattutto nel periodo della Controriforma.  
Il recente restauro ha gettato nuova luce sulla tecnica dell'artista, che non eseguiva disegni preparatori: le analisi condotte hanno infatti evidenziato soltanto alcune tracce di incisioni in corrispondenza delle figure.

Il dipinto fu commissionato a Caravaggio dalla Confraternita dei Palafrenieri per la loro cappella di Sant'Anna nella basilica di San Pietro. Considerata non decorosa per il luogo, ne fu rimossa dopo appena un mese e collocata nella vicina chiesa di Sant'Anna in Vaticano e in seguito ricomparve esposta nella collezione del cardinale Scipione Borghese. Il tema religioso è interpretato in un modo innovativo, fortemente umanizzato. L'uso della luce da parte di Caravaggio influenzò fortemente gli artisti contemporanei, compresi i pittori di tendenze più classiciste. Attraverso quest'opera è possibile capire il contrasto tra le scelte artistiche della Controriforma e il gusto disinibito del collezionista.
keywords: Confraternita; realismo; Controriforma; pala d'altare; tematiche cristiane; oggetto religioso

ar.name: قارورة الحاج.
description:
تعتبر قوارير الحاج التي كانت تستخدم لنقل الماء البارد خلال الرحلات الطويلة، والتي كانت مصنوعة من الفخار المقولب غير المزجج إحدى اختصاصات الخزافين السوريين في الفترة المملوكية. درجت هذه القوارير القوية بشكل واسع خلال القرنين السابع والثامن/ الثالث عشر والرابع عشر، وقد تم إنتاجها بأعداد كبيرة في عدد كبير من الأفران السورية. صنعت هذه القوارير جميعاً بالطريقة نفسها: الجسم البصلي الشكل بطرفيه الواسعين كان ينتج بواسطة قالبين متطابقين، ثم تضاف العروتان على الكتفين، والفتحة الضيقة نسبياً. الزخارف المقولبة على الجسم متنوعة، تتضمن مشاهد صيد، ومخلوقات أسطورية، ونماذج زهرية، وتصاميم عقدية الشكل، وكتابات ورنوك أميرية كان المقصود منها تمييز مالكيها من الضباط المماليك الذين كانوا يحملونها.  
تم الكشف مؤخراً عن هذه القارورة بحالتها الفنية الجيدة، والموجودة في المتحف الوطني بحلب، خلال الحفريات السورية الألمانية المشتركة في قلعة حلب، وزخارفها غير معتادة، فهي تظهر هلالاً كبيراً أعلى قاعدة مصمتة مثلثة الشكل محاطة بزوج من السيوف ضمن حلية دائرية. الخلفية مغطاة بدوائر صغيرة مدموغة، والجزء العلوي من الحلية مفصول ومزين بالوريقات. تمتد الأشرطة المنقطة على طول الحواف الخارجية للجسم.  
من الواضح أن التركيب المركزي غير المعتاد يمثل رنكاً مملوكياً، على الرغم منه غير معروف بين رنوك الأمراء المماليك، وقد يكون نتيجة لسوء فهم أو لخيال خزاف جامح خلط الهلال مع رمز الكأس الدارج. ومن المحتمل أن يكون قد قُصد من هذه الزخارف أن تشبه الرنوك دون أن تكون كذلك. لم يتم إنتاج هذه القطعة بإتقان على الرغم من أن القالب نفسه قد تم استعماله على الوجهين كما هو معتاد، فالطبعة على الجانب الخلفي ليست في المركز تماماً.
قارورة حجّ، تعود للعصر المملوكي، وُجدت خلال حفرية أثرية في قلعة حلب. شكلها نموذجي، ومزخرفة بشعار غير مفهوم التفاصيل، وغير معروف، وليس له مرجع في علم الشعارات.
holder: القسم الإسلامي، المتحف الوطني في حلب.
place: على الرغم من أن هذه القارورة قد تم العثور عليها خلال أعمال التنقيب الأثرية في قلعة حلب، إلا أن مكان إنتاجها غير معروف، وقد يكون سوريا.
keywords: آنية فخارية؛ رنك؛ فخار؛ قارورة حاج؛ قولبة.

en.name: Pilgrim’s flask.
description:
One of the specialities of Mamluk Syrian potters was the unglazed moulded pilgrim's flasks for the transportation of cool water on long journeys. These sturdy flasks became extremely popular in the AH 7th and 8th / AD 13th and 14th centuries and were certainly produced by a number of Syrian kilns. They were all made in the same manner: the globular body with its flattened sides was created from two identical moulds; the two handles on the shoulders and the short slightly tapering mouthpiece were then added separately. The moulded decoration on the body is various, including hunting scenes, mythical creatures, floral motifs, knotted designs, inscriptions and heraldic emblems which, no doubt, were meant to identify the ownership of the Mamluk officers who carried them.  
This well-preserved pilgrim's flask from the National Museum of Aleppo was uncovered during the course of recent Syrian-German excavations at Aleppo Citadel. Its decoration is highly unusual: it shows a large crescent on top of a solid triangular base, flanked by a pair of swords inscribed in a roundel. The background is covered with small impressed circles. The upper segment of the roundel is separated and decorated with foliage. Knotted bands run along the outer edges of the body.  
The unusual central composition is obviously meant to represent a Mamluk blazon, albeit the emblem depicted here is completely unknown in the canon of Mamluk heraldry. It might possibly be the result of a misunderstanding or indeed an inspired fantasy of the potter who mixed the crescent with the more popular cup symbol. It is possible that these decorations were only meant to look like heraldic emblems without actually being such. The piece has not been produced very carefully: although the same mould was used on both sides as usual, the impression on the back is seriously off centre.

This pilgrim's flask from the Mamluk period was found during recent excavations in the Citadel of Aleppo. Although its shape is typical, its decoration is highly unusual as the emblem is unknown in the repertory of Mamluk heraldry.
holder: National Museum of Aleppo, Islamic Department.
place: Although this flask was discovered during an archaeological excavation at Aleppo Citadel, its place of production is unknown, but it was possibly produced in Syria.
keywords: pilgrim flasks; canteen; earthenware; pottery; moulded; emblem; pilgrimage

es.name: Cantimplora de peregrino.
description:
Una de las especialidades de los alfareros mamelucos sirios eran las cantimploras de peregrino moldeadas y sin vidriar que servían para transportar agua fresca en los viajes largos. Estas resistentes botellas se hicieron muy populares en los siglos VII / XIII y VIII /XIV, y se sabe que se fabricaban en muchos hornos sirios. La elaboración seguía siempre el mismo proceso: el cuerpo globular de lados aplanados se fabricaba con dos moldes idénticos; las dos asas de la parte superior y la boca, corta y ligeramente apuntada, se añadían más adelante. La decoración moldeada de la panza es muy variada y puede presentar desde escenas de caza, seres mitológicos, motivos florales o patrones con nudos, hasta inscripciones y emblemas heráldicos que sin duda servían para indicar que eran propiedad de los oficiales mamelucos que las portaban.  
Esta cantimplora de peregrino del Museo Nacional de Alepo, muy bien conservada, se descubrió durante las recientes excavaciones sirias y alemanas en la ciudadela de Alepo. Su decoración es muy inusual: presenta una gran media luna sobre una sólida base triangular flanqueada por dos espadas, todo ello inscrito en un medallón. El fondo está cubierto con pequeños círculos impresos. La sección superior del medallón está separada y adornada con motivos vegetales. A lo largo de los bordes exteriores del cuerpo corren bandas decoradas con nudos.  
Resulta evidente que esta infrecuente composición central representa un blasón mameluco, aunque el emblema que aquí aparece no se encuentra entre los tipificados en la heráldica mameluca. Podría ser fruto de una confusión o quizás de una fantasía creativa del alfarero, que unió la media luna con el popular símbolo de la copa. Es posible que esta decoración sólo tratase de recordar los emblemas heráldicos sin serlo. La pieza no se elaboró con demasiada meticulosidad: aunque se empleó el mismo molde para los dos laterales, como era costumbre, la impresión de la parte trasera está claramente descentrada.

Esta cantimplora de peregrino se encontró en excavaciones recientes efectuadas en la ciudadela de Alepo y data del periodo mameluco. Aunque la forma es típica, posee una decoración poco común, ya que el emblema que presenta no está entre los símbolos conocidos de la heráldica mameluca.
holder: Museo Nacional de Alepo (Departamento de Arte Islámico).
dates: Siglo VIII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.
place: Pese a que esta cantimplora se encontró en la alcazaba de Alepo durante unas excavaciones arqueológicas, se desconoce su lugar de producción, aunque posiblemente se fabricó en Siria.
keywords: Cantimplora de peregrino; barro cocido; cerámica; moldeado; emblema.

fr.name: Gourde de pèlerin.
description:
Ce type de gourde de pèlerin en terre cuite moulée non vernie pour le transport de l'eau fraîche lors de longs voyages était l'une des spécialités des potiers syriens de la période mamelouke. Ces flasques trapues, très populaires aux VIIe et VIIIe siècles H (XIIIe et XIVe siècles J.-C.), furent certainement produites en grand nombre dans les fours syriens. Elles étaient toutes fabriquées de la même manière : le corps globuleux aplati était coulé à l'aide de deux moules identiques, les deux bélières et le court goulot évasé ajoutés dans un second temps. Le décor moulé sur la panse est varié et pouvait représenter des scènes de chasse, des créatures fabuleuses, des motifs floraux, des motifs tressés, des inscriptions et des emblèmes héraldiques qui, sans aucun doute, identifiaient les officiers mamelouks qui les portaient.  
Cette gourde bien conservée a été découverte lors de récentes fouilles syro-germaniques dans la citadelle d'Alep. Son décor est très inhabituel. Il présente au sommet un grand croissant sur une base triangulaire, flanqué de deux paires d'épées dans un rondeau. Le fond est recouvert de petits cercles estampés. La partie supérieure du rondeau est séparée et décorée de feuillage. Des bandeaux nattés courent sur les côtés de la panse.  
La curieuse composition centrale tend certainement à représenter un blason mamelouk, bien que l'emblème représenté soit complètement inconnu de l'héraldique mamelouke. Il peut être le fruit d'une erreur ou une fantaisie de potier qui a mélangé le croissant au symbole plus répandu de la coupe. Il est possible que ces ornements n'aient été créés que pour évoquer des emblèmes héraldiques sans en être réellement. Cette pièce a été produite sans beaucoup de soin. Bien que le même moule ait servi pour les deux côtés, le décor du revers est sérieusement décentré.

Cette gourde de pèlerin de la période mamelouke a été découverte lors de fouilles récentes dans la citadelle d'Alep. Bien que la forme soit typique, sa décoration est très inhabituelle et son emblème est inconnu de la héraldique mamelouke.
dates: VIIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIVe siècle J.-C.).
place: Bien que cette gourde ait été découverte lors de fouilles archéologiques menées dans la citadelle d'Alep, son lieu de production reste inconnu. Il peut s'agir d'une production syrienne.
keywords: Gourdes de pèlerin ; terre cuite ; poterie ; moulage ; emblèmes

en.name: Nossa Senhora do Pranto (Parish Church)
names: Nossa Senhora do Pranto (Vila Nova de Foz Côa Parish Church)
description: Built at the beginning of the 16th century, the Church has altered over time and today it only retains the original façade. The building is highly influenced by the style prevalent in neighbouring Castile, as can be seen by the brattishing with three openings for the bells and a Renaissance garland. The portal is Naturalist Manueline, with small columns framing the *archivolts* and the *pinnacle* with the royal arms and Manueline armillary sphere.

en.name: Santa Cruz (Parish Church)
names: Santa Cruz (Praia da Vitória Parish Church)
description: The Parish Church has retained a number of Manueline characteristics, though most of the building dates from the 18th century. It has interesting naturalistic decorative elements and anthropomorphic figures. Inside, the side chapels of São Francisco and Senhor dos Aflitos have entrance arches bordered with a carved-rope design, and depressed rib vaults, with crosses, escutcheons and intermediate ribs forming quatrefoils, together with curved segments. The main portal, built in 1517 according to the date on the front of the church, has naturalistic elements and also a conical canopy, in the mid-15th-century Batalha style.

en.name: Lisbon Astronomical Observatory
short_description: The Lisbon Astronomical Observatory is the Portuguese national observatory. It has the legal responsibility of national timekeeping. It is located in the Tapada da Ajuda, a green area in the west of Lisbon. It is part of the Museums of the University of Lisbon/National Museum of Natural History and Science. It includes several buildings. It promotes activities regarding the public understanding of astronomy and astrophysics for diverse audiences. The Observatory has important collections: scientific instruments, mostly from the 19th and early 20th century; a Library, which is reference in Portugal, and an important historical archive.
holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon
artist: Architects: Jean François Gille Colson, José da Costa Sequeira (1800–1872), Valentim José Correia (1822–1900); Engineer: Frederico Augusto Oom (1830–1890)
history: The Observatory was constructed with the support and sponsorship of King Pedro V (1837–1861). It began operating in 1867 and its first director was Frederico Oom, followed by Campos Rodrigues (1836–1919), an internationally recognised astronomer and a creator of several scientific instruments. In 1995, the Observatory integrated the University of Lisbon.
keywords: Observatory; Scientific Heritage; Astronomy; National Museum of Natural History and Science; University of Lisbon

en.name: *The Ruins of the Temple of the Sun at Baalbec*
short_description: This dramatic view looks across the great court of the temple complex in Baalbek. In the ancient world Baalbek, to the east of Beirut in Lebanon, was a great centre of trade between Europe and Asias, and home to a religion of sun worship. The Scottish artist David Roberts visited in 1839 and over the following years made many images of the still imposing ruins. This painting is Roberts's last of Baalbek, and he considered it as 'a grand finale' to his career as a painter of the Middle East. The complex's imposing architectural and artistic details also inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam. Since about 1864 many tourists visited the famed site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II on his way to Jerusalem. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulously presented and illustrated publication that further raised interest in Baalbek.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority

en.name: St George Greek Orthodox Cathedral
description: The Cathedral's main plan is rectangular, and approximately 30 metres long by 20 metres wide. The nave itself is 30 metres long by 7.5 metres wide and is subdivided into five bays, which are then subdivided into three aisles. These aisles are divided by eight impressive sandstone piers measuring approximately 8.5 metres in height, with square divisions, chamfered sides and protruding bases. The central aisle is a barrel vault intersected by a vaulted transept. Light which filters through the upper windows shines on the frescoes which cover the vaulted ceiling. The cathedral has three altar spaces, built into three semi-circular alcoves. Finally, the cathedral is most famous for the half-vaulted painted dome above the central apse, in the central aisle.
history: The final modifications to the cathedral's structure were completed in 1910, with its enlargement eastwards and westwards, the addition of a vaulted portico on the south facade and moving the bell tower to the south-east corner. The interior of the Church is decorated with frescoes donated by Ibrahim Yussef Saad.
keywords: Greek; Orthodox; Church; Cathedral; Religion; Beirut

en.name: Dr Charles Nicolle
short_description: This is a photograph of the Nobel Prize for Medicine won by Dr Charles Nicolle for his work on infectious illnesses during his time at l'Institut Pasteur from 1903 to 1936.
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Docteur Charles Nicolle, prix Nobel de médecine
short_description: Photo d’archive du docteur Charles Nicolle procédant à la vaccination des enfants de la population autochtone. Durant sa carrière à l’institut Pasteur (1903-1936), il œuvra à prévenir et éradiquer les maladies infectieuses.
keywords: Médecins en Tunisie; Hôpital; Vaccination
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: *Magnificent Atrium with Figures*
description:
The growing influence and interaction between communications, especially the printing press and foreign travel, reinforced the cosmopolitan culture that came to characterise the processes of the European courts. Lisbon took the lead, when, under the reign of the King João V, Absolutism gave the Portuguese monarchy a renewed lease of life. Sacred and profane music, heard either at the Patriarch or at court, had a strong political meaning and reinforced the king's aura of majesty. King João V, therefore, commissioned artists such as Domenico Scarlatti; built the monumental Opera House next to the Royal Palace in 1754 (destroyed during the earthquake of 1755), and enlarged the Royal Orchestra with new foreign soloists.  
The theatrical scenery drawings of the Galli Bibiena family were not made on durable material. Due to the fact that the theatre sets they designed for court functions were temporary, few of their creations have survived. The richness and splendour of their stage sets can however still be judged from contemporary drawings, preserved in great numbers, and found mainly in collections in [Vienna](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna"), [Munich](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich") and [Dresden](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dresden "Dresden").  
This drawing by Francesco Galli Bibiena is a study for an unknown stage set. It is possible that it was brought to Portugal in 1750–1751 by his son, Giovanni Carlo Sicino Bibiena (1717–1760), who was charged by King José I to modernise both the theatres themselves and their services.  
The drawing shows an interior space with large arcades seen from a diagonal perspective. The composition is dominated by two large arches leading up to corridors at the top of a staircase. The vaults are richly decorated and the balconies bear several medallions with mythological figures at the centre supported by little angels. Bound by columns and female sculptures, the central area is occupied by women with children. Two dogs can be seen on the left. Through the main arcade a young crowned ruler makes his entrance surrounded by soldiers carrying banners, attracting everyone's attention.

This drawing by Francesco Galli Bibiena is a study for an unknown stage set. It represents an interior space with large arcades seen from a diagonal perspective. The vaults are richly decorated and the balconies bare several medallions with mythological figures at the centre supported by angels.
place: Royal Academy of Fine Arts, Lisbon, 1884
keywords: Bibiena; architectural perspective; corner perspective; theatre; Bologna; stage-set, drawing; scenography
materials: Pen and brown ink with green and brown wash on paper
tags: Pen and brown ink with green and brown wash on paper

pt.name: *Átrio Magnifico com Figuras*
description:
A crescente influência e a interacção dos meios de comunicação reforçou a cultura cosmopolita que caracterizou o processo civilizacional das cortes europeias, a que Lisboa não ficou alheia, dando um novo impulso à monarquia portuguesa.  
Tanto na corte de D. João V como na Patriarcal, a música, sagrada e profana, revestiu-se de um forte significado político, reforçando a aura majestática do rei, que, por esta razão, contratou artistas como Domenico Scarlatti, mandou construir a Casa da Ópera, junto ao Palácio Real, em 1754 (destruída no terramoto de Lisboa de 1755) e estimulou o alargamento da Orquestra Real com novos solistas vindos do estrangeiro.  
Os trabalhos da família Galli-Bibiena, na área da cenografia teatral, não eram executados em material durável. Devido ao carácter temporário das decorações para as festividades de corte, poucas das suas criações sobreviveram; contudo, a riqueza e o esplendor das suas obras podem avaliar-se pelos desenhos feitos naquele tempo, muitos deles preservados até hoje e conservados, maioritariamente, nas colecções de Viena, Munique e Dresden.  
Este desenho, executado por Francesco Galli Bibiena, é um estudo para um cenário não identificado. É possível que tenha entrado em Portugal em 1750-51 pela mão do seu filho, Giovanni Carlo Sicino Bibiena (1717-1760), encarregado pelo rei D. José I de modernizar os teatros e os serviços teatrais.  
Representa um espaço interior com grandes arcadas vistas em perspectiva diagonal. A composição é dominada por dois grandes arcos que conduzem a largos corredores no cimo de uma escadaria. As abóbadas são profusamente decoradas e as balaustradas apresentam vários medalhões, com figuras mitológicas ao centro, suportadas por pequenos anjos. O espaço central, rodeado de colunas e de esculturas femininas, é ocupado por senhoras e crianças, sendo mesmo possível observar dois cães, à esquerda. Um jovem monarca faz a sua entrada pela arcada principal, rodeado de soldados carregando estandartes, olhando e apontando para os súbditos, atraindo assim a atenção de todos.

Este desenho de Francesco Galli Bibiena é um estudo para um cenário não identificado. Representa um espaço interior com grandes arcadas vistas em perspectiva diagonal. As abóbadas são profusamente decoradas e as balaustradas têm vários medalhões, com figuras mitológicas ao centro, sustentadas por anjos.
place: Academia Real de Belas Artes, Lisboa, 1884.
keywords: Bibiena; arquitectura; teatro; Bolonha; cenografia; desenho
materials: Pena e tinta castanha, com aguada verde e castanha, sobre papel.
tags: Pena e tinta castanha, com aguada verde e castanha, sobre papel.

en.name: *The Adoration of the Shepherds*
description:
This bas-relief is part of a series which includes four horizontal and four oval scenes, all are in their original frames.  
Three shepherds approach to adore the Child. The Madonna, St. Joseph and the angels, occupying the middle of the scene, point to the object of interest, Jesus. Piò moulds the tender scene to create a soft and delicate three-dimensional picture, similar to his contemporary painters.

This sculpture is a good example of the baroque technique of Bolognese terracotta. Terracotta bas-reliefs were intended as proper paintings, framed and hanging from the walls, but lacking colours. The figures are scattered on different planes; in the foreground they are nearly three dimensional while the background figures are drawn more two dimensionally.
holder: Museo Diocesano di Arte Sacra di San Giovanni in Persiceto
keywords: Angelo Gabriello Piò; *Adoration of the Sheperds*; Baroque sculpture; Religious object; Terracotta; Christian themes; bas-relief
partner: Museums' System of the Province of Bologna

it.name: Adorazione dei pastori
description:
Questo bassorilievo è parte di una serie (quattro scene orizzontali e quattro ovali) tutti ancora nelle cornici originali.  
I tre pastori si avvicinano per adorare il Bambino mentre la Madonna, S. Giuseppe e gli angeli, al centro della scena, indicano il centro dell'attenzione, Gesù. Piò modella la terracotta in modo da ottenere un dipinto tridimensionale morbido e delicato, non molto diverso dai risultati che nello stesso periodo erano raggiunti dai pittori suoi contemporanei.

Questa scultura è un buon esembpio della pratica bolognese della lavorazione della  terracotta. I bassorilievi in terracotta era intesi come veri e propri dipinti, incorniciati ed appesi alle pareti, ma privi della policromia. Le figure sono distribuite su piani diversi, dal primo piano, dove sono quasi tridimensionali, alle figure dello sfondo, più disegnate che scolpite.
holder: Museo diocesano di Arte Sacra di San Giovanni in Persiceto
keywords: Angelo Gabriello Piò; *Adorazione dei Pastori*; Scultura barocca; oggetto religioso; Terracotta; tematiche cristiane; bassorilievo

en.name: Petrie Stereo Photobook 1
short_description: Petrie was a pioneer of archaeological photography, even though at the time the technique of half-toning had not been developed, so that his photographs had to be turned into woodcuts for publication. He was a great believer in the importance of photography, and, at least at this time, took all of his archaeological photographs as stereo pairs, another of his pioneering works.
keywords: archaeology

en.name: *Fall of Stalać*
short_description:
Having mastered the cobbling trade and after studying theology, in 1873, the Serb Đorđe Krstić went to further his education at the Munich Art Academy thanks to a scholarship from the Knez that came after he had prepared for admission to an arts and crafts school. By 1920, there were approximately 50 Serbian students enrolled there. Though pieces from his Munich phase measure up to the best works of the time, a later painting by this historical and genre artist is better suited here. After the initial, strong influence of realism, on his return to Belgrade, in 1883, he endeavoured to present an open manner of painting, with strong and coloristic effects.  
Stalać was one of the largest fortified towns in Serbia in the Middle Ages, serving simultaneously as a checkpoint on the approaches to the then capital Kruševac and to strategically important valleys. At the same time as four other forts, Stalać was burned down and laid to waste in 1413, in initial raids by the Ottoman Turks, who subsequently conquered Serbia in 1459.  
This painting was commissioned by King Aleksandar Obrenović for the 1900 Paris Exposition. However, the committee rejected it before the Expo for an excessively extreme depiction of fighting. When the painting was exhibited in the National Museum in Belgrade in 1901, 1,000 visitors flocked to see it every day.
keywords: Historical Painting

ar.name: سجادة صلاة.
description:
يسيطر على هذه السجادة ألوان الأحمر والبني والأبيض، وهي مخصصة للصلاة بسبب وجود شكل المحراب ضمن الحقل المستطيل المركزي، ويعلو المحراب قوس مدبب متدرج تحيط به أزهار القرنفل، وتحت القوس، تظهر الزخارف الهندسية على أرضية من البني الفاتح، وقد تمت الاستعاضة عن القنديل الذي يظهر عادة في سجاد الصلاة بعنصر زخرفي زهري، أما أعلى القوس فقد تم ملء المساحة بأربع باقات من الأزهار الحمراء اللون. تظهر لوحتان عرضيتان واحدة فوق قمة القوس وواحدة تحت المحراب، ويظهر على كلتيهما التصميم نفسه المؤلف من شريط متموج وزهيرات تملأ المساحات. يحيط بالحقل المركزي الصغير إطار عريض مؤلف من صف داخلي وخارجي من أزهار القرنفل المجردة وسبعة أشرطة ضيقة ملونة بالتناوب بالأبيض والأحمر.  
تركز إنتاج هذا النوع من سجاد الصلاة في مكانين في تركيا هما غوردس وكولا، وتجمع هذه السجادة عناصر من كليهما، فعلى سبيل المثال هناك الأشرطة السبعة الضيقة الموجودة في السجاد المنتج في كول، والمحراب مع اللوحتين العرضيتين وتركيبة الألوان التي يسيطر عليها اللون الأحمر التي تميز سجاد الصلاة المنتج في غوردس.

هذا البساط مكرس للصلاة لأنه مزين في وسطه المستطيل بمحراب. أما الشكل النباتي في الفراغ الكائن تحت القوس فيحل محل المصباح الذي كثيراً ما يُرى في بسط الصلاة. نرى الامتداد المركزي مؤطراً بسلسلة من القرنفلات المنمطة وسبعة خطوط رفيعة.
keywords: دين؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ سجادة صلاة؛ صلاة؛ طهارة.

en.name: Prayer rug.
description:
This rug, dominated by the colours red, brown and white, is dedicated to prayer because of its niche motif in the central rectangular field. The niche is formed by a stepped, pointed arch and edged all around with carnations. A geometrical ornament is set against the light brown background of the area below the arch. A floral device replaces the lamp often to be seen in other prayer rugs. The spandrels are filled with five red flowering bushes. There are two transverse panels, one above the spandrels and one below the niche. Both show the same motif of a cloud-band in combination with rosette blossoms filling the spaces. The small central field is framed by a broad border consisting of an inner and an outer row of heavily stylised carnations and seven narrow stripes coloured alternately white and red.  
There were two places, Ghiordes (Gördes in Turkish) and Kula, manufacturing prayer rugs of similar patterns. This rug combines characteristic elements of both: for example, the seven narrow stripes are found in Kula prayer rugs and the niche with two transverse panels and a colour scheme dominated by red are typical of Ghiordes prayer rugs.

Rug dedicated to prayer because of the niche motif in the central rectangular field. The floral device in the area below the arch replaces the lamp often to be seen in other prayer rugs. The central field is framed by a border of stylised carnations and seven narrow stripes.
keywords: Prayer rug; religion; prayer; floral decoration; purity

es.name: Alfombra para el rezo.
description:
Alfombra decorada principalmente en rojo, marrón y blanco. El nicho central indica que era utilizada para el rezo. El nicho presenta un arco apuntado escalonado, rodeado de claveles. La ornamentación geométrica destaca sobre un fondo marrón claro que se aprecia tras el arco. El motivo en forma de lámpara es remplazado por un elemento floral, muy habitual en otras alfombras. Los tímpanos están decorados con arbustos con flores rojas. Los dos paneles transversales, uno encima de los tímpanos y otro bajo el nicho, están decorados con el mismo motivo de una cenefa de nubes combinada con rosetas. El pequeño espacio central está enmarcado con un borde ancho formado por dos filas de claveles muy estilizados y siete estrechas bandas que alternan el blanco y rojo.  
Estas alfombras se producían en Ghiordes (Gördes en turco) y Kula. Este ejemplo combina elementos característicos de ambos lugares; por ejemplo: las sietes bandas muy estrechas son típicas de Kula; por otro lado, el nicho con los paneles transversales y la composición cromática dominada por el color rojo son también típicos de Kula.

Alfombra con nicho en el campo rectangular central. La característica lámpara que decora la parte inferior de este tipo de alfombras, se sustituye aquí por un elemento floral. El campo central está enmarcado con un borde de claveles estilizados y siete bandas estrechas.
dates: Siglo XIII de la Hégira/ XIX d.C.
keywords: alfombra para el rezo; religión; oración; decoración floral; pureza

fr.name: Tapis de prière
description:
Ce tapis aux couleurs dominantes rouge, brun et blanc est consacré à la prière, comme l'indique son motif central en forme de niche. Celle-ci est délimitée par un arc brisé en degrés, bordé tout autour d'œillets. Un ornement géométrique figure dans le champ brun clair délimité par l'arc. Un autre ornement, de type floral, remplace la lampe souvent observée dans les tapis de prière. Les écoinçons sont occupés par cinq buissons fleuris rouges. Le champ central est encadré en haut et en bas par deux cartouches rectangulaires transversaux. Tous deux sont ornés du motif identique d'un bandeau de nuages combiné à des rosettes. Le champ central, réduit, est encadré d'une large bordure consistant en un rang intérieur et extérieur d'œillets très stylisés et sept étroites bandes de couleur rouges et blanches alternées.  
Deux centres, Ghiordès (Gördes en turc) et Kula, fabriquaient des tapis de prière de modèle similaire. Ce tapis contient des éléments des deux provenances. Par exemple, les sept bandes étroites sont caractéristiques de Kula ; la niche entre deux cartouches ainsi que la gamme de couleurs sont typiques de Ghiordès.

Tapis consacré à la prière, ainsi que le montre le motif de niche dans son champ rectangulaire central. La composition florale sous l’arc remplace la lampe souvent présente dans d’autres tapis de ce type. Le champ central est encadré d’une bordure d’œillets stylisés et de sept minces bandeaux.
dates: XIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIXe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: Tapis de prière; religion; prières; décoration florale; pureté.

en.name: *Mahbes* floral bowl
description: This bowl, *mahbes*, has a *tawq* (collar) and lotus flower design. It is intended for washing, salted meat preparation, bread dough, or couscous. Beginning in the 18th century, workshops in Qallaline, Tunisia, reached an apogee, marked by a mastery of colour and a variety of compositions.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Cuvier à décor floral *mahbes*
description:
Ce cuvier, *mahbes*, se compose d'un décor *tawq* (collier) et de fleurs de lotus. Il est destiné soit à la lessive, soit à la préparation des salaisons, de la pâte à pain ou du couscous.  
A compter du XVIIIe siècle J.-C., les ateliers de Qallaline en Tunisie connaissent une période d'apogée, marquée par une habileté dans la maîtrise des couleurs et des compositions variées.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: XIe siècle de l'Hégire / XVIIe siècle J.-C.
materials: Pâte argileuse, décor peint sur glaçure opaque
tags: Pâte argileuse, décor peint sur glaçure opaque

en.name: Bottle with bulbous neck
description: This ceramic bottle with a long neck with ovoid spout has a shallow moulded and incised decoration under glaze. A gadroon frieze (ornamental series of convex forms) belts the shoulder.
holder: Museum of the Arab word Institute
dates: Hegira end of 7th century - beginning of 8th century / AD end of 13th century - beginning of 14th century
materials: Siliceous clay; moulded design under monochrome glaze
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Bouteille à col renflé
description: Cette bouteille en céramique à long col à déversoir ovoïde présente un décor légèrement moulé et incisé sous glaçure. Une frise de godrons ceinture l'épaulement.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: AH fin du 7ème siècle - début du 8ème siècle / AD fin du 13ème siècle - début du 14ème siècle

ar.name: زهرية.
description: زهرية بعنق واسع وجسم بصلي الشكل وقاعدة منخفضة تتجه نحو الخارج. يوجد شريط ضيق حول العنق، مزين بنموذج ضفيرة، يقسم الزهرية إلى منطقتين مختلفتي الزخرفة. لقد تم ملء المنطقتين بالنماذج الزهرية ذات اللون الأحمر والأخضر والأزرق، وهي تتألف من القرنفل والخزامى والزهرة الياقوتية، وتنبثق جميعها من أطراف أغصان ملتفة بنعومة. يميز اللون الأخضر الزمردي فخار إزنيق في أوجه خلال سبعينات القرن السادس عشر، فبعد هذه الفترة، أدى التراجع في رعاية الفنون، بالإضافة إلى عوامل أخرى إلى تراجع صناعة الفخار العثمانية من الناحية الاقتصادية والجمالية، وتعتبر هذه الزهرية مثالاً رائعاً على الخزف العثماني في القرن السادس عشر وهو في أوج ازدهاره.
إناء للزهور، ذو شكل بصلي منتفخ، مُزخرف بزخارف نباتية مُتكرِّرة، وجميعها زخارف لمشاهد طبيعية. يدلُّ الإستخدام الأنيق للونين الأحمر والأخضر على أن هذه القطعة صُنعت في فترة إزدهار صناعة فخار إزنيق.
keywords: زخرفة زهرية؛ خزامي

en.name: Vase.
description: A vase with a wide neck, bulbous body, and low flaring foot. A narrow collar around the neck, decorated with a braided rope design, divides the vase into two areas of decoration. Both are filled with floral motifs in red, green, and blue. These include carnations, tulips, and hyacinths, all of which are shown blossoming at the ends of gently undulating green stems. The use of a brilliant emerald green is characteristic of Iznik ceramics at their peak of quality, in the 1570s. Shortly thereafter, slackening patronage and other factors led the Ottoman ceramic industry to economic and aesthetic decline. This vase, then, is a splendid token of the high point of 16th-century Ottoman ceramics.

A bulbous vase decorated with floral motifs which, rather than functioning as mere repeat units, are freely rendered and almost naturalistic. The use of brilliant red and emerald-green indicates that this vase was made at the height of the classical Iznik pottery industry.
keywords: floral decoration; hyacinths; patronage

es.name: Jarrón
description: Jarrón con cuello ancho, cuerpo bulboso y pie anular no muy alto. Una estrecha cenefa de cuerda trenzada divide en dos la superficie. Los dos espacios resultantes están decorados con motivos florales en rojo, verde y azul: claveles, tulipanes y jacintos en flor que nacen de tallos verdes ondulantes. El esmaltado verde esmeralda brillante es característico de la época de mayor calidad de la cerámica de Iznik y otomana en general, los años setenta del siglo XVI, de la que este jarrón es un espléndido ejemplo. Poco después, la industria cerámica otomana entró en una etapa de declive económico y estético debido a varios factores, entre ellos la disminución del número de encargos.

Jarrón de cuerpo bulboso decorado con motivos florales que, más que simple repetición de un dibujo, forman una composición libre y casi naturalista. El uso de rojo y verde esmeralda brillantes indican que esta pieza corresponde al momento álgido de la alfarería clásica de Iznik.
dates: Alrededor de 975 de la Hégira / 1575 d. C.
keywords: decoración floral; jacintos

fr.name: Vase.
description: Vase à large col, panse bulbeuse et petit pied évasé. Un étroit anneau autour du col, décoré d'un motif de corde tressée, divise l'objet en deux zones de décoration, toutes deux animées de motifs floraux en rouge, vert et bleu. Les fleurs sont des œillets, des tulipes et des jacinthes s'ouvrant à l'extrémité de tiges vertes délicatement incurvées. L'utilisation d'un vert émeraude brillant est caractéristique de la céramique d'Iznik à son apogée qualitatif, dans les années 1570. Peu après, le ralentissement des commandes et d'autres facteurs conduisirent à un déclin économique et esthétique de l'industrie de la céramique ottomane. Ce vase est un splendide exemple de cet art à son sommet.

Vase à panse bulbeuse décoré de motifs floraux qui, loin d'être de simples éléments répétitifs, sont d'un rendu très libre, presque naturaliste. L'usage du rouge brillant et du vert émeraude indique que ce vase a été fabriqué au sommet de l'art céramique classique d'Iznik.
keywords: Décoration florale; jacinthes

en.name: Qal‘at Salah al-Din
description:
The Castle of Salah al-Din, considered one of the most elaborate of the Eastern Mediterranean, is an example of Byzantine, Frankish, Ayyubid and Mamluk military architecture. Located in the northern part of western Syria, about 30 km north-east of the Port of Latakia along the northern buttress of the Alawite coastal mountains, it controlled the road between Latakia and the northern Ghab Plains. This castle was mostly a county residence rather than a garrison citadel.  
Appearing in the historical sources during the 4th/10th century, the Byzantines occupied the site until the end of the 5th/11th century and launched ambitious fortification campaigns. Kept for a short time by the Seljuqs, the castle was then conquered by the Crusaders between 507/1114 and 513/1119 and granted as a fief to the knight, Robert, son of Foulques and his successors. Significant improvements were made to the castle fortifications possibly with the help of the military orders. It was finally conquered by Salah al-Din in 584/1188 and subsequently granted as an *iqtâ‘* to the Mengüverish *emirs*. Following the Mongol menace of the mid 7th/13th century, the Mamluk Sultan Baybars recovered the castle peacefully in 671/1272, and granted it to the governor in his charge. After the advent of Sultan Qalawun in 679/1280, the anti-sultan, Sunqur al-Ashqar transformed the castle into his headquarters and kept it until its final conquest by Qalawun in 686/1287. Qal‘at Salah al-Din was then transformed into a provincial administrative centre within the Mamluk Empire.  
The triangular shaped castle, built on a rocky spur, is isolated from the mountain by a wide, artificial ditch about 30 m deep. The spur measures about 700 m east to west and has 120 m of maximal width along the eastern ditch, where there towers a pinnacle for the drawbridge. It has two topographical areas divided by a central ditch, deepened by the Byzantines so that the castle was on the high, eastern side and the defensive towers on the low, western side.  
The high courtyard to the east was initially the heart of the Byzantine citadel, with a small polygonal castle built at the top of a hillock and defended by four successive surrounding walls on the east side, lined by polygonal and semi-circular salient towers. Transformed into a manorial area by the Crusaders during the 6th/12th century, it included a huge square keep, two large cisterns, numerous surrounding towers and partial digging of the eastern ditch. Later, the Ayyubids improved the defences and built a large palatial complex combining a *hammam* and reception rooms on two levels, following the same model as that of the Citadel of Aleppo (VII.1.h). Two additional *hammams* and a mosque were built around this complex during the Mamluk period with a reception tower astride the west wall of the high courtyard. The low courtyard to the west was also improved defensively during the Crusader and Islamic occupations with the construction of two gate-towers and the completion of the surrounding wall.

ar.name: علبة من العاج.
description:
علبة مستطيلة ذات غطاء على شكل منصة، مكونة من صفائح عاجية مركبة مع بعضها بعضاً، يمسك الغطاء رباطان فضيان أضيفا في وقت لاحق لكن القفل مفقود. وتدل الثقوب الكثيرة على أن هذه العلبة ذات تاريخ حافل ويبدو أن العديد من الأربطة الحديدية كانت مثبتة عليها. والعلبة، ماعدا قعرها، مزينة برسوم حيوانية محاطة بأشرطة ضيقة من سعف النخيل. كما تظهر على الصفائح رسوم وصور لحيوانات تتصارع، أحياناً على شكل منمنمات وأحياناً بشكل حر، وتحيط بهذه الحيوانات أغصان دائرية. كما أن هناك تشكيلة كبيرة من الحيوانات، إذ توجد الأسود والأرانب وكذلك الجدي والوعل والجمل والزرافة إلى جانب الطيور. بالإضافة إلى ذلك يظهر بعض الحيوانات الأسطورية كالغرفين. والحيوانات إما مصورة في حالة صراع أو أن الصيادين يلاحقونها. أما الأشكال البشرية فتمثل صيادين أو سائقي جمال. يوجد على إحدى علب المجموعة المصرية، التي تنتمي إليها هذه العلبة أيضاً، اسم الشخص الذي طلب صنعها، مكتوباً بأحرف لاتينية. لذلك يمكن الافتراض أن علباً كهذه كانت تنحت على يد فنانين عرب وفق التقاليد الفاطمية في جنوب إيطاليا لصالح طبقة من الأغنياء. وتسمح أنواع الحيوانات الموجودة على هذه المجموعة بالتأكد من وجود صلة وثيقة بينها وبين الأبواق العادية حيث يمكن القول إن كلا النوعين كان يصنع على الأغلب في ورش العمل نفسها.  
كذلك أمكن التعرف على صور حيوانية من الطراز نفسه أو من طراز مشابه على العديد من أبنية القرنين الحادي عشر والثاني عشر في جنوب إيطاليا، وهذا ما يرجح الاستنتاج بأن المشاهد الحيوانية كانت موضع شغف وافتتان في أوروبا في ذلك الوقت.

كانت العلب ذوات الزخارف المحفورة من إيطاليا الجنوبية، واسعة الانتشار في القصور الملكية، ولدى عائلات النبلاء. المشاهد التي تغطّي هذه العلبة تبرز عدداً من الطيور والحيوانات (الأرانب، والأيائل، والأسود، والزرافات) ومخلوقات أسطورية تتصارع فيما بينها، أو يتمُّ قنصها، مع مقاتلين مُجهَّزين بترسين.
dates: القرن الرابع – الخامس / القرن الحادي عشر – الثاني عشر.
keywords: جنوب إيطاليا-صقلية؛ عاج؛ علبة عاجية؛ عهد فاطمي.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Elfenbeinkasten.
description: Der rechteckige Kasten mit pultförmigem Deckel entstand aus einzelnen Elfenbeinplatten, die zusammengefügt wurden. Der Deckel wird von zwei später entstandenen Silber beschlägen gehalten, das Schloß ist verloren. Vielerlei Einbohrungen zeigen, dass der Kasten eine wechselvolle Geschichte hatte und vermutlich mit zahllosen Eisenbeschlägen versehen war. Bis auf den Boden ist der gesamte Kasten mit Tierfriesen geschmückt, die von schmalen Streifen mit Halbpalmettenranken eingefasst werden. Auf den Platten kommen Tiere und Tierkämpfe, gelegentlich stilisiert oder auch freier komponiert, vor. Die Tiere werden von kreisförmigen Ranken überschnitten. Eine Vielzahl von Tieren wird wiedergegeben, nämlich Löwen, Hasen, Steinbock, Hirsch, Kamel, Giraffe und Vögel. Zudem kommen Fabeltiere wie Greifen vor. Die Tiere werden auch kämpfend geschildert oder von Jägern gejagt. Die menschlichen Figuren stellen Jäger oder Kamelführer dar. Einer der Kästen aus der ägyptischen Gruppe, zu der auch dieser Kasten gehört, nennt den Namen eines Auftraggebers in lateinischer Schrift, so dass angenommen wird, derartige Kästen könnten von arabischen Künstlern in fatimidischer Tradition stehend in Unteritalien für eine vermögende Schicht von Auftraggebern gearbeitet worden sein. Die auf dieser Gruppe vorkommenden Tiere lassen eine enge Beziehung zu einer Gruppe von Olifanten erkennen, so dass die Werkstätten möglicherweise sowohl Kästen als auch Olifante lieferten. Tierdarstellungen in vergleichbarem Stil lassen sich auch an unteritalienischen Bauten des 11.-12. Jh. feststellen, so dass angenommen werden kann, dass die Tiermotive auch in Europa eine besondere Faszination ausübten.

Kästchen mit Schnitzdekor aus Süditalien waren bei Hof und bei adligen Familien weit verbreitet. Die Szenen, die dieses Kästchen bedecken, zeigen Vögel und andere Tiere (Hasen, Hirsche, Löwen und eine Giraffe) sowie mythologische Wesen, die einander angreifen oder gejagt werden, und schließlich zwei Krieger mit Schilden.
keywords: Elfenbeinkasten; Sizilien-Unteritalien; Elfenbein; Fatimiden
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Ivory casket.
description:
A rectangular casket, with a desk-like lid, made of individual pieces of ivory that have been joined together. The lid is attached by two silver clasps/hinges, which were made at a later date, and the padlock has been lost. Various holes that have been bored through the casket demonstrate its chequered history and the possibility that it had an indefinite number of iron fittings. The bottom excepted, the entire box is covered in decorative animal-motif friezes, which are framed by narrow bands of tendrils of half-palmettes. Animals and animal fights, composed in both a stylised and a freehand form, are found on the panels. Circular tendrils overlap the animals. A great variety of animals are represented: lions, hares, ibex, stags, camels, giraffes and birds. Mythological creatures such as griffins are also included. The animals are portrayed as fighting one another or as being pursued by hunters. The human figures appear as hunters or camel leaders. One of the caskets from the Egyptian group, of which this one is part, states in Latin script the name of one of its patrons, which leads to the assumption that these caskets could have been made by Arab craftsmen, working in the Fatimid tradition in southern Italy, on the commission of wealthy patrons. The animals belonging to this group bear such a close resemblance to those on a group of oliphants that it is possible that the workshops produced both caskets and oliphants.  
A similar stylistic depiction of animals can also be seen on 11th–12th century buildings in southern Italy, so it can therefore be assumed that the animal motifs held a particular fascination in Europe as well.

Caskets with carved decoration from southern Italy had a widespread use at court or in noble families. The scenes that cover this casket show birds and animals (rabbits, stags, lions and a giraffe) and mythological creatures attacking each other or being hunted and two warriors with shields
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
Museum of Arts and Crafts, Berlin, Germany.
keywords: Ivory; Sicily, southern Italy; Fatimid; vegetal decoration; animal decoration; imaginary animal; zoomorphic imagery; inscription; hunting; patronage
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Arqueta de marfil.
description:
Arqueta rectangular con tapa en forma de pirámide truncada, hecha con placas de marfil individuales ensambladas. La tapa presenta dos bisagras añadidas posteriormente; no se conserva el cierre. Su superficie llena de agujeros da fe de su accidentada historia e hace pensar que quizá tuviera herrajes. Toda la superficie está decorada con motivos animales dentro de frisos con estrechos marcos de ramas y medias palmetas. Las figuras, rodeadas por zarcillos circulares a veces solapados, se caracterizan por la estilización y por la libertad de la talla. Aparecen representados numerosos animales (leones, libres, íbices, ciervos, camellos, jirafas y aves, pero también criaturas mitológicas como grifos) en lucha entre sí o perseguidos por cazadores o camelleros. Una arqueta del denominado "grupo egipcio" al que pertenece este ejemplo presenta una inscripción en latín con el nombre del mecenas de la obra, lo que lleva a pensar que los artesanos eran musulmanes del sur de Italia que trabajaban conforme a la manera fatimí para clientes adinerados. Los animales de este grupo de arquetas se asemejan a los de los olifantes, así que probablemente los talleres produjeran ambos objetos.  
En edificios de los siglos V-VI / XI-XII del sur de Italia también encontramos representaciones de animales con características estilísticas similares, lo que hace suponer que también en Europa hubo una cierta fascinación por los motivos de animales.

Las arquetas con decoración tallada del sur de Italia fueron muy utilizadas en la corte y en familias nobles. Adornan esta arqueta animales (aves, conejos, ciervos, leones y una jirafa) y criaturas mitológicas combatiendo entre ellos o siendo cazados, así como dos guerreros con escudos.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Siglos V-VI de la Hégira / XI-XII d. C.
keywords: Marfil; Sicilia; sur de Italia; marfil; fatimí;
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Coffret d’ivoire.
description:
Ce coffret rectangulaire à couvercle en pupitre a été fabriqué à partir de plaques d'ivoire assemblées. Le couvercle est retenu par deux charnières en argent postérieures, la serrure s'est perdue. De nombreux trous forés indiquent que le coffret a eu une histoire mouvementée et était probablement muni de multiples ferrures. Il est entièrement recouvert, à part le fond, de frises d'animaux entourées d'étroits rinceaux de demi-palmettes. Sur les plaques sont représentés de la faune et des combats d'animaux, tantôt stylisés, tantôt en composition plus libre. Les animaux sont découpés par des rinceaux circulaires, ils sont présents en nombreuses espèces : lions, lièvres, bouc, cerf, chameau, girafe et oiseaux. On remarque aussi des animaux fabuleux comme le griffon. Les figures humaines représentent le chasseur ou le chamelier. L'un des coffrets du groupe égyptien dont fait partie cette pièce donne le nom de son commanditaire en caractères latins ; on suppose donc que les coffrets de ce type ont été fabriqués en Italie du Sud pour de riches clients par des artistes arabes travaillant dans la tradition fatimide. Il existe une similitude entre les animaux représentés ici et ceux d'un groupe d'olifants, si bien que l'on peut supposer que les mêmes ateliers produisaient des coffrets et des olifants.  
Les représentations d'animaux d'une facture comparable se retrouvent dans l'architecture de l'Italie du Sud au XIe-XIIe siècle, on peut donc penser que les motifs animaliers exerçaient en Europe aussi une fascination particulière.

Les coffrets sculptés de l'Italie du Sud étaient d'un usage répandu à la cour ou dans les familles nobles. Les scènes qui ornent celui-ci représentent des oiseaux et des animaux (lièvres, cerfs, lions et une girafe) et des créatures mythologiques s'attaquant les unes les autres ou en train d'être chassées, ainsi que deux guerriers avec leurs boucliers.
dates: Ve-VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIe-XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Ivoire ; Sicile ; Italie du Sud ;  fatimide
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: Grand Bazar Arabe. A late-19th-century bazaar built in Tunis by the construction company of G. Di Vittorio, an Italian immigrant in Tunisia

On the main entrance one can read the shop sign “Grand Bazar Kassar Said”; on the left “Grand Bazar Arab” and on the right, one can read the shop sign “I. Piperno”: Piperno is an unmistakably Italian Jewish name.  
Giuseppe Di Vittorio, who ran the construction company that built this building, migrated from Termini Imerese (a small town near Palermo, Sicily, Italy) in 1882.

en.name: Bab Okla
description:
Bab Okla, one of seven *medina* gates, is situated on the east of the enclosure. Built around the middle of the 10th/16th century, it was probably restored in the middle of the 12th/18th century, when the last reconstruction of the *medina* walls took place. It was known for a long time as the “Gate of the Sea” because in the past it was through this gate that one found the path leading to the village of Martil on the Mediterranean.  
For the farmers wishing to sell their goods in town, it offered a direct route to one of the *medina*’s most commercial streets, allowing them thus to enter with their mules, who refreshed themselves at the nearest fountain, without disturbing the privacy or peace of the town’s inhabitants. The entrance of this parallelepipedic gate is straightforward, as opposed to being elbow-shaped as was the tradition for Mediaeval gates. Its proportions are enormous: 3 m. wide, 4 m. high, and 2.5 m. thick.  
Inside the recess of the gate, a bench, which sits beneath an interlacing vault, was constructed for a guard. A room, a *mesria*, was built above the opening of the gate to house a guardian whose principal duties were as follows: to stock the gunpowder used to load the canons in the fortress next to the gate; to open and close the gate at sunrise and sunset.

es.name: Bab Okla
description:
Bab Okla, una de las siete puertas de la *medina*, está situada al este del recinto. Habilitada hacia la mitad del siglo X/XVI, probablemente se restauró a mediados del XII/XVIII con ocasión de la última reconstrucción de las murallas de la *medina*. Durante mucho tiempo se conoció con el nombre de Puerta del Mar, ya que antaño se accedía por ella al camino que lleva al pueblo de Martil, a orillas del Mediterráneo.  
La puerta daba acceso a una de las calles más comerciales de la *medina* y permitía entrar en la ciudad a los campesinos que venían a vender sus productos con sus mulos, que bebían en la fuente contigua sin perturbar la intimidad de los ciudadanos. Esta puerta de forma prismática tiene el paso de entrada directo, no en codo, como era tradicional en las puertas medievales. Sus proporciones son gigantescas: 3 m de ancho, 4 m de alto y 2,50m de profundidad.  
En el hueco de la puerta había un banco donde se instalaba el centinela, cubierto por una bóveda de arista. Encima de la abertura de la puerta había una pieza acondicionada, o *mesriya*, donde se alojaba un guardián cuyas principales funciones eran almacenar la pólvora utilizada para los cañones instalados en una fortín anejo, y abrir y cerrar la puerta, respectivamente, a la salida y a la puesta del sol.

fr.name: Bab Okla
description:
Bab Okla, une des sept portes de la médina, se trouve à l’est de l’enceinte. Aménagée vers la moitié du Xe/XVIe siècle, elle fut probablement restaurée au milieu du XIIe/XVIIIe siècle lors de la dernière reconstruction des murailles de la médina. Elle fut longtemps connue sous le nom de “Porte de la mer”, car c’est par elle qu’on accédait jadis au chemin menant au village de Martil, sur la Méditerranée.  
Pour les paysans désireux de venir vendre leurs marchandises en ville, elle offrait un accès direct à une des rues les plus commerçantes de la médina, leur permettant ainsi d’y pénétrer avec leur mulet qui s’abreuvait à la fontaine attenante sans déranger l’intimité des citadins.  
Cette porte, en forme de parallélépipède, a un accès direct, et non en chicane comme c’était la tradition pour les portes médiévales. Ses proportions sont gigantesques: 3 m de large, 4 m de haut, et 2,50 m de profondeur.  
Dans le renfoncement de la porte, un banc, surmonté d’une voûte entrecroisée, était installé pour une sentinelle. Au-dessus de l’ouverture de la porte était aménagée une pièce, *mesria*, où logeait un gardien dont les principales fonctions étaient les suivantes: stocker la poudre servant à armer les canons installés dans une forteresse accolée à la porte; ouvrir et fermer la porte au lever et au coucher du soleil.

en.name: Arabian gold dagger
short_description: Arabian (Omani) dagger belonging to Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim. The dagger sheath is made of leather and embroidered with golden thread. The top and base of the sheath is decorated with a traditional flower design whilst the middle of the sheath is decorated with a leaf pattern. The dagger handle is made of rhinoceros ivory and is decorated with ten pearls. The dagger blade is steel called ‘*al-jawhar*’ which is derived from the finest Arabian Damascus plate.

en.name: Tile panel with inscription in *thuluth* script
description: From the time of the construction of the great mosque complex of Süleyman in Istanbul (Hegira 957–964 / AD 1550–1557) onward, Iznik epigraphic tiles increasingly came to grace Ottoman religious monuments. Stencils were used to transfer the designs of both epigraphic and pictorial tile compositions; however, this inscription seems not to have been conceived by one of the many professional calligraphers who flourished under the Ottomans. Rather it may be the work of a highly proficient amateur. The Arabic text, “This world is the sowing ground of the next \[world\]", appears to be an unsound *hadith*, probably a paraphrase of a verse from the Qur’an (al-Shura: 20). The inscription suggests that the panel was created for a religious context, but it does not tell us much more about its original location.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
dates: Hegira second half of the 10th century / AD second half of the 16th century

description: منذ العصور الرومانية فإن منطقة شرق المتوسط وخاصة سوريا كانت مركز انبعاث كبير لتكنولوجيا صناعة الزجاج وإن الحرفيين السوريين طوروا أيضا تقنيات تلوين الزجاج والتزيين ووسعوا العمل لمنتجات كثيرة  وتتمتع هذه القارورة المقولبة بالنفخ لزجاج أخضر شفاف بجسم أسطواني وعنق ضيق ذو تحدبين وتمثل نوعا معروفا جيدا للإنتاج السوري في أواخر القرن الحادي عشر – الثاني عشر والقارورة مزينة بالعديد من القطع الزجاجية بلون أحمر – بني والمضافة بشكل خطوط أفقية متوازية في الأعلى وفي أسفل الجدران وبشكل نموذج بخط منكسر إلى حد كبير فيما بينهما.وتحتوي مجموعة الزجاج السورية في متحف خنينكو قارورة أخرى ذات شكل مشابه وحجم مشابه ولكن المادة مختلفة من حيث التزيين ( يوجد فقاقيع صغيرة مضافة) تعود لأواخر القرن الحادي عشر.

en.name: Flask
description: Since Roman times the Eastern Mediterranean, particularly Syria, has been the centre of a vibrant flowering of glassmaking technology. Syrian craftsmen further developed techniques of glass colouring and decoration and expanded the variety products. This flask, mould-blown of a clear green glass, featuring a cylindrical body and a narrow neck with two convexities, represents a well-known type of Syrian production of late 11th–12th centuries. The flask is decorated with several thin trails of red-brown glass, applied in parallel horizontal lines at the top and the bottom of walls and in a large zig-zag pattern in between. The Khanenko Museum Syrian glass collection highlights another flask very similar in shape, size and material but different in décor (applied small blobs), dated to the late 11th century.
keywords: Glass; flask; Syria; Fatimid, Seljuq; Crusaders
materials: Clear glass with green tinge; mould-blown with applied décor

description: كُتبت هذه المخطوطة القرآنية الكريمة المغلفة بالجلد بصفحاتها الأولى المزخرفة بيد الخطاط العثماني الشهير حافظ عثمان. وتتألف كل صفحة من ثلاثة عشر سطرًا مكتوبة بخط النسخ الأسود الرفيع، وتتميز عناوين السور والحركات وأُطُر الصفحات باللون الذهبي. وقد أنهى حافظ عثمان كتابة 25 مخطوطة قرآنية، جاعلا مخطوطة الشارقة واحدة من ضمن مجموعة نادرة.

en.name: Manuscript of the Holy Qur’an
description: This leather-bound Qur’an manuscript with its richly ornamented front pages was written by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Hafiz Osman. Each page shows thirteen lines of delicate black *naskhi* script, gilt chapter headings, verse markers and gilt frames. Hafiz Osman completed 25 Qur’an manuscripts, making the Sharjah manuscript one of a rare group.
keywords: Hafiz Osman; Naskhi script; Ottoman Calligraphy; religious manuscript

en.name: Dar Jellouli
short_description: With a simple façade and built in a traditional Tunisian style, this house is built around a central square courtyard paved with white marble and with walls covered in blue tiles. The top two storeys are fitted with an ambulatory and wooden railings. The family's wealth is evident from the carved stone framework, ceramics, carved stucco, woodwork, and floors paved with imported marble. The ground floor contains a number of upside-down-T-shaped rooms which attempt to recreate scenes of daily life in 19th century Sfax. The first-floor rooms hold a collection of traditional clothes. Finally, the second floor holds a collection of painting and Arabic calligraphy.
history: Located in the heart of Sfax medina, the capital of southern Tunisia, Dar Jellouli once belonged to a rich family from the local nobility. Many members of this family had occupied important positions in the Regency's government throughout the modern period. For example, from 1772 to 1782 Baccar Jellouli was the governor of Sfax. His sons Mohamed and Mahmoud were also members of the city's local government. However, the family made much of its fortune through commercial activities, particularly by owning a fleet of privateer ships. This building was the seat of the local government then from 1939 housed the Centre des Arts under the direction of Lucien Golvin. after independence it became the Musée Régional des Arts et Traditions Populaires.
keywords: Architecture; Italian style; stucco; marble
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Dar Jellouli
short_description: A l’abri d’une façade toute simple et à l’instar des maisons traditionnelles tunisiennes, on pénètre dans une cour carrée dallée de marbre blanc et aux parois revêtues de céramique bleue. La maison a été édifiée en deux étages supérieurs disposant de déambulatoires et de balustrades en bois. La richesse de la famille transparaît dans la profusion des encadrements en pierre sculptée, des céramiques, des stucs, des boiseries, et dans le dallage en marbre importé. Au rez-de-chaussée, les chambres en forme de T renversé présentent une exposition de tableaux de la vie quotidienne traditionnelle de la ville de Sfax au XIXe siècle, tandis que le premier étage accueille les costumes traditionnels et le deuxième des peintures et des calligraphies arabes.
history: Situé au cœur de la médina de Sfax, la capitale du Sud tunisien, Dar Jellouli a appartenu à une grande famille de notables de la ville. Plusieurs membres de la famille ont occupé des fonctions importantes dans la Régence de Tunis durant toute la période moderne. Entre 1772 et 1782, Baccar Jellouli fut caïd de Sfax. Ses fils Muhammad et Mahmoud furent également chargés de la fonction de gouverneur de la même ville. La famille s’est également enrichie grâce à ses activités commerciales et surtout en tant qu’armateur de corsaires. Siège du caïdat, la maison abrite en 1939 le Centre des Arts sous la direction de Lucien Golvin. Enfin, depuis l’indépendance, elle a été aménagée en Musée régional des Arts et Traditions populaires.
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba
