en.name: Islamic quarter.
description:
The Islamic quarter was built at the end of AH 6th century / AD 12th century, on a platform built in the Byzantine period.  
Since the beginning of the excavations in 1978, the ancient fortress of Mértola has provided an enormous amount of materials from the Islamic period. At the same time, architectural remains have been unearthed which date from the Roman period (AD 1st century) to the period of the reconquest of the town (AH 7th / AD 13th century). The most interesting part of this is the urban area, of which the remains of some ten dwellings are visible today. The houses, repeating architectural styles common to the Mediterranean urban world, are organised around a central open courtyard and comprise a set of rooms with clearly defined functions (living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens and latrines, etc.). In the complex superimposition of structures which always results from urban archaeological interventions, it is possible to read with clarity the remains of streets, drainage systems and paving which bear witness to the final occupation of the Islamic citadel.  
It is an urban grouping of around 4,000 square metres, comprising some 30 dwellings. Up to the present, fragments of 15 houses have been uncovered, and excavation of nine of them has been completed, clearly showing their layout. Each of these houses is arranged around a central open courtyard, a 'room' which gives a clear indication of the spatial conception and identifies the cultural habits of the inhabitants. In spite of the evident differences in economic status between the residents of some of these houses (visible in the larger or smaller areas occupied by the dwellings and in the level of refinement found in some of them, in comparison with simpler and more economical solutions used in others), their schemes of functional organisation do not differ a great deal.  
The historical and archaeological research in progress, as well as having produced a set of basic data for the study of the urban organisation of the area or of the architecture of the dwellings, has also provided information on which to base a study of the daily lives of the population of Mértola in the Islamic period. Evidence from work tools, musical instruments, pieces from games, and kitchen or dining utensils revealing eating practices is gradually allowing us to piece together the immense jigsaw of the day-to-day lives of the inhabitants of this citadel eight centuries ago.

The Islamic quarter was built in the late AH 6th / AD 12th century on a Byzantine site. It covers an area of 4,000 square metres and contains some 30 houses. Archaeological excavations have identified some of these dwellings: arranged around a central, open courtyard, they include a number of clearly functional divisions (living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, latrines, etc.). There are also clear vestiges of roads and sanitation systems that are a record of the last Islamic occupation.
dates: Hegira last quarter of 6th / AD 12th century.
keywords: quarter; Mértola; Almohad; Byzantine period; Roman period; urban world; central courtyard; citadel; civil architecture
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

es.name: Barrio islámico.
description:
El barrio islámico fue construido a finales del siglo VI / XII sobre una plataforma levantada en el periodo bizantino.  
La antigua alcazaba de Mértola vino a proporcionar, desde el inicio de las excavaciones en 1978, un enorme conjunto de materiales del periodo islámico. Al mismo tiempo, se han descubierto vestigios arquitectónicos que van desde el periodo romano (siglo I a. C.) hasta la época de reconquista de la villa (siglo VII / XIII). El elemento de mayor interés es este conjunto urbano, del que hoy son visibles los restos de casi una treintena de viviendas. Estas repiten esquemas arquitectónicos comunes al mundo urbano mediterráneo: están organizadas en torno a un patio central descubierto y comprenden un conjunto de espacios cuya funcionalidad estaba bien definida (salas, alcobas, cocinas, letrinas, etc.). En la compleja superposición de estructuras que siempre resulta de las intervenciones arqueológicas urbanas, es posible identificar con claridad restos de calles, de sistemas de saneamiento y de pavimentos que constituyen el testimonio de la última ocupación de la alcazaba islámica.  
Es un conjunto urbano de unos 4.000 m² donde, de la treintena de casas que comprendería, hasta el momento se han puesto al descubierto restos de quince, nueve de ellas completas y de planimetría perfectamente legible. Todas ellas se organizaban en torno a un patio central descubierto, lugar que determina de forma indudable un modo de concepción espacial al tiempo que informa de los hábitos culturales de sus moradores. A pesar de las notorias diferencias de estatus económico entre los habitantes de algunas de esas casas (visibles en las mayores o menores áreas ocupadas por las casas y en el alto grado de acabado de algunas de ellas, frente a soluciones más simples y económicas puestas en práctica en otras), la organización funcional de los espacios no difiere mucho.  
La investigación histórico-arqueológica en curso, que busca un conjunto de datos fundamentales para el estudio de la organización urbanística del lugar o de la arquitectura de las casas, ha proporcionado también elementos para una primera aproximación al estudio de la vida cotidiana de la población de Mértola en época islámica. Herramientas de trabajo, instrumentos musicales, piezas de juego, utensilios de cocina o de mesa e incluso hábitos alimentarios van componiendo poco a poco el inmenso rompecabezas del día a día de los habitantes de esta alcazaba hace ocho siglos.

El barrio islámico fue construido a finales del siglo VI / XII sobre una plataforma del periodo bizantino. Es un conjunto de 4.000 m2 donde había cerca de una treintena de viviendas. Las excavaciones arqueológicas han permitido identificar algunas de ellas: estaban organizadas en torno a un patio central descubierto y comprendían un conjunto de espacios cuya función está bien definida (salas, alcobas, cocinas, letrinas, etc.). También es posible identificar con claridad los restos de las calles y los sistemas de saneamiento que constituyen el testimonio de la postrera ocupación islámica.
dates: Último cuarto del siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: Periodo bizantino; periodo romano; mundo urbano; patio central; alcazaba; arquitectura civil
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Quartier islamique.
description:
Le quartier islamique a été bâti à la fin du VIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.) au-dessus d'une plate-forme édifiée pendant la période byzantine.  
Depuis les fouilles de 1978, l'ancienne *alcáçova* de Mértola a livré un abondant ensemble de matériaux de la période islamique, ainsi que des vestiges architecturaux qui vont de la période romaine (Ier siècle) jusqu'à l'époque de la reconquête de la ville (VIe siècle H / XIIIe siècle J.-C.). L'élément le plus intéressant reste cet ensemble urbain dont on a rendu visibles une dizaine d'habitations. Les maisons développent des solutions architectoniques communes au monde urbain méditerranéen : autour d'un patio central découvert sont distribuées un certain nombre de pièces dont la fonctionnalité était bien définie (salles, alcôves, cuisines, latrines, etc.). Dans la complexe superposition de structures résultant des interventions archéologiques urbaines successives, il est possible de voir des restes de rues, de systèmes d'assainissement et de pavements qui témoignent de la dernière occupation de l'*alcáçova* islamique.  
Il s'agit d'un ensemble urbain d'environ 4 000 mètres carrés où auraient été implantées une trentaine d'habitations. Jusqu'à présent ont été mis au jour les vestiges de quinze maisons, parmi lesquelles neuf sont complètes et parfaitement lisibles dans leur planimétrie. Elles s'organisent toutes autour d'un patio central découvert, “compartiment” qui marque de façon indélébile une conception de l'espace habité tout en témoignant des habitudes culturelles de ses habitants. Malgré les nettes différences de statut économique entre les habitants (on s'en rend compte à la superficie des habitations, ou au degré de finition des maisons, certaines étant sophistiquées, d'autres ayant opté pour des solutions plus simples et moins onéreuses), l'organisation fonctionnelle ne diffère pas beaucoup dans son schéma directeur.  
La recherche historico-archéologique en cours n'a pas seulement livré un ensemble d'informations fondamentales pour l'étude de l'organisation urbaine du site ou de l'architecture des maisons ; elle a également fourni des éléments pour une première approche de la vie quotidienne de la population de Mértola à l'époque islamique. Outils de travail, instruments de musique, pièces de jeu, ustensiles domestiques employés en cuisine ou à table, habitudes alimentaires… peu à peu se recompose l'immense puzzle du quotidien des habitants de cette *alcáçova* d'il y a huit siècles.

Le quartier islamique fut construit à la fin du VIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.) sur un site byzantin. Il s'étend sur une surface de 4 000 mètres carrés et contient environ 30 maisons. Des fouilles archéologiques ont permis d'identifier quelques-unes de ces demeures : organisées autour d'une cour ouverte centrale, elles comprennent un certain nombre d'unités clairement fonctionnelles (séjours, chambres, cuisines, latrines, etc.). Il y a également des vestiges évidents de routes et d'installations sanitaires qui sont un rappel de la dernière occupation islamique.
dates: Dernier quart du VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: quartier ; Mértola ; Almohades ; période byzantine ; période romaine ; monde urbain ; patio central ; alcaçova ; architecture civile
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Bairro islâmico.
description:
O bairro islâmico foi construído no final do século VI AH / XII AD, sobre uma plataforma construída no período bizantino.  
  
A antiga alcáçova de Mértola tem vindo a proporcionar, desde o início das escavações em 1978, um enorme conjunto de materiais do período islâmico. Ao mesmo tempo têm sido revelados vestígios arquitectónicos que vão do período romano (século I) até à época da reconquista da vila (século XIII). O elemento de maior interesse é este conjunto urbano, do qual são hoje visíveis os restos de cerca de uma dezena de habitações. As casas repetem soluções arquitectónicas comuns ao mundo urbano mediterrânico, estão organizadas em torno de um pátio central descoberto e compreendem um conjunto de divisões cuja funcionalidade estava bem definida (salas, alcovas, cozinhas e latrinas etc.). Na complexa sobreposição de estruturas que sempre resulta das intervenções arqueológicas urbanas, é possível ler com clareza restos de ruas, de sistemas de saneamento e de pavimentos que constituem o testemunho da derradeira ocupação da alcáçova islâmica.  
  
É um conjunto urbano com cerca de 4000 metros quadrados, onde estariam implantadas cerca de três dezenas de habitações. Até ao momento foram postos a descoberto fragmentos de quinze casas, nove das quais estão completas e são perfeitamente legíveis na sua planimetria. Todas elas se organizam em torno de um pátio central descoberto, "compartimento" que marca de forma indelével um modo de concepção espacial ao mesmo tempo que identifica os hábitos culturais dos seus habitantes. Apesar das notórias diferenças de estatuto económico entre os moradores de algumas dessas casas (visíveis nas maiores ou menores áreas ocupadas pelas habitações e no apurado grau de acabamento de algumas delas, em detrimento de soluções mais simples e económicas postas em prática noutras), o seu esquema de organização funcional não difere muito entre si.  
  
A investigação histórico-arqueológica em curso, para além de ter fornecido um conjunto de dados fundamentais para o estudo da organização urbanística do local ou da arquitectura das habitações, proporcionou também elementos para uma primeira abordagem ao estudo do quotidiano da população de Mértola em época islâmica. Ferramentas de trabalho, instrumentos musicais, peças de jogo, utensilagens em uso na cozinha ou à mesa ou hábitos alimentares vão, aos poucos, compondo o imenso "puzzle" do dia-a-dia dos habitantes desta alcáçova há oito séculos.

O bairro islâmico foi construído no final do século VI AH / XII AD, sobre uma plataforma do período bizantino. É um conjunto com 4000 metros quadrados, onde estariam implantadas cerca de três dezenas de habitações. As escavações arqueológicas têm permitido identificar algumas dessas casas: organizadas em torno de um pátio central descoberto compreendem um conjunto de divisões cuja funcionalidade está bem definida (salas, alcovas, cozinhas e latrinas etc.). É também possível ler com clareza restos de ruas e de sistemas de saneamento que constituem testemunho da derradeira ocupação islâmica.
dates: Último quartel do século VI AH / XII AD.
keywords: bairro; Mértola; almóadas; período bizantino; período romano; mundo urbano; pátio central; alcáçova; arquitectura civil
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: Santa Cruz Monastery
description:
Work began on the Monastery on July 28th 1131, on the site of what was almost certainly the Muslim or Roman Royal Baths. D. Afonso Henriques, the first King of Portugal, was responsible for the initiative, and it was here that the young prince brought together the leading intellectuals and politicians in the kingdom. Among them were D. João Peculiar, D. Miguel Salomão, the Archdeacon D. Telo, and São Teotónio (St Theotonius), first Prior of the Monastery, which was granted to the Augustine Canons.  
Following a visit by D. Manuel I in 1502, profound alterations were made to the physical structure of the monastery, rebuilding the church, cloisters and dwellings from the very foundations. The promoter was the Prior and Bishop of Guarda, D. Pedro Gavião, whilst D. Manuel I was the patron and principal financier, and Boytac was the Master Builder.  
The Mediaeval façade was erected between 1507 and 1513; the portal was added in 1522. Designed and constructed by Diogo de Castilho, it was completed with statues by Nicolas Chanterène. The interior of the Church is spacious, although there is only one aisle. The vaulting, completed in 1513, was the work of Boytac. The ribbed vault is typically Late Gothic, but the bosses and spiral corbels are not at all like Boytac’s work. Diogo de Castilho constructed the upper choir over the entrance, in 1530.  
The chancel is also covered by a similar type of vault to that of the nave, and the key stones bear the royal coat of arms, armillary spheres and the cross of the Order of Christ, all alluding to the royal patronage. The tombs of D. Afonso Henriques and his son D. Sancho I, are on the lateral walls, although initially, they were in the nave, but were transferred to this more important location in 1535. D. Manuel I wished to highlight his ancestors and commissioned these two formidable reminders of the ascendancy of the Royal House, from João de Castilho, at that time in charge of works at the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos. Work was carried out between 1518 and 1522 and was overseen by Diogo de Castilho, younger brother of the Court architect. The superb recumbent statues were the work of the French sculptor, Nicolas Chanterène, and the remainder of the statuary was undertaken by other Portuguese and Spanish artists who had come from Jerónimos: Diogo Francisco, Pêro Anes, Diogo Fernandes, João Fernandes and Juan de la Faya. There is a contrast here between the aesthetics of the Late Gothic, obvious in the structures and some of the decoration, and that of the Renaissance, as can be seen in the recumbent statues and other sculptures, namely those of *Our Lady* and the *Virtues*. Another Manueline work of considerable importance is the Cloister of Silence by Marcos Pires, though it is possible that the design was by Boytac, his master, who, in 1513, had left Coimbra to work on the forts in North Africa. The cloister is totally Gothic, both in structure and decoration, vigorous in form and with exuberant foliate decoration.  
The cloister opens onto the upper choir, where the stalls made for the chancel 20 years earlier, by the Flemish woodworker Machim, were moved in 1531. This brilliant work with very rich cresting evokes the maritime voyages of the Portuguese and the cities to which they sailed, some clearly defined as Oriental or Muslim. On the chair arms, sculpted figures of Moorish, Asiatic and African kings are depicted in chains to display Portuguese sovereignty over their lands.

ar.name: سوار
description: هذا السوار يظهر الناحية الفنية والمستوى الرفيع لتقنيات تشغيل الذهب الإسلامية في العصر الفاطمي وقد كانت تصنع من صفيحة واحدة من الذهب وقلب السوار كان يزين بقطعة معدنية مطروقة نافرة وتصاميم مثلمة وبعدها تطوى بشكل أنبوب مجوف ، وهنا التصاميم الدقيقة النافرة بما فيها رؤوس بشرية وطيور وأشكال خرافية وتزيين القفل الدائري المتقن يوضح العديد من التقنيات المعقدة :حلزونات السلك المبروم والتخشين والتخريم وإن الأحجار هي من الزمرد والياقوت والأخيرة تم وضعها مع الكريستال الصخري وهو الحجر  المفضل في الفترة الفاطمية وإن الأساور من هذا النوع كانت تصنع بشكل واضح بشكل أزواج وهذا يزيد من أثر المصنعية الدقيقة والمواد النفيسة ومثل هذه المجوهرات الذهبية كانت تشكل ليس فقط شكلا رائعا من الزنية الشخصية ولكن أيضا مؤشر على ثروة النساء و موقعهن الاجتماعي .

en.name: Bracelet
description: This bracelet demonstrates the artistry and luxury of Islamic goldworking techniques in the Fatimid period. Fashioned from a This bracelet demonstrates the artistry and luxury of Islamic goldworking techniques in the Fatimid period. Fashioned from a single flat sheet of gold, the shank of the bracelet was decorated with repoussé and chased designs and then folded into a hollow tube; here the fine relief designs include human heads, birds, and harpies. The decoration of the elaborate circular clasp illustrates several complex techniques: twisted wire spirals, granulation and filigree. The stones are emeralds and rubies; the latter have been set with rock crystal, a favorite stone in the Fatimid period. Bracelets of this type were evidently made and worn in pairs, further magnifying the effect of the fine workmanship and precious materials. Such gold jewelry served not only as a spectacular form of personal adornment but also as an indicator of a woman’s wealth and social standing.

en.name: High altar for San Pietro Cathedral of Bologna
description:
This complex and precious altar was donated by Pope Lambertini to the San Pietro Cathedral of Bologna. Originally it was composed of six candlesticks, a silver cross and a silver frontal depicting *Jesus Handing the Keys to St. Peter in the Presence of the Apostles*. Unfortunately, these rich objects were probably handed to the Frenchmen in 1796, after the treaty of Tolentino, signed by Pope Pius VII.  
The invoices for the high altar are registered in the *Diario Benedettino*. The pope prayed that it reached Bologna safe and sound.  
In the middle of the side there is a silver embossed oval representing *Christ Rescuing Peter from the Water*, on the sides are two smaller roundels representing allegories of *Faith*. The three bas-reliefs are framed in gilded cast bronze, with cherubs' heads and garlands against a blue lapis-lazuli background. In the corners the oval bas-reliefs represent the *Martyrdom of St. Peter* on the left and *St. Peter in Jail Visited by the Angel*. On the upper side hangs the coat of arms of the Lambertini family in silver.  
The whole altar is on show together with a sumptuous frontal donated by the pope in 1742, made of  
hemp canvas embroidered with gold thread. Against the embroidered gold background are several sewn gold leaf decorations. In the middle is a roundel of *St. Peter* half bust and on the sides the coat of arms of the Lambertinis' with the tiara and the papal keys held by angels.  
This extremely precious altar, only a part of the richer original complex, is characterised by its technical skill and high artistic quality. The Roman silversmith Angelo Spinazzi, documented from 1721 to 1767, probably made the step. On the sides a hallmark, despite being not entirely legible is believed to be that of the Roman craftsman Filippo Tofani. No hallmark is visible on the main central relief.

This extremely precious altar was donated to the cathedral of Bologna by Pope Benedict XIV.  
The sides and corners are characterised by extremely detailed work: against a blue lapis-lazuli ground are intertwined coats of arms of the Lambertini family and oval bas-reliefs with figures in chiselled and embossed silver and gilded bronze. On the side, in the middle, *Christ Rescues Peter from the Water* flanked by two Allegories of Faith, on the corners *St. Peter in Prison Visited by the Angel* and the *Martyrdom of St. Peter*. The work was made in Roman workshops. The altar is completed by a beautifully worked frontal, also a gift from Pope Benedict XIV (1742).
place: Gift of Pope Benedict XIV Lambertini
keywords: Benedict XIV; St. Peter; Cathedral of Bologna; Roman silversmiths; liturgy; liturgical; Metalwork; bas-relief; allegory

it.name: Scaffa e angolari per l’altare maggiore di San Pietro con paliotto d’altare dono di papa Benedetto XIV Lambertini
description:
Il prezioso e articolato altare donato da papa Lambertini alla Cattedrale di Bologna originariamente comprendeva anche un corredo di sei candelieri con croce d'altare d'argento ed un “*pallio*” \[paliotto\] d'argento con rappresentato Gesù Cristo che consegna le chiavi a San Pietro con tutti gli apostoli. Con molta probabilità tutta questa ricca parte, non più presente, dovette essere inclusa fra gli oggetti consegnati ai Francesi nel 1796, in ottemperanza al trattato di Tolentino, sottoscritto da papa Pio VI.  
Nel *Diario Benedettino* si registrano le tappe cronologiche dell'invio del complesso per l'altare maggiore, che: “..*Preghiamo Iddio..arrivi sano, e salvo”.*  
Al centro della scaffa è uno sbalzo ovale in argento raffigurante *Cristo che salva Pietro dalle acque*, con ai lati due medaglioni più piccoli con le *Allegorie della Fede*. Inorniciano i tre sbalzi cornicine architettoniche in bronzo fuso e dorato, con testine di cherubini e festoni fitomorfi, su un fondo blu di lapislazzuli.Non meno ricchi gli angolari con sbalzi ovali nella parte inferiore, raffiguranti a sinistra *Il martirio di San Pietro* e a destra *San Pietro in vincoli visitato dall'angelo*. Nella parte superiore è lo stemma Lambertini in argento.  
Il complesso viene presentato con sontuoso paliotto lambertiano donato nel 1742, in tela di canapa ricamata in filo d'oro. Su fondo interamente ricamato sono applicate varie decorazioni in oro lamellare e riccio, con al centro entro medaglione la mezza figura di San Pietro e ai lati grande stemma lambertiano con triregno e chiavi apostoliche, retto da angioletti.  
Il pregiatissimo altare di papa Benedetto XIV, pur superstite rispetto al più ricco arredo originario, si contraddistingue per altissima perizia tecnica e qualità artistica. Il gradino sembrerebbe riconducibile all'argentiere romano Angelo Spinazzi, documentato dal 1721 al 1767, mentre un punzone di non facile lettura posto sugli angolari potrebbe appartenere al fonditore romano Filippo Tofani. Nessun punzone è presente nel maggior rilievo centrale.

Il pregiatissimo altare donato alla cattedrale di Bologna da papa Benedetto XIV era arricchito in origine da un corredo di candelieri e croce d'argento e da un prezioso paliotto in argento con *La consegna delle chiavi a Pietro,* arredi che dovettero essere di tributo ai Francesi nel 1796, secondo il Trattato di Tolentino.  
Scaffa e angolari superstiti spiccano per la finissima esecuzione: su fondo blu di lapislazzuli si sovrappongono l'argento cesellato e sbalzato e il bronzo dorato; con stemmi lambertiani e cartelle ovali figurate. Sulla scaffa, al centro *Cristo che salva Pietro dalle acque* e ai lati *Allegorie della Fede*; sugli angolari *San Pietro in vincoli visitato dall'angelo* e *Il martirio di San Pietro*. Maestranze romane sembrano aver siglato l'opera e forse si riconosce il punzone del fonditore Filippo Tofani. Accompagna l'arredo un paliotto donato da papa Benedetto XIV nel 1742 e di finissima esecuzione.

en.name: Castle
description:
Paderne Castle is an imposing tabiyya fortification built along military lines in the Almohad period and situated little more than 10 km. to the north of Albufeira in the heart of the Algarve Barrocal region. The rocky outcrop on which it was built, and in view of the fact that the Ribeira de Quarteira surrounded it, made Paderne a difficult place on which to lay siege.  
The enclosed area, which measures little more than 1,000 sq. m., still protects a lengthy section of its red-earth walls. Of particular interest in the north east section is the L-shaped gateway and the square watchtower connected to the main section by a passageway. Inside the fortification are 16th-century ruins of the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Castelo (whose original construction probably dates back to the 14th century) and the opening of a cistern close to the south wall.  
There is a reference made to Paderne in the *Crónica da Conquista do Algarve* (Chronicle of the Conquest of the Algarve): “this town of Paderne has moved to that place that is now called Albufeira, however the other town is still inhabited and protected by its castle and has a very good cistern inside”. This statement leads us to suppose that, after the Reconquest, the area must have entered into a period of prolonged decline. We find further reference to the town and its decline in a text by Henrique Sarrão in the late 16th century: at that time, the castle was said to be “uninhabited and devoid of people”.  
The state of isolation to which the town had been condemned for centuries was finally interrupted a few years ago with the building of the Via do Infante, the major road which passes very close to the castle.  
Paderne Castle has been classified as a Building of Public Interest since 1971.

es.name: Castillo
description:
El castillo de Paderne, una imponente fortificación en *tapial* militar de época almohade, está situado en pleno barrancal del Algarve, poco más de una decena de kilómetros al norte de Albufeira. La escarpada elevación de terreno donde se alzaba y el hecho de estar rodeada, en gran parte de su extensión, por el río Quarteira, hacían de Paderne un lugar difícil de asediar.  
El recinto, de poco más de 1.000 m2, conserva aún una parte considerable de sus murallas de tierra roja, y hay que señalar, en la cara orientada al norte, la puerta con recodo y la presencia de una torre albarrana de planta cuadrangular, unida al muro principal por un pasadizo. En el interior de la fortificación pueden identificarse las ruinas del siglo XVI de la capilla de Nossa Senhora do Castelo (cuya construcción original datará del siglo XIV) y el hueco de una cisterna junto a la muralla sur.  
La referencia que se hace en la *Crónica da Conquista do Algarve* (“esta villa de Paderna se mudó a aquel lugar que ahora llaman Albufeira, pero todavía la otra está habitada y mejorada con su castillo y una cisterna muy buena dentro”) hace suponer que, tras la Reconquista, se iniciaría una prolongada decadencia. Encontramos un eco en la referencia que de Paderne hace, a finales del siglo XVI, Henrique Sarrão: el castillo ya estaba por entonces “despoblado y sin gente”.  
El estado de aislamiento en que estuvo durante largo tiempo se interrumpió hace pocos años con la construcción de la Via do Infante, que pasa (entre los kilómetros 260 y 261) a escasa distancia del castillo.  
El castillo de Paderne está catalogado como Inmueble de Interés Público desde 1971.

en.name: Drinking cup
short_description: Small silver cup with a stepped pedestal for drinking hard liquors. The surface is decorated with geometric designs, including dots, lines and triangles. On the upper part of the cup, an engraved inscription in Russian ("your health") runs along the external surface. The year of manufacture (1896) is stamped. Items like this were brought to Jordan in the last quarter of the 19th century by Caucasian immigrants, the Circassians. The immigration of the Circassians started in the middle of nineteenth century and continued until 1900. They migrated to the eastern Arab countries with which they have spiritual and religious links. This object illustrates the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries and the various local costumes, crafts and rites.
holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Stepped pedestal; silver; geometric decoration; Caucasian immigrants; domestic vessels

en.name: Sprinkler
description: Perfume sprinklers or *qamaqim* (plural of *qumqum*) with enamelled and gilded decoration were characteristic of Mamluk glass production. This free-blown glass sprinkler presents a globular shaped body with a pronounced kicked-in base, and a long neck that gradually narrows to a pin-sized opening. The body of the sprinkler is decorated in blue enamel and gilding, outlined in red with a broad frieze of interlaced palmettes and four gilded fish encircling the shoulder. The fish motif became a popular decorative feature of early Mamluk enamelled glass and is often associated with prosperity. These long-necked glass sprinklers were used as perfume or rose water containers by elite members of Mamluk society.

en.name: *Taḏkerat al-Awliāʾ by Farid-al-Din ʿAṭṭār Neishabouri* (Social Gathering for Entertainment in Meadow)
description: The *Taḏkerat al-Awliāʾ*, in which Farīd al-Dīn Attār (Hegira 618 / AD 1221) narrates stories of the saints, begins with the chapter devoted to Ja'far al-Sādiq and ends with Hallāj al-Mansūr. The work contains information about the lives of 72 individuals, including Imām al-ʿĀzam, Imam Shāfi'ī, Ahmad b. Ḥanbal, Weysel Karānī and Rābia al-Adawiyya, and their stories and sayings. Each person is allocated a chapter, and the word *zikr* (remembrance) is placed at the beginning of each chapter. The work is written in Persian in *taliq* calligraphy on paper. On pages 1b-2a an entertainment scene is depicted that covers the entire page, while on pages 2b-3a the first section is written in two facing medallions. The work contains 27 miniature scenes depicting various parables. The outer edges of the medallions are embellished with a profusion of *simurgh* birds (benevolent mythical creatures) and a variety of floral motifs crafted in the *ringar* technique. The chapter headings are illuminated in a style characteristic of the period.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

ar.name: مجمَّع الياس باي.
description:
إن المدينة الأيونية الهامة، المعروفة في العصور القديمة باسم ميليتوس (بلاطية)، أصبحت جزءاً من إمارة مينتشي في النصف الأول من القرن 9 / 13 وعرفت باسم بلاط. وفي عام 793 / 1391 ألحق السلطان العثماني بايزيد الأول (الشهير بلقب يلديرم- الصاعقة) هذه الإمارة بالأراضي العثمانية. وبعد أن هزمه تيمور في معركة أنقرة عام 805 / 1402، استعيدت إمارة مينتشي وأصبحت بلاط عاصمتها.  
  
شهدت مدينة بلاط، التي تأسست فوق ميليتوس القديمة، تشييد العديد من المباني في العهد المينتشي، وأهمها مجمع المسجد الذي يضم مدرسة اللاهوت وحمامين عموميين بنيت كلها مباشرة بعد استعادة الياس باي العرش في عام 1402. بني المسجد والمدرسة في حديقة واسعة مسوَّرة، ويتقاسمان فناء مشتركاً. في الجهة الشمالية الغربية للمدرسة يوجد أنقاض بناء لم تُعرف وظيفته بالضبط. وقد بينت تنقيبات عام 1994 الآثارية أن البنية الأساسية لغرف المدرسة تعود إلى مدرسة أخرى أضيفت لاحقاً إلى المجمع، ممتدة بموازاة جدار الحديقة إلى الغرب من المدرسة الحالية. ومن المتفق عليه أن الحمامين الواقعين شمال شرق المدرسة هما جزء من المجمَّع الأصلي.  
  
يقع مسجد الياس باي في مساحة تقريبية 18x18 متراً مربعاً، وتتوجه قبة قطرها 14 متراً مبنية من الطوب، بينما جدرانه مكسوة بألواح بلاط معاد استخدامها. ولا يوجد رواق للمتأخرين بالقدوم. تقع المئذنة في الزاوية الشمالية الغربية، وكان يتم الصعود إليها من الداخل، وقد دمرها زلزال عام 1955. أما الدخول إلى المسجد فيتم عبر باب الإيوان الواقع في منتصف الجدار الشمالي. يُقسم الإيوان بواسطة أعمدة من الرخام إلى ممر مقنطر تعلوه ثلاث قناطر ذات قمم مسطَّحة (بورسة)؛ القنطرة الكبيرة المركزية واقعة في المدخل، بينما تحتوي كل من القنطرتين الجانبيتين على درابزين من الرخام وتستخدمان كنافذتين. وتستند قبة المبنى على كوّات ركنية ضخمة مزخرفة برسوم لأصداف محارية ومثلثات ومقرنصات.  
  
يستحق مسجد الياس باي الاهتمام نظراً للزخرفة الغنية لمنحوتاته الحجرية. أما الأشكال الزهرية والهندسية والنقوش المنحوتة والمطعَّمة فتظهر على المدخل والمحراب والمسطحات المثلثة لجميع نوافذ الجدران الشرقية والغربية والجنوبية. وهذه الزخرفة المطعَّمة تطال البلاطات والحجارة الملونة.  
  
أما المدرسة، التي تتقاسم الفناء مع المسجد، فقد بنيت من الحجر الخشن. وتتألف من غرفة كبيرة مقببة و 12 حجرة دراسية للطلاب، يتبين من الآثار المتبقية أن أسقفها كانت مكسوة بالخشب.  
  
يقع الحمامان إلى الشمال الشرقي من المدرسة والمسجد، وقد بنيت جدرانهما من الحجر الصلد، بينما بنيت القباب والأقبية من الطوب. يتألف الحمام الكبير، الواقع إلى الشمال، من غرفة حارَّة بثلاثة إيوانات وحجرتين ركنيتين، وغرفة التبديل التي اكتشفت خلال عمليات التنقيب عام 1991. تمت زخرفة جدران الغرفة الحارة بقوالب من الجص. أما الحمام الصغير، الواقع على بعد مترين من الحمام الكبير، فيتألف من ثلاث حجرات صغيرة متجاورة.  
المجمَّع مفتوح أمام الزوار.

en.name: Ilyas Bey Complex.
description:
The important Ionian city known in antiquity as Miletos (Palatia) became part of the Menteshe Emiratein the first half of the 7th / 13th century under the name of Balat. In AH 793 / AD 1391 the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I (known as Yıldırım, 'the Thunderbolt') added this emirate to Ottoman lands. After his defeat by Timur at the Battle of Ankara in AH 805 / AD 1402, the Menteshe Emirate was restored and Balat became its capital.  
Balat, founded on ancient Miletos, saw many buildings built in the Menteshe period. The most important of these is the mosque complex with a theological school (*madrasa*) and two public baths or *hammams,* built immediately after Ilyas Bey returned to the throne in 1402.  
The mosque and *madrasa*, built in a broad walled garden, share a common courtyard. In the northwest area of the *madrasa* are the remains of a structure whose function remains uncertain. Archaeological excavations in 1994 revealed the foundations of rooms belonging to another *madrasa* which was later added to the complex, extending parallel to the garden wall on the west of the existing *madrasa*. Two *hammam*s accepted as being part of the original complex are located to the northeast of the *madrasa*.  
The Ilyas Bey Mosque has a square plan of approximately 18 m x 18 m and is surmounted by a dome 14 m in diameter. The walls are covered with re-used marble slabs, while the dome is built with brick. There is no portico for latecomers. The minaret at the northwest corner, which is reached from inside, collapsed in an earthquake in 1955. The mosque is entered through an *iwan*\-portal in the middle of the north wall. The *iwan* is divided into an arcade of three flat-top (Bursa) arches by way of two marble columns; the wide central arch is the entrance, while the two side arches contain marble balustrades and serve as windows. The building's dome is supported by large squinches. These are decorated with oyster-shell motifs, triangles and *muqarnas*.  
The Ilyas Bey Mosque is noteworthy for its rich stonework decoration. Floral and geometric motifs and inscriptions, both carved and inlaid, appear on the portal and *mihrab* as well as on the tympana of each window in the east, west and south walls. The inlaid decoration includes coloured stone and tiles.  
The *madrasa*, which shares the courtyard with the mosque, was built with rough stone. It consists of a domed classroom and 12 students' cells, which traces reveal to have been covered with flat wooden ceilings.  
The two *hammam*s to the northeast of the mosque and *madrasa* have walls of rough stone, together with domes and vaults of brick. The Large Baths (*Büyük Hammam*) on the north, whose changing-room was discovered during excavations in 1991, has a hot room with three *iwan*s and two corner chambers. The walls of the hot room have decoration in moulded plaster. The *Küçük Hammam* (Small Baths), 2-m south of the *Büyük Hammam*, consists of three small rooms arranged side by side. The complex is open to visitors.

The Ilyas Bey complex in Balat, the last capital of the Menteshe Emirate, comprises a mosque, a *madrasa* and two *hammam*s (bathhouses). In spite of the plainness of the *madrasa* and the *hammams*, the mosque of the complex is one of the most striking examples of architecture from the Emirates period. The portal, *mihrab* and windows are lavishly decorated with floral and geometric motifs and calligraphic bands, carved and inlayed.
artist: Şücaeddin [Shuja‘ al-Din] İlyas Bey (r. AH 805–27 / AD 1402–24).
keywords: Mosque; madrasa; hammam; stonework decoration; geometric decoration; floral decoration; inscriptions; calligraphy; Balat; Miletus; Menteshe Emirate; İlyas Bey

es.name: Complejo de İlyas Bey.
description:
La importante ciudad jónica conocida en la Antigüedad como Mileto (Palatia) entró a formar parte del emirato Menteşe en la primera mitad del siglo VII / XIII con el nombre de Balat. En el año 793 / 1391, el sultán otomano Bayezid I (apodado *Yıldırım*, ‘el Rayo’) anexionó este emirato a los territorios otomanos. Tras la derrota frente a Tamerlán en la batalla de Ankara de 805 / 1402, se restableció el emirato Menteşe y Balat pasó a ser su capital.  
En Balat, fundada sobre la antigua Mileto, se construyeron numerosos edificios durante el periodo Menteşe. El más importante es el complejo de mezquita con escuela teológica (madrasa) y dos baños públicos (*hammam*) que se construyó en 1402, inmediatamente después del regreso de İlyas Bey al trono.  
La mezquita y la madrasa, erigidas en medio de un amplio jardín amurallado, comparten un patio. En el área noroeste de la madrasa quedan restos de una estructura cuya función no ha sido determinada. En el curso de unas excavaciones arqueológicas realizadas en 1994 se descubrieron los cimientos de unas salas pertenecientes a otra madrasa, agregada al complejo posteriormente, que se extendía en paralelo al muro del jardín, al oeste de la primera. Los dos *hammam* que formaban parte del complejo original están situados al noroeste de la madrasa.  
La mezquita İlyas Bey es de planta cuadrada (18 × 18 m aproximadamente) y está cubierta por una cúpula de ladrillo de 14 metros de diámetro. Los muros están revestidos con losas de mármol reutilizadas. No dispone de pórtico para los rezagados. El alminar está en la esquina noroeste y se accede a él desde el interior; se vino abajo a causa de un terremoto en el año 1955. A la mezquita se entra a través de un portal-*iwan* ubicado en mitad del muro norte. Este *iwan* está dividido en tres arcos escarzanos (al estilo de Bursa) que descansan sobre dos columnas de mármol. El amplio arco central es la entrada y los dos arcos laterales, con balaustradas de mármol, hacen las veces de ventanas. La estructura de la cúpula está sostenida por grandes trompas decoradas con motivos tales como conchas de ostra, triángulos y mocárabes.  
Esta mezquita destaca por la rica decoración de su mampostería. El portal, el *mihrab* y los tímpanos de las ventanas de los muros este, oeste y sur presentan motivos florales y geométricos e inscripciones, tallados o incrustados. Las incrustaciones están compuestas por piedras y azulejos de colores.  
La madrasa, que comparte el patio con la mezquita, se construyó con piedra sin labrar. Consta de un aula abovedada y doce celdas de estudiantes, cuyos vestigios revelan que estuvieron cubiertas por techos planos de madera.  
Los dos baños, al noreste de la mezquita y la madrasa, tienen muros de piedra sin labrar, y están coronados con cúpulas y bóvedas de ladrillo. Los Büyük Hammam (‘grandes baños’) de la zona norte, cuyo vestuario se descubrió en unas excavaciones en 1991, tienen una sala caliente con tres *iwan* y dos cámaras en los ángulos. Los muros de la sala caliente están decorados con yeso modelado. Los Küçük Hammam (‘baños pequeños’), dos metros al sur de los grandes, constan de tres salas pequeñas contiguas. El complejo está abierto a los visitantes.

El complejo de İlyas Bey en Balat, última capital del emirato Menteşe, comprende una mezquita, una madrasa y dos *hammam*. A pesar de la sencillez de la madrasa y los baños, la mezquita del complejo es uno de los ejemplos más llamativos de la arquitectura del periodo de los emiratos. El portal, el *mihrab* y las ventanas están esplendorosamente decorados con motivos florales y geométricos, y bandas caligráficas talladas o incrustadas.
dates: *Du l-Qada* de 806 de la Hégira / mayo-junio de 1404 d. C.
keywords: Mezquita; madrasa; hammam; decoración en mampostería; decoración geométrica; decoración floral; inscripciones; caligrafía; Balat; Mileto; emirato Menteşe; İlyas Bey.

fr.name: Complexe Ilyas Bey.
description:
L'importante cité ionienne connue dans l'Antiquité sous le nom de Miletos (Palatia, Milet) fut rattachée à l'émirat de Menteche au cours de la première moitié du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) sous le nom de Balat. En 793 H / 1391 J.-C., le sultan ottoman Bayézid (dit Yildirim, “la Foudre”) absorba l'émirat. Après que celui-ci eut été battu par Timour à la bataille d'Ankara en 805 H / 1402 J.-C., l'émirat de Menteche fut restauré et Balat devint sa capitale.  
De nombreux bâtiments datent de la période Menteche. Le plus important est le complexe de la mosquée à laquelle étaient adjoints une *madrasa* et deux bains publics ou hammams édifiés immédiatement après le retour d'Ilyas Bey sur le trône en 1402.  
La mosquée et la *madrasa* se dressent au milieu d'un vaste jardin clos de murs et partagent la même cour. Au nord-ouest de la *madrasa* figurent les vestiges d'une construction dont la fonction reste mal définie. Des fouilles archéologiques menées en 1994 ont mis au jour les fondations des salles d'une autre *madrasa* qui avait été ultérieurement ajoutée au complexe, parallèlement au mur du jardin, à l'ouest de la *madrasa* subsistante. Deux hammams que l'on attribue au complexe original sont situés au nord-est de celle-ci.  
La mosquée Ilyas Bey présente un plan carré de 18 x 18 m environ surmonté d'une coupole de 14 m de diamètre. Ses murs sont habillés de dalles de marbre de remploi tandis que la coupole est en brique. On note l'absence de portique extérieur pour les retardataires. Le minaret, à l'angle nord-ouest auquel on accédait par l'intérieur, s'est effondré lors d'un tremblement de terre en 1955. On pénètre dans la mosquée par un portail-*iwan* au centre du mur nord. L'*iwan* comprend une arcade à trois arcs surbaissés (de type Bursa) s'appuyant sur deux colonnes de marbre. L'entrée se fait par l'arche centrale, tandis que les deux arches latérales, dotées de balustrades, font office de fenêtres. La coupole repose sur d'importantes trompes décorées de motifs en coquille d'huîtres, triangles et *mouqarnas.*  
La mosquée est remarquable pour sa riche décoration de pierre. Des motifs floraux et géométriques et des inscriptions, sculptés et ornés d'incrustations, ornent le portail, le *mihrab* et les tympans de chaque fenêtre des murs est, ouest et sud. La décoration incrustée se compose de pierres de couleur et de carreaux de céramique.  
La *madrasa* a été édifiée en moellons. Elle consiste en une salle de cours sous coupole et 12 cellules d'étudiants dans lesquelles certaines traces montrent qu'elles possédaient sans doute des plafonds plats en bois.  
Les deux hammams au nord-est de la mosquée et de la *madrasa* sont également en moellons. Leurs coupoles et leurs voûtes sont en brique. Les Grands Bains (Büyük Hammam) au nord, dont le vestiaire a été découvert lors des fouilles de 1991, possèdent une salle chaude, trois *iwan* et deux chambres d'angle. Les murs de la pièce chaude présentent une décoration en plâtre moulé. Le Petit Bain (Küçük Hammam), à 2 m au sud du Grand, consiste en trois petites pièces contiguës. Le complexe est ouvert à la visite.

Le complexe Ilyas Bey à Balat, dernière capitale de l’émirat de Menteche, comprend une mosquée, une *madrasa* et deux hammams. En dépit de la simplicité de la *madrasa* et des hammams, la mosquée du complexe est l’un des plus saisissants exemples de l’architecture de la période des émirats. Le portail, le *spolia* et les fenêtres sont décorés à profusion de motifs floraux et géométriques ainsi que de bandes calligraphiques, sculptées et incrustées.
keywords: mosquée ; madrasa ; hammam ; décoration en pierre ; décoration géométrique ; décoration florale ; inscriptions ; calligraphie ; Balat ; Milet ; émirat de Menteche ; Ilyas Bey

tr.name: İlyas Bey Külliyesi.
description:
Antik dönemin önemli İyon kentlerinden biri olan Miletos (Palatia), 7. / 13. yüzyılın ikinci yarısında “Balat” adıyla Menteşe Beyliği topraklarına katılmıştı. Osmanlı Sultanı Yıldırım Bayezid, 793 / 1391'de Menteşe Beyliği topraklarını Osmanlı topraklarına dahil etmişti. Yıldırım Bayezid'in 805 / 1402'deki Ankara Savaşı'nda Timur'a yenik düşmesi sonrasında, bu topraklar tekrar Menteşe Beyliği'ne iade edilmiş ve Balat beyliğin başkenti olmuştu.  
  
Antik Miletos kenti üzerine kurulan Balat'ta, Menteşe Beyliği döneminde inşa edilmiş çok sayıda yapı bulunmaktadır. Bu yapıların en önemlisi, İlyas Bey'in tahta dönüşünden hemen sonra, bir medrese ve iki hamamla birlikte inşa ettirdiği camisidir.  
  
Duvarlarla çevrili geniş bir bahçe içine yerleştirilmiş olan cami ve medrese, ortak bir avluyu paylaşmaktadır. Medresenin kuzeybatısında, işlevi tartışmalı bir yapı kalıntısı vardır. 1994 yılında gerçekleştirilen kazı çalışmalarında, medresenin batısında, bahçe duvarına paralel uzanan, külliyeye sonradan eklenmiş başka bir medreseye ait hücrelerin temelleri ortaya çıkarılmıştır. Külliyeye ait olduğu kabul edilen iki hamam, medresenin kuzeydoğusundadır.  
  
*İlyas Bey Camii*, yaklaşık 18 x 18 metre boyutlarında, 14 metre çapında bir kubbeyle örtülü, kare planlı bir yapıdır. Beden duvarları devşirme mermerlerle kaplanmış; kubbesi tuğlayla örülmüştür. Son cemaat yeri yoktur. Yapının kuzeybatı köşesinde yer alan ve girişi harimden sağlanan minaresi, 1955 yılında meydana gelen depremde yıkılmıştır. Camiye, kuzey cephesinin ortasında yer alan eyvan şekilli bir taçkapıdan girilmektedir. Eyvan, iki mermer sütunla Bursa kemerli üç bölüme ayrılmış; ortadaki geniş bölüm giriş açıklığı, yanlardaki iki bölüm ise şebekeli mermer levhalar içeren birer pencere olarak düzenlenmiştir. Yapının kubbe geçişleri, iri tromplarla sağlanmıştır. Trompların içi, istiridye kabuğu, üçgen ve mukarnaslarla süslenmiştir.  
  
İlyas Bey Camii, zengin taş süslemeleriyle dikkat çeken bir yapıdır. Başta taçkapı ve mihrap olmak üzere doğu, batı ve güney cephelerindeki tüm pencerelerin alınlıklarında ve alt sıra pencerelerinin tavanlarında, oyma ve kakma teknikli bitkisel ve geometrik süslemelerle, yazı şeritlerine yer verilmiştir. Kakma teknikli süslemelerde renkli taşlar ve çiniler kullanılmıştır.  
  
Camiyle aynı avluyu paylaşan *medrese*, kaba yonu taşlarla inşa edilmiştir. Kalan izlerden düz ahşap tavanla örtülü olduğu anlaşılan 12 öğrenci hücresi ve kubbeyle örtülü bir dershane mekanından oluşmaktadır.  
  
Cami ve medresenin kuzeydoğusunda yer alan iki hamamın beden duvarları kaba yonu taşlarla, kubbe ve tonozları ise tuğlayla inşa edilmiştir. Soyunmalık mekanı 1991 yılında gerçekleştirilen kazı çalışmalarında ortaya çıkarılan kuzeydeki *Büyük Hamam*, “üç eyvanlı ve iki köşe hücreli” bir sıcaklığa sahiptir. Sıcaklık duvarlarında, sıva üzerine baskı tekniğiyle oluşturulmuş süsleme izleri görülmektedir. Büyük Hamam'ın 2m. güneyinde yer alan *Küçük Hamam* ise yan yana dizilmiş üç küçük mekandan oluşmaktadır.  
  
Külliye, ziyarete açık durumdadır.

Menteşe Beyliği'nin son başkenti Balat'ta yer alan İlyas Bey Külliyesi, cami, medrese ve iki hamamdan oluşmaktadır. Medrese ve hamamların sadeliğine karşılık cami, inşa malzemesi ve süslemeleri bakımından Beylikler Dönemi mimarisinin en göz alıcı örneklerindendir. Taçkapı, mihrap ve pencerelerdeki oyma ve kakma teknikli bitkisel ve geometrik süslemeler ile yazı şeritleri görülmeye değer güzelliktedir.
keywords: Balat; Milet; Menteşe; Külliye; İlyas Bey; cami; medrese; hamam; taş süsleme; geometrik süsleme; bitkisel süsleme; yazı

en.name: Historic Centre
description:
The road layout of the old part of the city has remained largely as it was in the 16th century. The Manueline fortifications, with gateways leading to the beach and countryside, governed the basic outline, though these in turn were affected by the Muslim plan. Houses, warehouses and small businesses gradually occupied the ineffective Manueline defences, hiding the walls and taking over the towers and passages. Despite a series of earthquakes, there were very few alterations to the network of streets inside the city walls, other than the regularising of churchyards and the courtyards of religious buildings.  
Some of the houses date from the 16th century and there is also a Manueline window, from which D. Sebastião is said to have addressed his troops before embarking for Morocco, in 1578.

en.name: An example of Italian colonial propaganda describing 'The first railway engine crossing Libya, causing astonishment and panic among the Arabs'
names: A colonial postcard about the inauguration of the first railway in Libya
*'La prima locomotiva attraversa il suolo libico tra lo spavento e lo stupore degli arabi'*
short_description:
The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. The construction of railways in colonial situations was thus often celebrated by the colonialists’ popular press or in postcards, as in this case.  
In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.
keywords: cartoon; caricature

en.name: Mosaic of Virgil
short_description: This mosaic shows Virgil listening to Clio and Melpomene. It was discovered in Sousse (ancient Hadrumetum) in 1896 and is one of the gems of the Musée du Bardo. Dressed in a splendid white toga decorated with gold embroidery, this mosaic is one of the most remarkable portraits of the famous Roman poet. He is surrounded by the muses Clio and Melpomene and holds a roll of parchment on his knee, on which the eighth verse of the Aeneid is written. The mosaic is the oldest representations of Virgil known today.
keywords: Mosaic; Virgil; Hadrumetum; Sousse
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: La mosaïque de Virgile
short_description: L’emblème de la mosaïque représentant Virgile, écoutant Clio et Mélpomène, découverte à Sousse, l’antique Hadrumète, en 1896 constitue l’un des joyaux du musée du Bardo. C’est l’un des plus remarquables portraits de l’illustre poète romain Virgile, vêtu d’une ample toge blanche décorée de broderies. Entouré des muses, Clio et Melpomène, il tient dans sa main, posée sur ses genoux, un rouleau de parchemin où sont écrits des extraits de l’Enéide et précisément le huitième vers. L’œuvre est la plus ancienne représentation du poète connue à ce jour.
keywords: Mosaique; Virgile; Hadrumète; Sousse
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

description: In 1908, the French General Albert d’Amade led the pacification of the Kabyle Berber peoples on the plains of Chaouia and also oversaw the construction of a railway line between Casablanca and Berrechid. By 1914, the railway was mainly used for the civil transportation of people and goods. This shot of Casablanca Station in 1920 depicts a train arriving at the station, where the passengers waiting to board appear to be European settlers and Moroccan notables.

en.name: Small bowl with eagle.
description: This poly-lobed bowl is decorated with the stylised figure of an eagle with its wings outstretched, painted in solid lustre with the exception of a few details left uncoloured, such as the eye and the neck. It is surrounded by small dotted panels and the edge is decorated with semi-circles.

The shape and decoration of this bowl are influenced by a combination of different styles and traditions. Its shape is related to early Sassanid metalwork, while its decoration is reminiscent of a style used in late Abbasid figurative ceramics.

es.name: Pequeño cuenco con águila.
description: El fondo de este cuenco polilobulado está decorado con una figura estilizada de águila con las alas desplegadas, pintada en reflejo metálico compacto, salvo algunos detalles reservados como el ojo y el cuello, y rodeada de pequeñas secciones punteadas. El borde, en cambio, está decorado con semidiscos.

Tanto en su forma como en su decoración, este cuenco presenta una combinación de estilos y tradiciones. La forma deriva de modelos de la metalistería sasánida; la decoración, en cambio, evoca una estilización propia de la cerámica figurativa abbasí tardía.

ar.name: سجادة
description:
سجادة من الصوف الفارسي تعرض مزهرية مركزية ومحرابًا للصلاة في الأعلى. تمثل هذه السجادة نموذجًا للمنسوجات التي تم إنتاجها للمحاكم القاجارية في أصفهان ، أحد أبرز المراكز منذ القرن السابع عشر.  
  
كان مصنعو السجاد الأصفهاني يستخدمون عقدة السينه والألوان المتناسقة وزهور الأرابيسك مثل القرنفل والورد الدمشقي. الورود على الحدود تجسد سكان أصفهان المفعمين بالحيوية.  
  
كُتب على الجزء العلوي من السجادة "العهد الأبدي للسلطان ابن السلطان مظفر الدين شاه قاجار في القرية احتفالاً بمصنع الملا الإيمراد 1317 هجري" (1899). قصيدة تمدح أصفهان والشاه تزين السجادة بتكرار كلمة ظفر (نجاح ، نصر) ، وهي أيضًا جزء من اسم السلطان.

en.name: Isfahan Carpet
description:
This Persian wool carpet displays a central flower vase and a prayer niche (mihrab) at the top. This rug represents an example of textiles produced for the Qajar courts in Isfahan, one of the most prominent centres since the 17th century.  
  
Isfahani carpet manufacturers would employ the seneh knot, harmonious colours and Arabesque flowers such as the carnation and Damascene rose. The roses on the border embody the lively inhabitants of Isfahan.  
  
The top of the carpet reads the "The eternal reign of the Sultan, son of Sultan Mozafaradin Shah Qajar in the village celebrating the factory of Mullah Alimorad 1317 Hegira" (1899). A poem praising Isfahan and the Shah embellishes the carpet with the repetition of the word *zafar* (success, victory), also part of the Sultan's name.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Iran; Isfahan; Carpet; Rug; Qajar; Poetry
